situation_name: IMS_WaitSVC
description: Control task TCB in SVC wait
actions: {"The control task has a TCB in SVC wait. This could slow down the performance of the IMS system if it persists. You should look at the job for the IMS control region and determine if it has abnormally terminated or is in the process of generating a dump."}

situation_name: IMS_Wait_IRLM
description: Waiting for response from IRLM address space
actions: {"Bottleneck Analysis found an application program had issued a request to IRLM and was waiting for a response. This wait reason can occur when there is a database conflict or when IRLM is waiting for internalIRLM processing. Review the Local or Global Lock Conflict workspace todetermine if the application is waiting and identify the resource being locked. Review the IRLM Information workspace to determine if the IRLMCSA usage is within limits and if any RLE are available."}

situation_name: IMS_Wait_IWAIT_in_Term
description: Application program IWAITing while terminating
actions: {"The application program is in a wait state at termination. Review IMS Connect Summary workspace to determine if any transaction or client has elongated Output Confirm Times.IMS Connect clients using the commit mode 1 (CM1) and sync-level confirm model must acknowledge receipt of the message before IMS will fully terminate and unschedule the transaction.Slow client response can cause the IWAIT in termination also driving message region utilization high."}

situation_name: IMS_Wait_LGMSG_IO
description: Waiting for I/O to the long message (LGMSG) dataset
actions: {"Bottleneck Analysis found a transaction waiting for I/O to complete on the long message (LGMSG) dataset. Check the IMS Logical Terminal workspace (Output Queued) to determine if there are a lot of messages queued to a particular LTERM. Dequeue these messages to reduce the utilization of the longt message dataset. Also, use the TRMQxx command to determine all LTERMS with queue counts. See the specific instructions for the LTOQ and LPOQ commands."}

situation_name: IMS_Wait_PI
description: Waiting for a Program Isolation (PI) resource
actions: {"Bottleneck Analysis found the application program executing within a dependent region. The dependent region issued a request to Program Isolation (PI) and was waiting for a response. Program Isolation is the mechanism which allows database to be simultaneously accessed and even updated by different users. Review the Local Lock Conflict workspace. Determine if the application is waiting and identify the resource being locked."}

situation_name: IMS_Wait_QBLKS_IO
description: Waiting for I/O to complete to the queue blocks dataset
actions: {"Bottleneck Analysis found a transaction waiting for I/O to complete to the queue blocks dataset. See if a transaction is looping and flooding the message queue, by checking whether the IMS Dependent Region workspace and reviewing the Message Insert value. Also check the queue blocks dataset utilization to see if the dataset if filling up with messages from a runaway transaction. This can cause IMS to abend."}

situation_name: IMS_Wait_SHMSG_IO
description: Waiting for I/O to the short message (SHMSG)dataset
actions: {"Bottleneck Analysis found a transaction waiting for I/O to complete on the short message (SHMSG) dataset. Check the IMS Logical Terminal workspace (Output Queued) to determine if there are a lot of messages queued to a particular LTERM.Dequeue these messages to reduce the utilization of the short message dataset. Also, use the TRMQxx command to determine all LTERMS with queue counts. See the specific instructions for the LTOQ and LPOQ commands."}

situation_name: IMS_Wait_Sync_Point
description: Waiting for synchronization (SYNC) point processing
actions: {"Bottleneck Analysis found the transaction waiting on I/O to complete as a result of synchronization (SYNC) point processing. Review the IMS DASD Logging workspace to determine if WADS or OLDS checkwrite rate is high. Review IMS Device Activity workspace to determine if volume on which the OLDS/WADS reside is responding and potential I/O queue depth issues."}

situation_name: IMS_Waiting_Dyn_SAP
description: Waiting on dynamic SAP
actions: {"The system is waiting on dynamic SAP, which could cause delays to the applications. The SAP should be checked to insure that it is functioning properly."}

situation_name: INET6_Max_Sockets_Critical
description: Internet v6 Sockets in use Critical
actions: {"The number of Internet v6 Sockets in use has reached its Critical threshold. If the maximum is reached, UNIX System Services will not be accessible by Internet v6 connections. System programmer help is needed immediately. Consider increasing the value of NETWORK DOMAINNAME(AF_INET6)- MAXSOCKETS(). Use the SETOMVS RESET command to dynamically change the MAXSOCKETS value or to make a permanent change, edit the BPXPRMxx member in SYS1.PARMLIB."}

situation_name: INET6_Max_Sockets_Warning
description: Internet v6 Sockets in use Warning
actions: {"The number of Internet v6 Sockets in use has reached its Warning threshold. If the maximum is reached, UNIX System Services will not be accessible by Internet V6 connections. Consider increasing the value of NETWORK DOMAINNAME(AF_INET6)- MAXSOCKETS(). Use the SETOMVS RESET command to dynamically change the MAXSOCKETS value or to make a permanent change, edit the BPXPRMxx member in SYS1.PARMLIB."}

situation_name: INET_Max_Sockets_Critical
description: Internet Sockets in use Critical
actions: {"The number of Internet Sockets in use has reached its Critical threshold. If the maximum is reached, UNIX System Services will not be accessible by Internet connections. System programmer help is needed immediately. Consider increasing the value of NETWORK DOMAINNAME(AF_INET)- MAXSOCKETS(). Use the SETOMVS RESET command to dynamically change the MAXSOCKETS value or to make a permanent change, edit the BPXPRMxx member in SYS1.PARMLIB."}

situation_name: INET_Max_Sockets_Warning
description: Internet Sockets in use Warning
actions: {"The number of Internet Sockets in use has reached its Warning threshold. If the maximum is reached, UNIX System Services will not be accessible by Internet connections. Consider increasing the value of NETWORK DOMAINNAME(AF_INET)- MAXSOCKETS(). Use the SETOMVS RESET command to dynamically change the MAXSOCKETS value or to make a permanent change, edit the BPXPRMxx member in SYS1.PARMLIB."}

situation_name: JES_Spool_Allocated_Pct_Crit
description: JES Spool Allocated Percent Crit The JES Spool space usage reached a critical level.This is set as a percentage of total Spool Space that was allocated.
actions: {"Display spool information to monitor JES2 spooling and determine the action to take to control the spool environment. Use the  JOBQ,SPOOL=(%>NN) commandto display all of the jobs in the configuration that are using a specified amount of spool space. It is recommended to use this command starting with 10% or 20%.","The results will help you identify jobs that are using a high number of track groups as candidates for purging or off-loading.","You may also want to add (and, optionally, format) a new spool volume dynamically by issuing the  SPOOL command. You can also use the  SPOOL command to reactivate a previously inactive volume."}

situation_name: JVM_GC_Pause_Critical
description: Critical threshold exceeded for Garbage Collection Pause Time
actions: {"The JVM is taking too long to perform Garbage Collections. Check the Garbage Collection detail and history panels for Global Garbage Collections.This could be because the maximum heap size is too small.Check the value of the -mx java command line option which sets the maximum heap size.If it is already set as high as possible, then it could indicate that the application has a memory leak."}

situation_name: JVM_GC_Pause_Warning
description: Warning threshold exceeded for Garbage Collection Pause Time
actions: {"The JVM is taking too long to perform Garbage Collections. Check the Garbage Collection detail and history panels for Global Garbage Collections.This could be because the maximum heap size is too small.Check the value of the -mx java command line option which sets the maximum heap size.If it is already set as high as possible, then it could indicate that the application has a memory leak."}

situation_name: JVM_General_CPU_Critical
description: Critical threshold exceeded for General CPU Utilization
actions: {"If Garbage Collection rate is also high, the CPU utilization could be due to this.Check the threadhistory: if the number of threads is increasing, this could be causing additional CPU."}

situation_name: JVM_General_CPU_Warning
description: Warning threshold exceeded for General CPU Utilization
actions: {"If Garbage Collection rate is also high, the CPU utilization could be due to this.Check the threadhistory: if the number of threads is increasing, this could be causing additional CPU."}

situation_name: JVM_IFA_on_General_CPU_Critical
description: Critical threshold exceeded for zIIP on CP Time
actions: {"There was zIIP-eligible work for this JVM that could have executed on zIIP or zAAP processorsbut the available zIIP processors were busy executing other workloads. Capacity planning foradditional general CPUs may be mitigated by purchasing additional zIIP or zAAP processors instead."}

situation_name: JVM_IFA_on_General_CPU_Warning
description: Warning threshold exceeded for zIIP on CP time
actions: {"There was zIIP-eligible work for this JVM that could have executed on zIIP or zAAP processorsbut the available zIIP processors were busy executing other workloads. Capacity planning foradditional general CPUs may be mitigated by purchasing additional zIIP or zAAP processors instead."}

situation_name: JVM_Lock_Missed_Critical
description: Critical threshold exceeded for Lock Missed
actions: {"The named lock object has a high proportion of misses. This means the lock must be retried and resultsin a delay to the application. Use the Lock Analysis workspace to determine if multiple threads waitfor the same lock.Based on this, the application code should be reviewed to see whether synchronized blocks of code are used unnecessarily or inappropriately."}

situation_name: JVM_Lock_Missed_Warning
description: Warning threshold exceeded for Lock Missed
actions: {"The named lock object has a high proportion of misses. This means the lock must be retried and resultsin a delay to the application. Use the Lock Analysis workspace to determine if multiple threads waitfor the same lock.Based on this, the application code should be reviewed to see whether synchronized blocks of code are used unnecessarily or inappropriately."}

situation_name: JVM_MEM24Free_Critical
description: The critical threshold for free 24-bit memory has been breached.

situation_name: JVM_MEM24Free_Warning
description: The warning threshold for free 24-bit memory has been breached.

situation_name: JVM_MEM31Free_Critical
description: The critical threshold for free 31-bit memory has been breached.

situation_name: JVM_MEM31Free_Warning
description: The warning threshold for free 31-bit memory has been breached.

situation_name: JVM_MEM64Free_Critical
description: The critical threshold for free 64-bit memory has been breached.

situation_name: JVM_MEM64Free_Warning
description: The warning threshold for free 64-bit memory has been breached.

situation_name: JVM_Occupancy_after_GC_Critical
description: Critical threshold exceeded for Average Occupancy Percent after Garbage Collection
actions: {"Occupancy is the proportion of total Java heap that is in use after garbage collection. The JVM runtime tries to maintain a maximum occupancy between 40% and 70% of the total availableheap. If occupancy goes above 70%, then the heap is expanded. If the heap is already at themaximum size, then there is a danger of storage shortage and OutOfMemory errors. This may indicate a possible memory leak in the application. If not, consider increasing the maximum heap size withJava option -mxnnnn; using a 64-bit JVM, or deploying some of the workload to another JVM."}

situation_name: JVM_System_GC_Warning
description: Warning issued for System (forced) Garbage Collections in application code.
actions: {"The JVM runtime usually does an excellent job in managing the Java heap. Some applicationprogrammers use the System.gc() method call to release memory.This is normally unnecessaryand often adversely affects the JVM by executing global garbage collections which can cause the JVM to pause."}

situation_name: JVM_Thread_Blocked_Warning
description: Warning threshold exceeded for blocked threads
actions: {"Use the Lock Analysis workspace to find the thread holding the contended lock. If there are otherthreads waiting for the same lock, this could indicate a deadlock condition. Find the thread holding the lock and from the stack trace identify the code that leads to this condition."}

situation_name: JVM_z/OS_Connect_Avg_Response_Time_Warning
description: Warning threshold exceeded for Average Elapsed Time
actions: {"Use OMEGAMON for JVM workspaces to examine Garbage Collection, CPU, Locks and Threads.It will highlight any problems with the Java heap size, excessive garbage collection delays, or high rates of garbage collection.","If the address space is consuming high CPU, there may be a loop in the application. Use the Threads workspace to see which threads are consuming the CPU.","Check the Locks information to see if threads are being delayed due to excessive locking."}

situation_name: JVM_zOS_Connect_Http_Warning
description: Warning threshold exceeded for HTTP status code
actions: {"Examine the HTTP Code attribute for the failing request for the exact error."}

situation_name: JVM_zOS_Connect_Resp_Critical
description: Critical threshold exceeded for request response time
actions: {"z/OS Connect request was found with very high total response time, use OMEGAMON for JVM resource monitoring to check for CPU, lock or heap problems. The fields zOS_Conn_Time and SoR_Resp_Time will tell you whether the high response time occurred in z/OS Connect or the System of Record."}

situation_name: JVM_zOS_Connect_Resp_Warning
description: Warning threshold exceeded for request response time
actions: {"z/OS Connect request was found with moderately high total request response time, use OMEGAMON for JVM resource monitoring to check for CPU, lock or heap problems. The fields zOS_Conn_Time and SoR_Resp_Time will tell you whether the high response time occurred in z/OS Connect or the System of Record."}

situation_name: JVM_zOS_Connect_Timeout_Warning
description: Warning threshold exceeded for Connect_Timeout
actions: {"An asynchronous request timeout occurred. TheHTTP Code may return 200 as the work completed successfully in the system of record, but if the asynchronous request timeout expired before the request had finished processing, the HTTP client will have actually received the HTTP status code 503."}

situation_name: KD5_ARCM_Warning
description: Archive log mount required for backout.
actions: {"A DB2 thread is not executing because it is waiting for a tape mount request to be resolved. While the thread is waiting, it is blocked from doing anything else. If this problem persists, you should ensure that the tape management facility you are using, is operating properly."}

situation_name: KD5_CONDBAT_Appr_Max_Warning
description: The number of DBAT connections is approaching DSNZPARM CONDBAT.The situation's formula is: DB2_SRM_Subsystem.DBAT_Conn_Utilization GE 70
actions: {"This situation indicates that the number of DBAT connections is approaching DSNZPARM CONDBAT. If this condition is detected, make sure CONDBAT is defined accurately for remote connections."}

situation_name: KD5_CPU_Time_Warning
description: Thread CPU time exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the CPU time used by a thread is too high. Look into the thread or application to determine the cause for the high CPU."}

situation_name: KD5_CTHD_Warning
description: Application is waiting for thread creation.
actions: {"The application is waiting for a thread to be created. An application can be in this state if the maximum number of allowed threads has been reached. The application will not start to execute until some other thread terminates. The maximum allowed thread count can be changed, however it is probably set up as a throttle to prevent over utilization of the DB2 system."}

situation_name: KD5_DB2DBM1_Usage_Warning
description: DB2DBM1 CPU utilization exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the DB2DBM1 CPU utilization is too high. Look into DB2DBM1 to determine the cause for the high CPU usage."}

situation_name: KD5_DB2MSTR_Usage_Warning
description: DB2MSTR CPU utilization exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the DB2MSTR CPU utilization is too high. Look into DB2MSTR to determine the cause for the high CPU usage."}

situation_name: KD5_DB2_CPU_Usage_Warning
description: DB2 CPU utilization exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the DB2 CPU utilization is too high. Look into DB2 to determine the cause for the high CPU usage."}

situation_name: KD5_DBAT_Wait_Warning
description: Database Wait percent has exceeded the critical threshold. It indicates the percentage of DBAT (Database Access Thread) that has to wait because MAXDBAT exceeded the threshold. A critical condition is detected when the percentage of active background connections to DBAT_Wait reaches 0%. The situation's formula is: DB2_System_States.DB_Wait_Percent GE 0
actions: {"When the MAXDBAT limit is reached, conversations are queued (waiting on DBAT allocation), which can considerably increase response time."}

situation_name: KD5_DBD_Pool_InUse_Pct_High
description: DBD Pool in use percent exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the DBD Pool in use percent is too high. Look into DBD Pool to determine the cause for the high space usage."}

situation_name: KD5_DBM1_Storage_Usage_Warning
description: DBM1 storage consumption exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates that the DBM1 storage consumption is too high. Look into the DBM1 storage usage to determine the cause for the high storage consumption."}

situation_name: KD5_DSMAX_Approach_Max_Warning
description: The number of data sets opened is approaching DSMAX. It indicates when the maximum percentage of open data sets exceeded the threshold. A critical condition is detected when the percentage of open data sets to DSMAX is approaching 80%. The situation's formula is: DB2_System_States.DSMAX_Approaching_Max GE 80.0
actions: {"The current number of data sets opened is approaching the allowed maximum which is specified in DSNZPARM DSMAX."}

situation_name: KD5_DSNP001I_Space_Warning
description: Impending data set space shortage warning.
actions: {"This situation indicates an impending space shortage. For more information refer to the description of message DSNP001I."}

situation_name: KD5_DSNP007I_Space_Critical
description: Impending data set space shortage warning.
actions: {"This situation indicates an extension on a data set failed. For more information refer to the description of message DSNP007I."}

situation_name: KD5_DSNT375I_Deadlock_Critical
description: Application deadlock warning.
actions: {"This situation indicates that a deadlock has occurred. For more information refer to the description of message DSNT375I."}

situation_name: KD5_DSNT376I_Timeout_Critical
description: Application lock timeout critical.
actions: {"This situation indicates that a lock timeout has occurred. For more information refer to the description of message DSNT376I."}

situation_name: KD5_DSNT500I_ResUnavail_Warning
description: Resource unavailable warning.
actions: {"This situation indicates that the requested function requires a resource that is currently not available. For more information refer to the description of message DSNT500I."}

situation_name: KD5_DSNT501I_ResUnavail_Warning
description: Resource unavailable warning.
actions: {"This situation indicates that the requested function requires a resource that is currently not available. For more information refer to the description of message DSNT501I."}

situation_name: KD5_DSNU511I_Recovery_Critical
description: Object not in a recoverable state.
actions: {"This situation indicates that an object is not in an recoverable state. For more information refer to the description of message DSNU511I."}

situation_name: KD5_DSNU548I_Recovery_Critical
description: RECOVER utility job terminates.
actions: {"The RECOVER utility job terminates because the DBID and PSID in the header page do not match the DB2 catalog. For more information refer to the description of message DSNU548I."}

situation_name: KD5_DSNU621I_Runstats_Critical
description: RUNSTATS commit or rollback failed.
actions: {"This situation indicates that RUNSTATS commit/rollback failed. For more information refer to the description of message DSNU621I."}

situation_name: KD5_DWAT_Warning
description: The Wait for remote SQL time exceeds critical limit.
actions: {"A distributed allied thread has been waiting for a response to a remote SQL request for a period of time that exceeds the critical threshold. Check the activity on the remote DB2 subsystem to determine if it works correctly."}

situation_name: KD5_ETIM_Warning
description: The Thread elapsed time exceeds critical threshold.
actions: {"The elapsed time for a DB2 thread (from sign-on or create thread) exceeds the critical threshold. Some threads are intended to run for long periods and can be ignored. Long elapsed times for other threads indicate that bottlenecks in the system are preventing applications from completing in time."}

situation_name: KD5_Fail_Stmt_Percent_Warning
description: Appliation SQL fail percent exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the failed SQL statement percentage for an application is too high. Look into the application and determine the cause for the high failed SQL statement percentage."}

situation_name: KD5_GETP_Warning
description: Getpage ratio less than critical threshold.
actions: {"The ratio of logical page read (getpage) requests to physical page read (read I/O) requests is less than the critical threshold. This exception is an indication that DB2 is having a low hit ratio for this application. You can try to execute the RUNSTATS utility against this application plan."}

situation_name: KD5_IDAA_Avg_QueueTime_Warning
description: IDAA average query wait time exceeded warning threshold.
actions: {"Average query wait time greater then n seconds. High query workload impacts query performance. More accelerator capacity might be needed, bigger model or additional accelerator server. n is customer defined."}

situation_name: KD5_IDAA_Elap_Time_Warning
description: IDAA accumulated elapsed time exceeded warning threshold.
actions: {"The accumulated elapsed time spent in the accelerator when executing requests from the DB2 subsystem.It could be a run-away queries that trigger this situation."}

situation_name: KD5_IDAA_Not_Online_Warning
description: IDAA is not online warning.
actions: {"The Accelerator is not operational. This could be due to planned maintenance, network problems or other issues related to the setup of the Accelerator."}

situation_name: KD5_IDAA_Queue_Length_Warning
description: IDAA current queue length exceeded warning threshold.
actions: {"A high number in this counter can be an indication that the accelerator is not able to process the scheduled work efficiently as the current queue length at the accelerator is large. The elements queued can be queries, loads, replication and maintenance tasks."}

situation_name: KD5_IDAA_Replic_Latency_Warning
description: IDAA average query wait time exceeded warning threshold.
actions: {"When replication latency too high (5min/300s in this sample), it may impact query result correctness as the data on the Accelerator is not current. Note that sporadically high values of this counter might be acceptable and the value should be observed for a certain interval of time. If the value constantly increases or stay on an elevated value, this indicates a potential problem with the replication setup, that might have to be tuned."}

situation_name: KD5_IDAA_Replic_State_Warning
description: There is an issue with incremental update function warning.
actions: {"There is an issue with replication (incremental update) function."}

situation_name: KD5_IDAA_Req_Fail_Warning
description: IDAA failed requests exceeded warning threshold.
actions: {"The number of connections that failed when this DB2 system sent requests to the accelerator. Failed requests should not normally occur."}

situation_name: KD5_IDAA_SQL_Exe_Fail_Warning
description: IDAA SQL execution failed exceeded warning threshold.
actions: {"The number of SQL statements sent by all DB2 systems since accelerator started that were not successfully executed for any reason."}

situation_name: KD5_IDAA_Wait_Time_Warning
description: IDAA wait time spent exceeded warning threshold.
actions: {"The wait time spent in the accelerator when executing requests from the DB2 subsystem. It could be a run-away query that triggers this situation."}

situation_name: KD5_IDBC_Warning
description: DB2 CPU usage exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"The amount of CPU time used by DB2 to process a thread is exceeds the critical threshold. Analyze the SQL used by this thread to see if it could be optimized."}

situation_name: KD5_IDBT_Warning
description: DB2 elapsed time exceeds critical threshold.
actions: {"The period of time that DB2 has been processing a thread exceeds the critical threshold. Check if the DB2 system is looping or if it is processing a complex request."}

situation_name: KD5_INDB_Warning
description: Thread is in the INDOUBT state.
actions: {"The thread has terminated and is in the INDOUBT state. Data associated with this thread is not in a consistent state. This can happen when a rollback operation is performed on an IMS or CICS thread, but the DB2 system is waiting for the IMS or CICS regions to restart the attachment facilities."}

situation_name: KD5_In_DB2_IIP_CPU_Time_Warning
description: Thread In_DB2 IIP CPU time exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the In_DB2 IIP CPU time used by a thread is too high. Look into the thread or application to determine the cause for the high In_DB2 IIP CPU time."}

situation_name: KD5_LOCK_ESCAL_EXCL_Warning
description: The number of exclusive lock escalations exceeded the threshold. It indicates when the number of times lock escalation exclusive happened exceeded the threshold. A warning condition is detected when the number of count of lock escalations to exclusive mode is greater than 20. The situation's formula is: DB2_System_States.Lock_Escalation_Excl GE 20.0
actions: {"The number of exclusive lock escalations exceeded the warning threshold. The number of times that the allowable number of locks per table space was exceeded resulting in page (IX) lock to escalate to table or table space lock in exclusive mode."}

situation_name: KD5_LPAR_CPU_Usage_Warning
description: CPU usage on the LPAR exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the CPU utilization on the LPAR is too high. Look into the active jobs to determine the cause for the high CPU usage."}

situation_name: KD5_MVS_Extended_CSA_Warning
description: MVS extended CSA exceeds the warning threshold.
actions: {None.}

situation_name: KD5_MVS_Low_Private_Warning
description: MVS low private exceeds the warning threshold.
actions: {None.}

situation_name: KD5_Max_Agent_Overflows_Warning
description: Maximum agent overflow exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"The number of times a request to create a new agent was received after the MAXAGENTS configuration parameter had already been reached. This might indicate that the workload for this node is too high or that the MAXAGENTS configuration parameter is set too small."}

situation_name: KD5_Max_Agents_Waiting_Warning
description: Maximum of agents waiting for token exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"The number of times a request to create a new agent was received after the MAXAGENTS configuration parameter had already been reached. This might indicate that the workload for this node is too high or that the MAXAGENTS configuration parameter is set too small."}

situation_name: KD5_Percent_Log_Avail_Warning
description: The percentage of active logs available is dropping below the threshold. The situation's formula is: Percent Logs Available = Logs_Available * 100 / Logs_Defined
actions: {"This situation indicates that the log files might be too small. This exception can happen when logs are filled up faster than they can be archived."}

situation_name: KD5_Process_CPU_Usage_Warning
description: Process CPU usage percentage exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the CPU usage used by a process is too high. Check the process or the program to determine the cause for the high CPU usage."}

situation_name: KD5_RCPU_Warning
description: Remote CPU seconds exceed the critical threshold.
actions: {"The amount of CPU time used by a distributed data access thread exceeds the critical threshold."}

situation_name: KD5_RDS_Pool_above_Use_Pct_High
description: RDS Pool above in use percent exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the RDS Pool above the bar in use percent is too high. Check the RDS Pool above the bar to determine the cause for the high space usage."}

situation_name: KD5_RDS_Pool_below_Use_Pct_High
description: RDS Pool below in use percent exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the RDS Pool below the bar in use percent is too high. Check the RDS Pool below the bar to determine the cause for the high space usage."}

situation_name: KD5_RID_Fallback_Warning
description: The number of RID Pool fallbacks exceeded the threshold. Itindicates when the number of times RID Pool fallback exceeded the threshold. A warning condition is detected when the number oftimes RID fallback is greater than 20. The situation's formula is: DB2_System_States.RIDPool_Fail_No_Storage GE 20
actions: {"The number of times that DB2 could not use more than one index when accessing a table, because there is not sufficient storage for the candidate RID lists."}

situation_name: KD5_RIO_Warning
description: Read I/O rate exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"The physical read I/O rate per second on behalf of a thread exceeds the critical threshold."}

situation_name: KD5_Real_Storage_Usage_Warning
description: Real storage exceeds the warning threshold.
actions: {None.}

situation_name: KD5_Recent_Stmt_ETIM_Warning
description: Application statement elapsed time exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the most recent statement elapsed time for an application is too high. Check the application to determine the cause for long statement elapsed time."}

situation_name: KD5_SKEL_Pool_inUse_Pct_High
description: SKEL Pool in use percent exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the SKEL Pool in use percent is too high. Check the SKEL Pool to determine the cause for the high space usage."}

situation_name: KD5_STMT_Pool_InUse_Pct_High
description: STMT Pool in use percent exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates a performance issue when the STMT Pool in use percent is too high. Check STMT Pool to determine the cause for the high space usage."}

situation_name: KD5_Stolen_Agents_Warning
description: Agents stolen exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates the number of times that agents are stolen from an application. Agents are stolen when an idle agent associated with an application is reassigned to work on a different application. If the number of times that agents are stolen is high, consider increasing the NUM_POOLAGENTS configuration parameter."}

situation_name: KD5_Storage_Cushion_Warning
description: Storage cushion exceeds the warning threshold.
actions: {None.}

situation_name: KD5_TCPU_Warning
description: CPU utilization exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"The CPU rate (percent) of active threads exceeds the critical threshold."}

situation_name: KD5_TRCV_Warning
description: Distributed receive rate exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"The amount of data received by distributed threads from a remote DB2 subsystem exceeds the critical threshold."}

situation_name: KD5_TSND_Warning
description: Distributed send rate exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"The amount of data sent by distributed threads to a remote DB2 subsystem exceeds the critical threshold."}

situation_name: KD5_Total_DBM1_Warning
description: Total DBM1 exceeds the warning threshold.
actions: {None.}

situation_name: KD5_WCLM_Warning
description: Time waiting on drain claims exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"A thread has been waiting for more than the specified critical length of time for a resource to be drained of claimers."}

situation_name: KD5_WDLK_Warning
description: Time waiting on drain of locks exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates that a thread has been waiting longer than the specified critical threshold to acquire a drain lock."}

situation_name: KD5_WGLK_Warning
description: Time waiting on global locks exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates that a thread has been waiting for a global lock longer than the specified critical threshold. The global locks are maintained in the coupling facility for DB2 systems using the data sharing environment. The owner of the lock may be on any of the DB2 systems that make up the data sharing group."}

situation_name: KD5_WLGQ_Warning
description: Time waiting on log queue exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates that a thread has been waiting for an ARCHIVE LOG MODE(QUIESCE) command to complete longer than the critical threshold."}

situation_name: KD5_WSPS_Warning
description: Time waiting for stored procedure exceeds critical threshold.
actions: {"The time that this thread has been waiting for the stored procedures address space to schedule a stored procedure is longer than the critical threshold."}

situation_name: KD5_WSRV_Warning
description: Time waiting for service exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates that a thread has been waiting for a DB2 service for more than the critical length of time. DB2 service waits include Open/Close data set, SYSLGRNG update, DFHSM recall, Dataspace Manager services, and Define/Delete/Extend data set."}

situation_name: KD5_Wait_Time_Warning
description: A thread wait time exceeded the threshold.
actions: {"This situation indicates that the wait time of the thread exceeded the threshold. Check the wait time and determine which event has the longest wait time."}

situation_name: KDP_ARCV_Critical
description: Recovery log archive is waiting on tape mount.
actions: {"The DB2 system is waiting for a tape mount to complete a rollback operation. While the system is in this state, the DB2 performance will be reduced. If the problem persists, verify that the tape management system at your site is working correctly. You can reduce the frequency of having the system wait by increasing the size of the log files."}

situation_name: KDP_ARCV_Warning
description: Recovery log archive is waiting on tape mount.
actions: {"The DB2 system is waiting for a tape mount to complete a rollback operation. While the system is in this state, the DB2 performance will be reduced. If the problem persists, verify that the tape management system at your site is working correctly. You can reduce the frequency of having the system wait by increasing the size of the log files."}

situation_name: KDP_BMTH_Critical
description: Buffer pool approaching maximum size.
actions: {"The critical threshold for buffer pool utilization has been exceeded. This is typically caused by a poorly defined application or by having too many concurrent DB2 applications running. The buffer pool allocation can be increased to avoid this problem, or some applications can be changed to use different buffer pools."}

situation_name: KDP_BMTH_Warning
description: Buffer pool limits exceed warning threshold.
actions: {"The warning threshold for buffer pool utilization has been exceeded. This is typically caused by a poorly defined application or by having too many concurrent DB2 applications running. The buffer pool allocation can be increased to avoid this problem, or some applications can be changed to use different buffer pools."}

situation_name: KDP_CICT_Critical
description: Percentage of thread max (THRDMAX) reached (critical).
actions: {"The CICS thread utilization has exceeded the critical threshold. CICS transactions are executing longer than anticipated causing more CICS transactions to be active at any given time. This may be due to MVS, CICS, or DB2 issues. The limits for CICS threads are defined in the CICS regions."}

situation_name: KDP_CICT_Warning
description: Percentage of thread max (THRDMAX) reached (warning).
actions: {"The CICS thread utilization has exceeded the warning threshold. CICS transactions are executing longer than anticipated causing more CICS transactions to be active at any given time. This may be due to MVS, CICS, or DB2 issues. The limits for CICS threads are defined in the CICS regions."}

situation_name: KDP_COMT_Critical
description: Ratio of updates to commits is greater than critical threshold.
actions: {"The commit ratio for this thread has exceeded the critical threshold. The ratio is made up of the number of modified pages divided by the number of commits that the thread has performed. A high ratio would mean that a recovery operation would take longer to complete. To reduce the ratio a change to the DB2 application is necessary."}

situation_name: KDP_COMT_Warning
description: Ratio of updates to commits is greater than warning threshold.
actions: {"The commit ratio for this thread has exceeded the warning threshold. The ratio is made up of the number of modified pages divided by the number of commits that the thread has performed. A high ratio would mean that a recovery operation would take longer to complete. To reduce the ratio a change to the DB2 application is necessary."}

situation_name: KDP_DDFS_Critical
description: Monitors if DDF is active.
actions: {"The Distributed Data Facility (DDF) is inactive on the DB2 system. If DDF is not used, you can disable this situation or ignore it. You should check if the started task db2id_DIST is running. If not, you can try and start it up."}

situation_name: KDP_LKUS_Warning

situation_name: KDP_LOGN_Critical
description: Number of available logs less than critical threshold. KDP_LOGN_Critical monitors the availability of primary active logs. Active log data sets are allocated to DB2 during start-up processing. When an active log data set is full, it is automatically archived by DB2 to an archive log. When an active log is successfully archived, it is available for reuse. The availability of active logs is critical to the functioning of DB2. If no active log is available, the DB2 subsystem hangs until one becomes available. The lack of an active log could be caused by an insufficient number of logs defined at installation time, too small a log data set size, or possibly because of problems encountered during the archive process. A critical condition is detected when the logs available is less than one. The situation's formula is: KDP_SRM_Log_Manager.Logs_Available LT 1
actions: {"The number of available primary active logs is less than or equal to the critical threshold. This is an indication that the log files may be too small. This exception indicates that logs are filled up faster than they can be archived."}

actions: {"The movement of tracks from the physical device to cache has exceeded the critical threshold.If performance is impacted, it may be necessary to move the logical volume causing the activity or to move datasets on the logical volume."}

situation_name: KS3_Cachecu_Write_HitP_Critical
description: The cache write hit percent is below the critical threshold.
actions: {"The percentage of Cache eligible write commands that were successfully processed without accessing the volume is below the critical threshold.If performance is impacted it may be necessary to move a volume or dataset to another control unit to balance the workload."}

situation_name: KS3_Cachecu_Write_HitP_Warning

situation_name: KS3_Channel_Busy_Pct_Critical
description: Channel path utilization exceeds critical threshold.
actions: {"Over utilization of a channel can result in high response time for I/O requests to volumes being serviced by the channel.It may be necessary to balance the workload between channels by moving volumes or datasets."}

situation_name: KS3_Channel_Busy_Pct_Warning
description: Channel path utilization exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"Over utilization of a channel can result in high response time for I/O requests to volumes being serviced by the channel.It may be necessary to balance the workload between channels by moving volumes or datasets."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Backup_Held_Critical
description: The HSM backup function is being held.
actions: {"The HSM backup function is being held.If the hold is inadvertent, then issue the HSM RELEASE BACKUP command to allow the backup function to continue processing."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Backup_Queue_Critical
description: Waiting HSM backup requests exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"The number of HSM backup requests waiting on the backup queue exceeds the critical threshold.If the number of backup tasks is not at the maximum, the HSM SETSYS MAXBACKUPTASKS command may be used to increase the number of backup tasks to increase the processing rate.Keep in mind that the number of available backup volumes serves as a constraint on the number of active backup tasks."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Backup_Queue_Warning
description: Waiting HSM backup requests exceeds the warning threshold.
actions: {"The number of HSM backup requests waiting on the backup queue exceeds the warning threshold.If the number of backup tasks is not at the maximum, the HSM SETSYS MAXBACKUPTASKS command may be used to increase the number of backup tasks to increase the processing rate.Keep in mind that the number of available backup volumes serves as a constraint on the number of active backup tasks."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_CRQ_Element_Full_Warn
description: The percentage of elements in use on the Common Recall Queue exceeds the warning threshold. HSM throttles the use of the CRQ when the percent utilized reaches 95%.
actions: {"The Common Recall Queue structure can be expanded using the SETXCF START,ALTER command."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_CRQ_Entry_Full_Warning

situation_name: KS3_HSM_CRQ_Host_Critical
description: The host is not connected to the Common Recall Queue.
actions: {"To reconnect the host to the Common Recall Queue issue the SETSYS COMMONQUEUE(RECALL(CONNECT(basename))) command."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_CRQ_Host_Disconn_Crit

situation_name: KS3_HSM_CRQ_Host_Place_Crit

situation_name: KS3_HSM_CRQ_Host_Recall_Crit

situation_name: KS3_HSM_CRQ_Host_Select_Crit

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Dump_Held_Critical

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Dump_Queue_Critical

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Dump_Queue_Warning

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Inactive_Host_Warning
description: One or more HSM hosts are no longer active.
actions: {"If the inactive HSMhosts were purposely stopped, then no action should be taken as aresult of this situation being true.However, if the inactive HSM hostswere not purposely stopped, then the reason why they stopped should beinvestigated.When appropriate, the HSM hosts may be restarted usingthe z/OS St art operator command."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Migrate_Held_Critical
description: The HSM migration function is being held.
actions: {"The HSM migrate function is being held.If the hold on the function is inadvertent, then issue the HSM RELEASE MIGRATION command to allow migration to continue."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Migrate_Queue_Critical
description: Waiting HSM migration requests exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"The number of HSM migration requests waiting on the migration queue exceeds the critical threshold.If the number of migrate tasks is not at the maximum, the HSM SETSYS MAXMIGRATIONTASKS command may be used to increase the number of migration tasks to increase the processing rate.Note that this will affect only those migrations requested by automatic functions.Only one task is available to process command migration requests."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Migrate_Queue_Warning

actions: {"The number of HSM migration requests waiting on the migration queue exceeds the warning threshold.If the number of migrate tasks is not at the maximum, the HSM SETSYS MAXMIGRATIONTASKS command may be used to increase the number of migration tasks to increase the processing rate.Note that this will affect only those migrations requested by automatic functions.Only one task is available to process command migration requests."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Recall_Held_Critical
description: The HSM recall function is being held on this z/OS image.
actions: {"The HSM recall function is being held on this z/OS image.If the hold is inadvertent, then issue the HSM RELEASE RECALL command to allow recalls to resume on this z/OS image.If a connection to the common recall queue is active, then recalls originating on this z/OS image are possibly being executed on another z/OS image."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Recall_Queue_Critical

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Recall_Queue_Warning
description: Waiting HSM recall requests exceeds the warning threshold.
actions: {"The number of HSM recall requests waiting on the recall queue exceeds the warning threshold.If the number of recall tasks is not at the maximum, the HSM SETSYS MAXRECALLTASKS command may be used to increase the number of recall tasks to increase the processing rate."}

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Recovery_Held_Critical

situation_name: KS3_HSM_Recovery_Queue_Critical

situation_name: KS3_LCU_Av_Delay_Q_Critical

actions: {"The average number of requests queued to devices assigned to a logical control unit due to busy conditions on physical paths has exceeded the critical threshold.If performance is impacted, then it may be possible to balance the workload across multiple LCUs by moving a volume or dataset.Otherwise, it may be necessary to add physical paths to the LCU."}

situation_name: KS3_LCU_Av_Delay_Q_Warning

actions: {"The average number of requests queued to devices assigned to a logical control unit due to busy conditions on physical paths has exceeded the warning threshold.If performance is impacted, then it may be possible to balance the workload across multiple LCUs by moving a volume or dataset.Otherwise, it may be necessary to add physical paths to the LCU."}

situation_name: KS3_LCU_Cont_Rate_Critical
description: The contention rate has exceeded the critical threshold.
actions: {"The rate at which I/O requests are being queued to devices on a logical control unit (LCU) due to busy conditions on physical paths has exceeded the critical threshold.If performance is impacted, then it may be necessary to migrate volumes or datasets to another LCU, otherwise, it may be necessary to add physical paths to the LCU."}

situation_name: KS3_LCU_Cont_Rate_Warning

situation_name: KS3_LCU_IO_Rate_Sec_Critical

actions: {"The I/O rate per second to volumes in the logical control unit (LCU) has exceeded the critical threshold.If performance is impacted, it may be necessary to balance the workload across multiple LCUs by moving volumes or datasets."}

situation_name: KS3_LCU_IO_Rate_Sec_Warning

actions: {"The I/O rate per second to volumes in the logical control unit (LCU) has exceeded the warning threshold.If performance is impacted, it may be necessary to balance the workload across multiple LCUs by moving volumes or datasets."}

situation_name: KS3_RMM_CDS_Backup_Critical
description: The number of days since the last backup of the DFSMSrmm CDS or Journal exceeded the critical threshold.
actions: {"Ensure that the DFSMSrmm back-up procedure is scheduled to run daily. You need to ensure that the journal does not fill up because a full journal can impact tape usage on your system. You can run regular backups as part of inventory management in order to clear the journal. Automating control data set backup and clearing the journal help to ensure that the journal does not fill up. Refer to the DFSMSrmm Implementation and Customization Guide."}

situation_name: KS3_RMM_CDS_Backup_Warning
description: The number of days since the last backup of the DFSMSrmm CDS or Journal exceeded the warning threshold.
actions: {"Ensure that the DFSMSrmm back-up procedure is scheduled to run daily. You need to ensure that the journal does not fill up because a full journal can impact tape usage on your system. You can run regular backups as part of inventory management in order to clear the journal. Automating control data set backup and clearing the journal help to ensure that the journal does not fill up. Refer to the DFSMSrmm Implementation and Customization Guide."}

situation_name: KS3_RMM_CDS_Space_Critical
description: The percentage of space used by the DFSMSrmm CDS or Journal is greater than the critical threshold.
actions: {"Use EDGBKUP to reorganize the control data set. The DFSMSrmm subsystem must be stopped orquiesced when you reorganize the active control data set. DFSMSrmm reorganizes the controldata set by first backing up the control data set and optionally the journal. Then DFSMSrmmrestores the control data set from the backup control data set.Refer to the DFSMSrmmImplementation and Customization Guide for details on CDS space planning, allocation,reallocation, backup & reorganization."}

situation_name: KS3_RMM_CDS_Space_Warning
description: The percentage of space used by the DFSMSrmm CDS or Journal is greater than the warning threshold.
actions: {"Use EDGBKUP to reorganize the control data set. The DFSMSrmm subsystem must be stopped orquiesced when you reorganize the active control data set. DFSMSrmm reorganizes the controldata set by first backing up the control data set and optionally the journal. Then DFSMSrmmrestores the control data set from the backup control data set.Refer to the DFSMSrmmImplementation and Customization Guide for details on CDS space planning, allocation,reallocation, backup & reorganization."}

situation_name: KS3_RMM_Exit_Status_Critical
description: The DFSMSrmm EDGUX100 and/or EDGUX200 exit is not Enabled.
actions: {"The DFSMSrmm installation exits perform a variety of installation-specific critical functions. If utilized in your DFSMSrmm environment, ensure that the exits are enabled and active. Refer to the DFSMSrmm Implementation and Customization Guide."}

situation_name: KS3_RMM_Inactive_Critical
description: DFSMSrmm is not active on the system.
actions: {"If the system is a DFSMSrmm-managed environment, the subsystem should be started at IPL or by automation immediately following a shutdown to ensure that all tape activity is properly managed.If the system on which this alert was raised is not a DFSMSrmm-managed environment, this situation should be stopped."}

situation_name: KS3_RMM_Journal_Status_Critical
description: The DFSMSrmm Journal is either Disabled or Locked.DFSMSrmm does not allow further updates to the journal until BACKUP is run to back up the DFSMSrmm control data set and to clear the journal. If the Journal is Locked, DFSMSrmm fails any requests that result in an update to the DFSMSrmmcontrol data set. Message EDG2103D may also have been issued to the DFSMSrmm operator console.
actions: {"Use the DFSMSrmm EDGHSKP utility with the BACKUP parameter to back up the DFSMSrmm control data set and clear the journal."}

situation_name: KS3_RMM_Operating_Mode_Warning
description: DFSMSrmm is not operating in Protect mode.Certain actions that should be rejected are permitted if DFSMSrmm is not operating in protect mode, for example attempting to read a scratch tape volume.
actions: {"Set the EDGRMMxx parmlib member to Protect mode."}

situation_name: KS3_RMM_Scratch_Tape_Critical
description: The number of Scratch volumes is below the critical threshold.
actions: {"Run the DFSMSrmm scratch procedure to take action to replenish the scratch pool, for exampleby triggering the inventory management expiration processing job."}

situation_name: KS3_RMM_Scratch_Tape_Warning
description: The number of Scratch volumes is below the warning threshold.
actions: {"Run the DFSMSrmm scratch procedure to take action to replenish the scratch pool, for exampleby triggering the inventory management expiration processing job."}

situation_name: KS3_Stg_Toolkit_Result_Critical
description: The action request return code exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"The batch job submitted by the Storage Toolkit to execute a command or user-defined JCL returns a value greater than 4. Or the Storage Toolkit encountered an error while attempting to process a command or user-defined JCL.A return codethat is greater than 4 and is not specific to the Storage Toolkit, typically denotes that a command failed to complete. If you elected to save the results of the batch job, you can check the Storage Toolkit Result Detail workspace todetermine whether the error requires further attention.","Values set by the Storage Toolkit when it detects an error while processing a command or user-defined JCL are described in the following table.If one of these values is returned, also consult the RKLVLOG of the Tivoli Enterprise Monitoring Server for additional messages to help determine the cause of the failure. 117The JCL exceeded 72 characters after variable substitution was applied or other JCL-relatederror, such as a missing JOB card.119User Data Server ended abnormally or the batch job ended, but the Storage Toolkitwas unable to determine the return code.121Authorization failed.123Data set error occurred, such as the data set containing your JCL does not exist.125Group error occurred.The groups associated with the action request are emptyor do not exist.If you see a return code value that does not look familiar, you might want to convert it to its hexadecimal equivalent, becausethe value might indicate an abend in the batch job.For example, a return code of 193 is the same as x'0C1'."}

situation_name: KS3_Stg_Toolkit_Result_Warning
description: The action request return code equals the warning threshold.
actions: {"The batch job submitted by the Storage Toolkit to execute a command or user-defined JCL returns a value equal to 4.A return code of 4 typically denotes a warning.If you elected to save the results of the batch job, you can check the Storage Toolkit Result Detail workspace to determine whether the warning requires further attention."}

situation_name: KS3_Storage_Gr_Pct_Free_Crit
description: Critical situation for the free space in a storage group
actions: {"The percentage of free space available for allocation in the storage group has dropped below the critical threshold.In order to prevent allocation failures, it may be necessary to either add one or more logical volumes to the storage group, or to migrate datasets off of the logical volumes in the storage group."}

situation_name: KS3_Storage_Gr_Pct_Free_Warning

description: An array has one or more DDMs that need rebuilding.
actions: {"Contact hardware support personnel to address the problem."}

situation_name: KS3_TDS_Array_Prob_Crit

situation_name: KS3_VTS_Disconnect_Time_Crit
description: The LCU disconnect time exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"The logical control unit disconnect time for the virtual tape server exceeds the critical threshold.This is often an indication that the tape volume cache capacity is being exceeded."}

situation_name: KS3_VTS_Disconnect_Time_Critical
description: The LCU disconnect time exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"The logical control unit disconnect time for the virtual tape server exceeds the critical threshold.This is often an indication that the tape volume cache capacity is being exceeded."}

situation_name: KS3_VTS_Host_GB_Warning
description: Host channel activity exceeds warning threshold.
actions: {"The activity between the MVS system and the virtual tape server on the host channels exceeds 19 GB over the hour interval.This could be an indication that the virtual tape server is being overloaded."}

situation_name: KS3_VTS_Pct_Copy_Throt_Warn
description: Throttling of copy operations (copy throttle) might occur in a source TS7700 tape virtualization engine (TS7700). This type of throttling happens when the cache of the TS7700 is more than 95% full of data that needs to be copied to target TS7700 peers. These peers are located in a TS7700 Grid configuration.
actions: {"If copy throttling occurs while all peers are available, check for a failure in the links between the TS7700s. Contact the service team of your company for assistance."}

situation_name: KS3_VTS_Pct_Wr_Over_Throt_Warn
description: Throttling of write overruns (write overrun throttling) might occur in a source TS7700 tape virtualization engine (TS7700). This type of throttling happens when the cache of theTS7700 is more than 95% full of data that needs to be copied to the physical tape that is attached to the TS7700.
actions: {"If write overrun throttling occurs, check whether the physical drives that are attached to the TS7700 are not available. Also check whether another type of failure has occurred withinthe TS7700 that prevents data from being copied from cache to physical tape. Contact the service team of your company for assistance."}

situation_name: KS3_VTS_Recall_Pct_Warning
description: The virtual mounts causing a physical mount exceed the threshold
actions: {"The percent of virtual tape mounts that required a physical tape mount to be satisfied exceeded the warning threshold.This may lead to unacceptably large virtual mount times.If so, then investigate the reason for the recalls.If rescheduling or removing the application workload is not possible, then it may be necessary to increase the cache capacity of the VTS."}

situation_name: KS3_VTS_Virt_MtPend_Av_Warning
description: The average virtual mount time exceeded the warning threshold.
actions: {"The average seconds required to satisfy a virtual mount in the virtual tape subsystem exceeded the warning threshold.If this persists, then further study is required to determine the cause for the elongated mount times.It may be due to VTS hostile applications or to a shortage of VTS resources."}

situation_name: KS3_VTS_Virt_MtPend_Mx_Warning

actions: {"The maximum seconds required to satisfy a virtual mount in the virtual tape subsystem exceeded the warning threshold.If this persists, then further study is required to determine the cause for the elongated mount times.It may be due to VTS hostile applications or to a shortage of VTS resources."}

situation_name: KS3_Vol_Cache_DFW_Retry_Crit

actions: {"The percentage of DASD fast write attempts for a volume that could not be satisfied due to a shortage of available non-volatile storage (NVS) space exceeded the critical threshold.Check for pinned NVS and correct the problem if NVS is pinned.Otherwise, if the impact onperformance is not acceptable, it may be necessary to move a volume or dataset to another cache control unit or to add NVS to this control unit."}

actions: {"The cache read hit percent for a volume is below the critical threshold.If performance is impacted determine the reason for the low read hit percent.Common problems are cache unfriendly applications and over utilization of the control unit."}

situation_name: KS3_Vol_EAV_Fragment_Index_Crit
description: The fragmentation index in the track managed area of an Extended Address Volume exceeds the critical threshold.
actions: {"The volume should be defragmented so that free extents in the track manage area are combined to help prevent dataset allocation failures."}

situation_name: KS3_Vol_EAV_Fragment_Index_Warn
description: The fragmentation index in the track managed area of an Extended Address Volume exceeds the warning threshold.
actions: {"The volume should be defragmented so that free extents in the track manage area are combined to help prevent dataset allocation failures."}

situation_name: KS3_Vol_EAV_Free_Space_Pct_Crit
description: The percentage of free space in the track managed area of an Extended Address Volume is below the critical threshold.
actions: {"If datasets on the volume will require more space in the track managed area, then either migrate some datasets to another volume or release space from datasets that may be over-allocated."}

situation_name: KS3_Vol_EAV_Free_Space_Pct_Warn

situation_name: KS3_Vol_Free_Space_Pct_Warning

situation_name: Linux_High_CPU_Overload
description: Percentage of time the processor is busy is extremely high.
actions: {"A frequently low value for CPU in idle state indicates that the processor can be overloaded. Check for run-away processes, or any configuration changes that may have caused CPU usage to spike. Check /var/log/messages for signs of hardware failures. Finally, if it this is due to an increase in workload, consider upgrading the processor."}

situation_name: Linux_High_CPU_Overload_2
description: Percentage of time the processor is busy is extremely high.

Check for run-away processes, or any configuration changes that may have caused CPU usage to spike. Check /var/log/messages for signs of hardware failures. Finally, if it this is due to an increase in workload, consider upgrading the processor."}

situation_name: Linux_High_CPU_System
description: The percentage of processor time that is used for system calls is high. The percentage of time spent servicing user level (API) calls versus system level calls can point out whether a system's load is primarily due to running applications, or due to operating system kernel overhead. High user-level to system level ratios tend to be good and are generally considered normal.
actions: {"Find the specific processes that are spending an inordinate amount of their CPU time servicing system calls. If these are system processes, look to see if there are any available kernel patches. Check for run-away processes, or any configuration changes that can have caused System CPU usage to spike. Check /var/log/messages for signs of hardware failures. Finally, look for other signs of sudden increase in the workload, such as excessive paging. If this is due to an increase in workload, considerincreasing available system resources by upgrading the system."}

situation_name: Linux_High_Packet_Collisions
description: Percentage of packet collisions during data transmission is high.
actions: {"Check your /var/log/messages for signs of hardware failures. Also check other devices on the same sub-net that may be experiencing network interface hardware failures. Check on the health of any networked applications that might be running on that system, including networked filesystems. If the cause of the increased collisions can be narrowed to a particular application, such as NFS or Apache, consider tuning some system parameters for better application performance, such as increasing network buffers. This might also reduce network collisions. Finally, if you are using wireline connections, double-check all your cable connections and their layout."}

situation_name: Linux_High_RPC_Retransmit
description: The percentage of retransmits due to RPC Server calls is extremely high.
actions: {"Try increasing your network socket buffers. If the high number of RPC retransmits are due to a networked file system, try retuning some of the TCP and UDP parameters. If possible, choose TCP over UDP as the network transport mechanism for the RPC application.Check to see if new patches are available for your RPC application. If available, apply these after a suitable system backup. Finally, for networked file systems, try modifying the filesystem mount options, such as application cache options. Check your man pages for suggestions."}

description: The number of RPC retransmits are high with no duplicate acknowledgements.
actions: {"Check for any NFS configuration changes that might affect performance and remediate. If there has been an increase NFS activity, check the NFS socket receive queue buffers. Consider increasing socket buffer sizes if the set is too small.Consider choosing more optimal NFS mount options to reduce network traffic. Consider using TCP as the transport for NFS if you are not already doing so."}

If the increase in swapping is due to valid workload increases, increase the amount of system real memory (RAM)."}
