situation_name: MQSeries_Alias_Queue_Problem
description: An MQOPEN or MQPUT1 call was issued specifying an alias queue as the definition, but the alias queue attribute is not recognized as a queue name, or the alias queue definition resolves to a queue that is not a local queue or local definition of a remote queue.
actions: {"Correct your queue definitions, or correct your MQI calls to match your current queue definitions.This situation is reporting an MQSeries event.The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Appl_MQI_Failures_High
description: The percentage of MQI request failures is high. The default \"% MQI Failure\" threshold value in the situation formula is a suggested value. The threshold value can be customized to suit your own environment.
actions: {"Determine the application name from the Formula view. Use the Application Debugging Trace to determine the cause of the failure and take the appropriate corrective action. Check the Application Statistics by Tran/Pgm workspace for statistics associated with this situation; it is available as an alternative workspace under the Application Statistics by ApplID navigator item. The Application Statistics by Tran/Pgm workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Appl_MQ_RespTime_High
description: The average response time for MQI requests is high. The default \"Avg MQ Resp Time\" threshold value in the situation formula is a suggested value. The threshold value can be customized to suit your own environment.
actions: {"Increase the dispatching priority for the queue manager to improve the response time. Check the Application Statistics by Tran/Pgm workspace for statistics associated with this situation; it is available as an alternative workspace under the Application Statistics by ApplID navigator item. The Application Statistics by Tran/Pgm workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Appl_Msgs_Put_High
description: The messages PUT from the application is high. The default \"Msgs Put\" threshold value in the situation formula is a suggested value. The threshold value can be customized to suit your own environment.
actions: {"Check if the application is in a loop putting messages to the queue. Check the Application Statistics by Tran/Pgm workspace for data associated with this situation. It is available as an alternative workspace under the Application Statistics by ApplID navigator item. The Application Statistics by Tran/Pgm workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Authority_Problem
description: The user ID is not authorized to use an MQI call for an object (such as opening a queue) or is not authorized to issue a command (such as alter and delete).
actions: {"If the user ID should not have the authorization, then you should note that it is attempting such access without authority to do so. If the user ID should be authorized, then you should update your security specifications to allow the access. This situation is reporting an MQSeries event.The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Automation_ChlStart
description: A channel is stopped.
actions: {"This situation will automatically start a stopped channel and reset the situation event. No corrective action is needed. Check the Channel Performance workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Channel Performance navigator item to access this workspace."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Automation_Fix_XmitQ
description: The XmitQ is not triggered.
actions: {"The IBM MQ Monitoring agent will alter the XmitQ to enable GET and turn on trigger control when this situation is detected and reset this situation event. No corrective action is needed. Check the Queue Statistics for Monitored Transmission Queues workspace. It is available as an alternative workspace under the Queue Statistics navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Bufpool_Buffer_Shrt_Crt
description: 95% or more of the buffers in the buffer pool are in use and not available for read requests. The default \"% of Bufrs Available\" threshold value in the situation formula is a suggested value. The threshold value can be customized to suit your own environment.
actions: {"In this event, updates will be performed concurrently, negatively affecting application performance. If this occurs, the buffer pool size should be increased. Check the Buffer Pool Statistics workspace for statistics associated with this situation. To access this workspace, click the Buffer Pool Statistics navigator item. The Buffer Pool Statistics workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Bufpool_Buffer_Shrt_Wrn
description: 85% to 95% of the buffers in the buffer pool are in use and not available for read requests. The default \"% of Bufrs Available\" threshold value in the situation formula is a suggested value. The threshold value can be customized to suit your own environment.
actions: {"This is a normal situation that results in MQSeries writing out updates to free up buffers. If this frequently occurs, the buffer pool size can be increased. Check the Buffer Pool Statistics workspace for statistics associated with this situation. To access this workspace, click the Buffer Pool Statistics navigator item. The Buffer Pool Statistics workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Bufpool_High_GetPage_IO
description: High % of GetPage requests resulting in Pageset I/O. The default \"GetPg IO %\" threshold value in the situation formula is a suggested value. The threshold value can be customized to suit your own environment.
actions: {"Increasing the buffer pool size might reduce the percentage of GetPage requests, resulting in more page requests being found in the buffer pool. If it does not, it might be that there are long delays between message PUTs and GETs. Check the Buffer Pool Statistics workspace for statistics associated with this situation. To access this workspace, click the Buffer Pool Statistics navigator item. The Buffer Pool Statistics workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_CICS_Channel_Stopped
description: A CICS channel is stopped.
actions: {"Use the Take Action view to start the channel. Check the Channel Performance workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Channel Performance navigator item to access this workspace."}

situation_name: MQSeries_ChInst_per_Client_High
description: The % Max Instances per Client value in the Channel Summary workspace is greater than 80%. The % Max Instances per Client attribute reflects the highest number of the channel instances that are grouped by clients as percentage of the maximum number of instances that can be started for a channel from a single client.
actions: {"Navigate to the Channel Summary workspace for the server-connection channel that triggers this situation, check the values of the Highest Instances per Client and Maximum Instances per Client attributes, evaluate if the value of the channel parameter, MAXINSTC (the maximum number of simultaneous instances of a server-connection channel that can be started from a single client), is large enough, and determine if a larger value is required by the potential for a large number of the server-connection channel instances from a single client. If the MAXINSTC value is fairly large, consider balancing MQI applications among all the clients or offloading part of the MQI applications to other server-connection channels or to other queue managers. For details of all the channel instances, check the Channel Performance and Channel Status workspaces."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Channel_Active_High
description: The percentage of active channel connections within the maximum number of channels that can be active is higher than 80%.
actions: {"In the Current Queue Manager Status workspace, check the values of the Active Channel Connections and Max Active Channels attributes, evaluate if the value of the queue manager parameter, MaxActiveChannels (the maximum number of channels that can be active at any time), is large enough, and determine if a larger maximum number is requried for the potential active channels. The count of active channels includes any current channel instances that are not in retrying, stopped, or starting states, including server connection channels. If the MaxActiveChannels value is fairly large, consider offloading part of the workload to other queue managers, since the MQI applications are the most likely cause to start a large number of server connection channels in a server-side queue manager. For detailed information about the channels that are active, check the Channel Summary, Channel Performance, and Channel Status workspaces."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Channel_Autodef_Error
description: The automatic definition of a channel has failed; this may be that an error occurred during the definition process, or the channel automatic-definition exit inhibited the definition.
actions: {"Consult the error identifier that is associated with the event. Note that event details are available in the Event Parameters workspace that can be linked to from the Event Log workspace for the event.The Event Log workspace is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item.If the action was suppressed by the channel automatic-definition exit, you need to update your exit specifications if the definition should have been allowed. Otherwise, the identifier will give the MQRC_* or MQRCCF_* reason code for the error that occurred."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Channel_Current_High
description: The percentage of current channel connections within the maximum number of channels that can be current is higher than 80%.
actions: {"In the Current Queue Manager Status workspace, check the values of the Current Channel Connections and Max Channels attributes, evaluate if the value of the queue manager parameter, MaxChannels (the maximum number of channels that can be current), is large enough, and determine if a larger maximum number is requried for the potential current channels. The count of current channels includes any channel instances that are not in an inactive state, including server connection channels. If the MaxChannels value is fairly large, consider offloading part of the workload to other queue managers, since the MQI applications are the most likely cause to start a large number of server connection channels in a server-side queue manager. For detailed information about the channels that are current, check the Channel Summary, Channel Performance, and Channel Status workspaces."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Channel_Initiator_Prob
description: The Channel Initiator for the monitored queue manager is in stopped, stopping or retrying state.
actions: {"Use the MQSC command START CHINIT to start the channel initiator. Check the Channel Initiator Status workspace. To access this workspace, select the Channel Initiator Status navigator item. The Channel Initiator Status workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Channel_Instance_High
description: The percentage of total number of the channel instances within the maximum number of instances that can be started for a server-connection channel is higher than 80%.
actions: {"Navigate to the Channel Summary workspace for the server-connection channel that triggers this situation, check the values of the Total Instances and Max Instances attributes, evaluate if the value of the channel parameter, MAXINST (the maximum number of simultaneous instances of a server-connection channel that can be started), is large enough, and determine if a larger value is required by the potential of a large number of server-connection channel instances. If the MAXINST value is fairly large, consider offloading part of the MQI applications to other server-connection channels or other queue managers. For details of all the channel instances, check the Channel Performance and Channel Status workspaces."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Channel_Out_Of_Sync
description: The local and remote queue managers do not agree on the next message sequence number.
actions: {"Determine the cause of the inconsistency. If the condition cannot be resolved, use Take Action to issue the RESET CHANNEL command at the sending end of the channel. You can issue the command automatically by specifying the RESET CHANNEL command and substituting the attribute Error_Log.Involved_Object in the Action tab of the situation editor. Refer to IBM MQ (WebSphere MQ) manual for usage of the RESET CHANNEL command. Check the Error Log workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Error Log navigator item to access this workspace."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Channel_Remain_Indoubt
description: The Highest In-Doubt Samples value in the Channel Summary workspace is greater than 1. The IBM MQ Monitoring agent samples the monitored queue managers for performance data. The default sample interval is 300 seconds, which is configured by the SAMPINT parameter. This situation alerts for the continuous in-doubt samples that are greater than one, which indicates that a channel remains in-doubt for too long. And the connection between the in-doubt channel and the remote channel about which messages are sent and received is lost.
actions: {"Find out which channel triggers this situation in either the Initial Situation Values and Current Situation Values table views of the situation workspace, or in the Channel Summary workspace.","You can use the Batch Heartbeat channel parameter (BATCHHB) to reduce the opportunity for a channel to be placed in doubt. When this paramter is specified, a sender channel first checks if the remote channel is still active before it takes any further action. If no response is received, the receiver channel is considered to be no longer active. The messages can be rolled back and rerouted, and the sender channel is not put in doubt.","In-doubt channel problems are usually solved automatically when the connection is re-established. However, you can manually resynchronize the channel when necessary. For manual synchronization process, refer to IBM MQ (WebSphere MQ) online help."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Channel_SSL_Error
description: A channel using Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) failed to establish an SSL connection.
actions: {"To determine the reason for this error, check the Event Qualifier column in the Event Log workspace, which provides the MQRQ_SSL_* error code that identifies the reason. The Event Log workspace is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Channels_Indoubt
description: An in-doubt channel was detected.
actions: {"MQSeries usually resolves in-doubt channels automatically. Determine, from the attributes, the LUWID and sequence number for the last message. If needed, use the RESOLVE CHANNEL command. Check the Queue Manager Status workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Queue Manager Status navigator item to access this workspace. Check the Channel Performance workspace to see which channels are in indoubt status."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Cluster_QMgr_Suspended
description: A cluster queue manager is suspended if SUSPEND QMGR command is issued.
actions: {"This is to inform other queue managers in a cluster that the local queue manager is not available for processing and cannot be sent messages to. Its action can be reversed by the RESUME QMGR command. Check the Cluster Queue Manager workspace for data associated with this situation. To access this workspace, click the Cluster Queue Manager navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Conversion_Error
description: A channel was unable to carry out data conversion and the MQGET call to get a message from the transmission queue resulted in a data conversion error.
actions: {"To determine why the conversion failed, consult the conversion reason code associated with the event. Note that event details are available in the Event Parameters workspace that can be linked to from the Event Log workspace for the event. The Event Log workspace is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Dead_Letter
description: The Dead Letter Queue is not empty.
actions: {"The Dead-Letter Queue Messages workspace shows the reason codes for messages in the Dead Letter Queue. These reason codes can be used to determine the corrective action to take. Check the Dead-Letter Queue Messages workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Dead-Letter Queue Messages navigator item to access this workspace."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Delayed_Message_Group
description: This situation is an example of the type of situation that can be written for the Message Statistics attribute group. In this situation, a queue named TEST.QUEUE is monitored for messages older than 300.00 seconds. Note: To use this situation, you must change the queue name to a valid queue name; otherwise, the situation will fail. You must make changes to the situation only in the Description field of the situation.
actions: {"This situation is intended to be copied, renamed, and customized to specify desired thresholds and queue name. Note that a separate situation must be written for each individual queue. Check the Current Message Statistics workspace for statistics associated with this situation. To access this workspace, click the Queue Definitions navigator item to go to the Queue Definitions workspace and then link to view the Current Message Statistics workspace for any given queue."}

situation_name: MQSeries_High_Delayed_Messages
description: This situation is an example of the type of situation that can be written for the Message Statistics attribute group. In this situation, a queue named TEST.QUEUE2 is monitored for 10 messages that have been on the queue for longer than 300.00 seconds. Note: To use this situation, you must change the queue name to a valid queue name; otherwise, the situation will fail. You must make changes to the situation only in the Description field of the situation.
actions: {"This situation is intended to be copied, renamed, and customized to specify desired thresholds and queue name. Note that a separate situation must be written for each individual queue. Check the Current Message Statistics workspace for statistics associated with this situation. To access this workspace, click the Queue Definitions navigator item to go to the Queue Definitions workspace and then link to view the Current Message Statistics workspace for any given queue."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Inhibit_Problem
description: MQGET calls are currently inhibited for the queue or MQPUT and MQPUT1 calls are currently inhibited for the queue.
actions: {"If the get or put activity should not be inhibited, issue an ALTER queue command to specify GET(ENABLED) or PUT(ENABLED. This situation is reporting an MQSeries event. The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Listener_Not_Started
description: The listener is not started.
actions: {"Use START LISTENER to start a channel listener. Check the Listener Status workspace for data associated with this situation. It is available as an alternative workspace under the Queue Manager Status navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Local_DestQ_Depth_High
description: The depth threshold of a subscription's destination queue has been reached.
actions: {"Go to the Subscription Status workspace and check if the subscription that uses the queue that triggered the situation is durable. If it is a non-durable subscription, you can increase the maximum depth of the subscription's destination queue. If it is a durable subscription, right-click the row in the Subscription Status workspace that represents the subscription and link to the Application Connections workspace. If the ApplicationConnections workspace contains no data, the application is stoppedand messages sent to the queue by the publisher are not beingremoved from the queue. Start the applicatoin to resolve theproblem. If the Application Connections workspace contains data,then messages are probably not being processed fast enough by the subscribing application. To resolve this problem, increase themaximum depth of the subscription's destination queue."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Local_DestQ_Full
description: The destination queue of a subscription is full.
actions: {"Go to the Subscription Status workspace and check if the subscription that uses the queue that triggered the situation isdurable. If it is a non-durable subscription, you can increase themaximum depth of the subscription's destination queue.If it is a durable subscription, right-click the row in the Subscription Status workspace that represents the subscription and link to the Application Connections workspace. If the ApplicationConnections workspace contains no data, the application is stoppedand messages sent to the queue by the publisher are not beingremoved from the queue. Start the applicatoin to resolve the problem. If the Application Connections workspace contains data, then messages are probably not being processed fast enough by the subscribing application. To resolve this problem, increase the maximum depth of the subscription's destination queue."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Local_Object_Unknown
description: For an open request, the ObjectName in the object descriptor is not recognized for the specified object type.
actions: {"Correct your object definition, or correct your MQI calls to match your current definition. This situation is reporting an MQSeries event. The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_LogMgr_Buffer_Waits
description: An application had to wait because log buffers were being written to the log.
actions: {"This situation indicates a problem writing to the active log. Review subsystem initialization parameters relating to logging in CSQ6LOGP, especially, the value for OUTBUFF. Check the Log Manager Performance workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Log Manager Performance navigator item to access this workspace. The Log Manager Performance workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_LogMgr_High_Archiv_Read
description: High number of reads resolved from an archive log data set. The default \"Arch Log Read %\" threshold value in the situation formula is a suggested value. The threshold value can be customized to suit your own environment.
actions: {"Review applications to reduce length of units of recovery, increase the size of the active log, or both. Check the Log Manager Performance workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Log Manager Performance navigator item to access this workspace. The Log Manager Performance workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_LogMgr_Reads_Delayed
description: Log reads have been delayed because MAXRTU limited the number of archive log data sets that could be allocated at the same time. The default \"% Rd Log Delayed\" threshold value in the situation formula is recommended to be 1 percent.
actions: {"Increase MAXRTU value in CSQ6LOGP or using the MQSC command SET LOG. Check the Log Manager Performance workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Log Manager Performance navigator item to access this workspace. The Log Manager Performance workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Logging_High_RBA_Crit
description: The 6-byte log RBA of the queue manager has reached X'730000000000'. This situation indicates that the log RBA is approaching its upper limit when the queue manager uses 6-byte RBAs.
actions: {"Reset the logs. If using 6-byte RBAs, allowing the log RBA to reach the maximum value of X'FFFFFFFFFFFF' will result in an unplanned outage, and the queue manager needs to be restarted. For information about how to reset the logs, refer to IBM MQ documentation.","NOTE: When the queue manager is set to use 8-byte RBAs, you should be using a situation testing the 8-byte RBA value instead of the example in this situation based on 6-byte RBAs.The attribute name to test for 8-byte RBAs is \"UOW Start RBA 8 Bytes\", which is a 16-byte hex character string. The comparison value would be larger in that case."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Logging_High_RBA_Warn
description: The 6-byte log RBA of the queue manager has reached X'700000000000'. This situation indicates that the log RBA is approaching its upper limit when the queue manager uses 6-byte RBAs.
actions: {"Reset the logs. If using 6-byte RBAs, allowing the log RBA to reach the maximum value of X'FFFFFFFFFFFF' will result in an unplanned outage, and the queue manager needs to be restarted. For information about how to reset the logs, refer to IBM MQ documentation.","NOTE: When the queue manager is set to use 8-byte RBAs, you should be using a situation testing the 8-byte RBA value instead of the example in this situation based on 6-byte RBAs.The attribute name to test for 8-byte RBAs is \"UOW Start RBA 8 Bytes\", which is a 16-byte hex character string. The comparison value would be larger in that case."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Logging_Suspended
description: Indicates whether logging is suspended.
actions: {"Logging is suspended if SUSPEND QMGR LOG command is issued. All logging and update activity for the queue manager is suspended until RESUME QMGR LOG command is issued(z/OS only, Version 5.3 and above). Check the Log Manager Performance workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Log Manager Performance navigator item to access this workspace. The Log Manager Performance workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_MQSecure_Problem
description: A problem is detected by MQSecure.
actions: {"The SYSTEM.MQSECURE.PROBLEMS queue is not empty. Determine the cause from the MQSecure Channel exit log and take the appropriate corrective action. Check the Queue Statistics workspace for statistics associated with this situation. It is available as an alternative workspace under the Queue Statistics navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_MQ_Channel_Stopped
description: A channel is stopped because of an error.
actions: {"Consult the Event Qualifier column in the Formula view for the reason of the failure and perform the corrective action accordingly. This situation is reporting an MQSeries event. The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Manager_Inactive
description: A queue manager is inactive.
actions: {"The queue manager is probably down. Start the queue manager and verify that it is available for connection. Check the Queue Manager Status workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Queue Manager Status navigator item to access this workspace."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Manager_Inactive_Event
description: A queue manager is inactive until manually reset.
actions: {"The queue manager is probably down. Start the queue manager and verify that it is available for connection. You need to reset this event manually. This situation is reporting an MQSeries event. The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_No_Queue_Messages_Read
description: No messages have been read.
actions: {"There are messages on the queue and there has been no read activity during the sampling interval. Determine the cause and take the appropriate corrective action.Check the Queue Statistics workspace for the statistics associated with this situation. It is available as an alternative workspace under the Queue Statistics navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Old_Message_On_Queue
description: The age of the oldest message on a queue is older than the given number of seconds.This can indicate that messages are not being processed in a timely way. The default \"Oldest Msg Age\" threshold value in the situation formula is a suggested value. The threshold value can be customized to suit your own environment.
actions: {"Look at the application that should be removing messages from the queue and determine if there is a problem. Consider starting another copy of the application, if possible, to drain the queue faster.Check the Queue Status workspace for data associated with this situation; it is available as an alternative workspace under the Queue Statistics navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_PageSet_Unavailable
description: A defined page set is not available for use.
actions: {"Determine the cause by examining the MQSeries log and take the appropriate corrective action.Check the Page Set Statistics workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Page Set Statistics navigator item to access it. The Page Set Statistics workspace is available only on z/OS."}

situation_name: MQSeries_PageSet_Usage_High
description: Pageset almost full and maximum extents reached. The default \"% Pages In Use\" and \"Total Extents\" threshold values in the situation formula are suggested values. The threshold values can be customized to suit your own environment.
actions: {"Review contents of queues to see what messages are in the pageset and why. If this is not a temporary unexpected message accumulation, increase the size of the pageset or move some queues to another pageset.Check the Page Set Statistics workspace for data associated with this situation.Link to the Queue Statistics workspace for queues associated with a given page set, and then link to view Queue Messages for any given queue."}

situation_name: MQSeries_PubSub_Problem
description: The Pub/Sub engine or hierarchical connection is either inactive or failed.
actions: {"Determine the cause for this alert from the Pub Sub Status column in the Formula view and take the appropriate corrective action. Check the Publish Subscribe Status workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Publish Subscribe navigator item to access this workspace."}

situation_name: MQSeries_QMgr_Instance_Standby
description: An instance of the queue manager is detected to be running as a standby, or running elsewhere.
actions: {"Determine the cause of this informational alert by checking the QMgr Status column in the Formula view and take appropriate actions if necessary. View the Queue Manager Status workspace for data that is associated with this situation. Click the Queue Manager Status navigator item to access this workspace."}

situation_name: MQSeries_QSG_CFBackup_Delay
description: A coupling facility structure backup has not occurred in the last 24 hours. Frequent CF structure backups minimize restart time.
actions: {"A backup should be scheduled to avoid the possibility of a lengthy outage. Consider automating the backup process, or if the process is automated, investigate why it is not being successfully completed. Check the Queue Sharing Group CF Structure Backups view for data associated with this situation. To access this view, click the QSG CF Structure Statistics item under the Queue-Sharing Group navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_QSG_CFStruct_Failed
description: A coupling facility structure associated with the queue sharing group fails.
actions: {"If the status is failed, run recovery procedures for your coupling facility structures, if necessary,restore from the backup. Check the Queue Sharing Group CF Structure Statistics view for data associated with this situation. To access this view, click the QSG CF Structure Statistics item under the Queue-Sharing Group navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_QSG_CFStruct_HighEnts
description: The percentage of list entries used by a coupling facility structure that is associated with the queue sharing group is high.
actions: {"You need to control application usage. If the list entries are exhausted, applications might fail with reason code MQRC_STORAGE_MEDIUM_FULL. Check the Queue Sharing Group CF Structure Statistics view for data associated with this situation. To access this view, click the QSG CF Structure Statistics item under the Queue-Sharing Group navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_QSG_CFStruct_HighMem
description: The percentage of storage used by a coupling facility structure that is associated with the queue sharing group is high.
actions: {"If not at maximum, set a larger memory allotment. Control application usage. Check the Queue Sharing Group CF Structure Statistics view for statistics associated with this situation. To access this view, click the QSG CF Structure Statistics item under the Queue-Sharing Group navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_QSG_CFStruct_Inhibit
description: A coupling facility structure associated with the queue sharing group is either being backed up or being recovered. Ordinarily this situation requires no action.
actions: {"If it persists, verify that the backup or recovery action is proceeding normally and correct any problems found. Check the Queue Sharing Group CF Structure Statistics view for data associated with this situation. To access this view, click the QSG CF Structure Statistics item under the Queue-Sharing Group navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_QSG_DB2_Failed
description: The queue manager is running but cannot connect to DB2 because the DB2 server has abnormally terminated.
actions: {"Restart the DB2 server with recovery procedures. Check the Queue Sharing Group Queue Manager Status view for data associated with this situation. To access this view, click the Queue-Sharing Group item under the Queue-Sharing Group navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_QSG_QMgr_Failed
description: A queue manager in the QSG has abnormally terminated.
actions: {"Restart the queue manager with recovery procedures. Check the Queue Sharing Group Queue Manager Status view for data associated with this situation. To access this view, click the Queue-Sharing Group item under the Queue-Sharing Group navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_QSG_QMgr_NotStarted
description: A queue manager is defined to the QSG but has not yet started.
actions: {"Unless otherwise advised, start the queue manager to correct this problem. Check the Queue Sharing Group Queue Manager Status view for data associated with this situation. To access this view, click the Queue-Sharing Group item under the Queue-Sharing Group navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_QSG_Queue_HighUse
description: The number of messages on a queue of a queue sharing group is high.
actions: {"Either start more processes to service the queue or reduce the number of applications that are putting messages on the queue. Investigate performance issues on the active queue managers, particularly factors that might inhibit coupling facility access. You might consider increasing the maximum queue depth if adequate memory and list entries are available in the application structure. Check the Queue Sharing Group Queue Statistics view for data associated with this situation. To access this view, click the QSG Resources item under the Queue-Sharing Group navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_QSG_StrConn_Failed
description: The connection to the coupling facility application structure that is associated with the queue sharing group fails.
actions: {"If the queue manager has failed, restart it with recovery procedures. If it is inactive, restart it. Check the Queue Sharing Group CF Structure Connection Statistics view for data associated with this situation. To access this view, click the Queue-Sharing Group item under the Queue-Sharing Group navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Queue_Depth_High
description: A queue has reached its high depth threshold.
actions: {"You can increase the maximum depth of the queue or remove some messages from the queue. This situation is reporting an MQSeries event. The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item. Check the Queue Statistics workspace to see which queues have reached their high depth thresholds."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Queue_Full
description: A queue is full.
actions: {"You can increase the maximum depth of the queue or remove some messages from the queue. This situation is reporting an MQSeries event. The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item. Check the Queue Statistics workspace to see which queues are full. The Queue Statistics workspace is available as an alternative workspace under the Queue Statistics navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Queue_Full_Until
description: A queue is full.
actions: {"You can increase the maximum depth of the queue or remove some messages from the queue. This alert is automatically reset after 15 minutes. This situation is reporting an MQSeries event. The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item. Check the Queue Statistics workspace to see which queue is full."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Queue_Manager_Problem
description: A problem is detected in a queue manager.
actions: {"Determine the cause for this alert from the QMgr Status column in the Formula view and take the appropriate corrective action. Check the Queue Manager Status workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Queue Manager Status navigator item to access this workspace."}
metadata: {"odp_table_name":[],"metric_key":["mq_manager_status"],"teps_full_name":["Managers.MQ_Manager_Status"],"formula":"*IF *VALUE Managers.MQ_Manager_Status *EQ QueueManager_Not_Available *OR *VALUE Managers.MQ_Manager_Status *EQCommandServer_Not_Responding *OR *VALUE Managers.MQ_Manager_Status *EQ Dynamic_Queue_Allocation_Error *OR *VALUE Managers.MQ_Manager_Status *EQ Cluster_Repository_Unavailable *OR *VALUE Managers.MQ_Manager_Status *EQ Inactive"}

situation_name: MQSeries_Queue_Manager_Quiesce
description: The queue manager is quiescing.
actions: {"Use the strmqm command to restart the queue manager. Check the Queue Manager Status workspace for data associated with this situation. Click the Queue Manager Status navigator item to access this workspace."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Queue_Not_Being_Read
description: There are messages on a queue, but there is no application to remove messages from the queue. This can lead to a full queue if left unattended.
actions: {"Start the application that should be removing messages from the queue. Check the Queue Status workspace for data associated with this situation. It is available as an alternative workspace under the Queue Statistics navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Queue_Service_Int_High
description: Queue service time reached high threshold.
actions: {"No successful GETs or PUTs have been detected within an interval greater than the limit specified in QServiceInterval. No corrective action is needed. This is to identify that this event has occurred. This situation is reporting an MQSeries event. The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item."}

situation_name: MQSeries_Remote_Queue_Error
description: An application (or the queue manager) cannot access a (remote) queue on another queue manager. For example, the transmission queue to be used might not be correctly defined.
actions: {"Correct your object definitions, or correct your MQI calls to match your current definitions. This situation is reporting an MQSeries event. The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item."}
metadata: {"odp_table_name":[],"metric_key":["event"],"teps_full_name":["MQSeries_Events.Event"],"formula":"*IF ( ( *VALUE MQSeries_Events.Event *EQ Queue_Type_Error ) *OR ( *VALUE MQSeries_Events.Event *EQ Default_Xmit_Queue_Type_Error ) *OR ( *VALUE MQSeries_Events.Event *EQ Default_Xmit_Queue_Usage_Error ) *OR (*VALUE MQSeries_Events.Event *EQ Remote_Queue_Name_Error ) *OR ( *VALUE MQSeries_Events.Event *EQ Transmission_Queue_Type_Error ) *OR ( *VALUE MQSeries_Events.Event *EQ Transmission_Queue_Usage_Error ) )"}

situation_name: MQSeries_Remote_Queue_Problem
description: An application cannot access a remote queue on another queue manager. The reason may be that the default or other transmission queue is unknown, or that the remote queue manager is unknown.
actions: {"Correct your object definitions, or correct your MQI calls to match your current definitions. This situation is reporting an MQSeries event. The Event Log workspace shows recent MQSeries events that have occurred; it is available as an alternative workspace under the MQSeries Events navigator item."}

situation_name: MSU_4Hour_Warning
description: MSU 4-Hour Rolling Average is High
actions: {"The 4-hour MSU average is high.This condition may or may not be a matter of immediate concern.You may need to adjust your workload to prevent your MSUs from exceeding your capacity.If this is a chronic issue, consider upgrading your MSU capacity.","If this value is within your expected range, and not above your MSU capacity, consider adjusting the situation threshold to a larger value."}

situation_name: MVS_CFStructStat_FalseLock_Crit
description: Coupling Facility Structure Statistics Critical
actions: {"Coupling facility false contention for lock structures has reached a high level.False contention should be less than half of total lock contention or less than 0.5% of total lock requests.If this condition occurs frequently, the size of the lock structure should be increased."}

situation_name: MVS_CFStructStat_FalseLock_Warn
description: Coupling Facility Structure Statistics Warning
actions: {"Coupling facility false contention for lock structures is about to reach a high level.False contention should be less than half of total lock contention or less than 0.5% of total lock requests.If this condition occurs frequently, the size of the lock structure should be increased."}

situation_name: MVS_CFStructToMVS_Requests_Crit
description: Coupling Facility Structure to z/OS Requests Critical
actions: {"The coupling facility performance has deteriorated severely.Check the status of the coupling links and the performance data for the coupling facility machine or LPAR.A link may be down or a processor may be offline or malfunctioning.If the coupling facility is in an LPAR with shared processors, the overall CPC may be fully loaded, thus causing the LPAR weights to come into effect.If more LPs are assigned to the CF than its share of total weight can support, try varying a LP offline."}

situation_name: MVS_CFStructToMVS_Requests_Warn
description: Coupling Facility Structure to z/OS Requests Warning
actions: {"The coupling facility performance has deteriorated to the extent that requests may begin to time out or otherwise fail.Check the status of the coupling links and the performance data for the coupling facility machine or LPAR.You may have exhausted the current capacity."}

situation_name: MVS_CFStructUsers_Connect_Crit
description: Coupling Facility Structure Users Connectivity Status Critical
actions: {"Coupling facility connections are failing and rebuild is not working.If another coupling facility is available as a backup, it should be made the primary facility.Check the links and the status of the coupling facility hardware."}

situation_name: MVS_CFStructUsers_Connect_Warn
description: Coupling Facility Structure Users Connectivity Status Warning
actions: {"Coupling facility connections are failing and rebuild is in effect.If another coupling facility is available as a backup, it should be made the primary facility.Check the links and the status of the coupling facility hardware."}

situation_name: MVS_CFStruct_Status_Crit
description: Coupling Facility Structures Status Critical
actions: {"Coupling facility structures have failed.An immediate rebuild is necessary.If another coupling facility is available as a backup, it should be made the primary facility."}

situation_name: MVS_CFStruct_Status_Warn
description: Coupling Facility Structures Status Warning
actions: {"Coupling facility structures are about to fail.A rebuild may soon be necessary.If another coupling facility is available as a backup, it should be made the primary facility."}
metadata: {"odp_table_name":["mcfstrct"],"metric_key":["structure_status"],"teps_full_name":["CF_Structures.Structure_Status"],"formula":"*IF *VALUE CF_Structures.Structure_Status *NE ActiveInUse *AND *VALUE CF_Structures.Structure_Status *NE ActivePersistent *AND *VALUE CF_Structures.Structure_Status *NE ActiveDuplexAlternate *AND *VALUE CF_Structures.Structure_Status *NE ActiveDuplexPrimary *AND *VALUE CF_Structures.Structure_Status *NE Defined *AND *VALUE CF_Structures.Structure_Status *NE Failed *AND *VALUE CF_Structures.Structure_Status *NE PolicyChange *AND *VALUE CF_Structures.Structure_Status *NE Transitional"}

situation_name: MVS_CFSystemPaths_Busy_Crit
description: Coupling Facility System Paths Critical
actions: {"Coupling facility path contention exceeds 95%.Severe performance degradation will continue until action is taken to reduce the traffic or increase the data bandwidth to the coupling facility.Traffic may be reduced by adding coupling facilities; bandwidth may be increased by using more links or faster links.See the IBM Redbook OS/390 Parallel Sysplex Configuration Volume 2: Cookbook, Publication number SG24-5638 for details and further recommendations."}

situation_name: MVS_CFSystemPaths_Busy_Warn
description: Coupling Facility System Paths Warning
actions: {"Coupling facility path contention is high, or a link is down.Performance degradation may continue until action is taken to reduce the traffic or increase the data bandwidth to the coupling facility.Traffic may be reduced by adding coupling facilities; bandwidth may be increased by using more links or faster links.See the IBM Redbook OS/390 Parallel Sysplex Configuration Volume 2: Cookbook, Publication number SG24-5638 for details and further recommendations."}

situation_name: MVS_CFSystems_Performance_Crit
description: Coupling Facility Systems Performance Critical
actions: {"Coupling facility may be in an overload condition.Check the performance data for the coupling facility and, if it is unacceptable, determine if some large structures can be replicated in another facility to reduce the data rate.The long term solution may require an increase in coupling facility capacity or a technology upgrade to faster coupling links."}

situation_name: MVS_CFSystems_Performance_Warn
description: Coupling Facility Systems Performance Warning

User Query: How does the bond interface work in IBM DB2 Analytics Accelerator for z/OS? Agent: The bond interface in IBM DB2 Analytics Accelerator for z/OS is a virtual network device driver that creates a virtual network interface to the operating system and its applications. It determines the physical connection that is used, with only one being active at any time. If the active connection fails, the passive connection is activated automatically, allowing applications to continue using the bond interface without requiring a configuration change. User Query: What is the purpose of the OSA-Express card in the network setup for IBM DB2 Analytics Accelerator for z/OS? Agent: The OSA-Express card in the network setup for IBM DB2 Analytics Accelerator for z/OS is used to connect the switches with the OSA-Express card and the Netezza hosts. In case of a failover on the accelerator side, the switch guarantees a path from System z to the active host in a basic setup, while a high-availability setup uses two OSA-Express cards, two switches, and additional cables to ensure continuous connectivity. Agent: A direct network connection between System z and IBM DB2 Analytics Accelerator for z/OS has severe limitations, which is why IBM does not support such a setup in production, development, or test environments. situation_name: Metric cf_structure_name is lower than usual on MQ Queue Sharing Group
description: Anomaly detected: Metric cf_structure_name is lower than usual on MQ Queue Sharing Group
actions: {"If the z/OS cf_structure_name is low, it could indicate that the Coupling Facility (CF) structure used by IBM MQ for z/OS has approximately 50% entries in use, even though the queues that use it have no depth or have a low CURDEPTH. This situation is considered normal as it is caused by the batch delete mechanism not being driven yet for messages that were put out-of-syncpoint. When an out-of-syncpoint MQGET is performed, the message is moved to an uncommitted list header on the structure, and the message is added to the batch delete list. When an in-syncpoint MQGET is performed, the message is moved to the uncommitted list header, and then, when a commit is issued, the message is deleted. A message takes up one structure entry and however many 256-byte elements are needed for the message plus a x'30'-byte header. The batch delete mechanism does not take place for a particular queue manager until the number of entries to be deleted reaches a threshold of 341. This threshold is per queue manager, so you could have up to (341 * N) entries in the structure, where N=number_of_queue_managers_in_qsg, when all queues on the structure have no messages and no uncommitted activity. If the structure fills, the entries to be deleted are cleaned up. This behavior is observed in the  In use  column of the CSQOREXX panel for DISPLAY CFSTATUS and might also be indicated by the IXC585E STRUCTURE <structure_name> IS AT OR ABOVE STRUCTURE FULL MONITORING THRESHOLD message. In summary, a low cf_structure_name does not necessarily indicate a problem, as it could be due to the normal operation of the batch delete mechanism for out-of-syncpoint messages. However, if you suspect a problem, consult the relevant IBM documentation or seek assistance from IBM support."}

situation_name: Metric cpu_time_since_reset is higher than usual on CICS Region
description: Anomaly detected: Metric cpu_time_since_reset is higher than usual on CICS Region
actions: {"If the z/OS cpu_time_since_reset is high, it could be due to an issue with the OMEGAMON Messaging agent leaving zombie or orphan processes. This issue has been resolved in OMEGAMON Messaging on z/OS V730 FP2. To fix this, you should apply the following 9 PTFs and any pre-reqs or co-reqs: HKCF730 UA83334, HKMC730 UA83330, HKMQ730 UA83394, UA83707, UA91741, UA92394, HKQI730 UA83372, UA94112, UA95011. Additionally, high cpu_time_since_reset could also be caused by tasks browsing resources, such as files by the file control domain, terminals, functions where CICS domains browse the CICS catalog, RDO checking, and many other internal areas within CICS where it is desirable to give up control to allow other tasks an opportunity to run. This is typically seen for tasks that are browsing resources, and a CICS domain issues a DFHDSATM FUNCTION(CHANGE_PRIORITY) which results in the DFHTASK 184 GVUPWAIT monitor field count and time being incremented. Lastly, high cpu_time_since_reset could be due to high CPU usage in CICS Transaction Server for z/OS (CICS TS) transactions, especially when running Top Secret from CA Technologies. In this case, you should apply APARs SO00168 and SO00169 if you plan to implement AES256 encryption in CA Top Secret R . In all cases, it is recommended to gather relevant documentation and submit it to the support team for further analysis. This documentation may include HPU version and maintenance level, DB2 version, mode and maintenance level, complete job output with MSGLEVEL=(1,1), INZTVAR and INZUTIL from SINZSAMP, DDL of all involved DB2 objects, and SYSABEND data set in case of ABEND."}

actions: {"If the z/OS database_deq_calls is low, it might indicate that the batch delete mechanism has not been driven yet for messages that were put out-of-syncpoint. This is a normal state because when an out-of-syncpoint MQGET is performed, the message is moved to an uncommitted list header on the structure, and the message is added to the batch delete list. When an in-syncpoint MQGET is performed, the message is moved to the uncommitted list header, then, when a commit is issued, the message is deleted. A message takes up one structure entry and however many 256-byte elements are needed for the message plus a x'30'-byte header. The batch delete mechanism does not take place for a particular queue manager until the number of entries to be deleted reaches a threshold of 341. This threshold is per queue manager, so you could have up to (341 * N) entries in the structure, where N=number_of_queue_managers_in_qsg, when all queues on the structure have no messages and no uncommitted activity. If the structure fills, the entries to be deleted are cleaned up. To address a low database_deq_calls issue, you should not arbitrarily increase MAXPROCSYS, MAXPROCUSER, or PROCUSERMAX to unsustainable values. This KPI is directly derived from QTXADEA in the SQL Accounting section of the SMF type 100 subtype 1 record. If deadlocks become problematic, they should be handled as a performance problem, not as a hang. This is because a deadlocked process does not use any CPU time, unlike a process that is caught in an infinite loop or suffering from very bad performance."}

When an out-of-syncpoint MQGET is performed, the message is moved to an uncommitted list header on the structure, and the message is added to the batch delete list. A message takes up one structure entry and however many 256-byte elements are needed for the message plus a x'30'-byte header. The batch delete mechanism does not take place for a particular queue manager until the number of entries to be deleted reaches a threshold of 341. This threshold is per queue manager, so you could have up to (341 * N) entries in the structure, where N=number_of_queue_managers_in_qsg, when all queues on the structure have no messages and no uncommitted activity. situation_name: Metric hwm_common_subspace_users is higher than usual on CICS Region
description: Anomaly detected: Metric hwm_common_subspace_users is higher than usual on CICS Region
actions: {"If the z/OS hwm_common_subspace_users is high, it could indicate that the Data Virtualization Manager (DVM) Server is running in the system's default service class SYSOTHER. This often results in suboptimal performance as SYSOTHER is typically one of the less performing service classes. To resolve this issue, it is recommended to properly define DV to WLM. To do this, a STC classification rule for the DV subsystem should be defined within WLM. If a rule does not exist, one should be created. All work that the DV server does not specially create an enclave for will run in this service class. This includes internal admin subtasks as well as startup and shutdown. It's important to note that simply changing the default WLM service class of the DV address space does not affect newly created enclaves used to run client transactions or even DV administrative subtasks. When each subtask is created, such as for a client connection or transaction, each subtask then creates individual enclaves based on the WLM transaction name or other classification fields associated with the request. If no WLM rule is found, the WLM default is taken, which is not the server (STC rule) default, but rather the default service class when no classification is found in WLM. In summary, to address high hwm_common_subspace_users, ensure that the DV subsystem is correctly classified in WLM to avoid running in the SYSOTHER service class, which can lead to performance degradation."}

description: Anomaly detected: Metric in_storage_read_log_percent is lower than usual on MQ Queue Manager
actions: {"If the in_storage_read_log_percent is low, it indicates that a Coupling Facility (CF) structure used by IBM MQ for z/OS has approximately 50% entries in use, even though the queues that use it have no depth or have a low CURDEPTH. This state is normal because the batch delete mechanism was not driven yet for messages that were put out-of-syncpoint. When an out-of-syncpoint MQGET is performed, the message is moved to an uncommitted list header on the structure, and the message is added to the batch delete list. When an in-syncpoint MQGET is performed, the message is moved to the uncommitted list header; then, when a commit is issued, the message is deleted. The batch delete mechanism does not take place for a particular queue manager until the number of entries to be deleted reaches a threshold of 341. This threshold is per queue manager, so you could have up to (341 * N) entries in the structure, where N=number_of_queue_managers_in_qsg, when all queues on the structure have no messages and no uncommitted activity. If the structure fills, the entries to be deleted are cleaned up. There is no specific action to take if in_storage_read_log_percent is low. The described behavior is considered normal and does not require intervention. The batch delete mechanism will eventually remove the uncommitted messages, ensuring the structure does not become overly congested."}

actions: {"If the z/OS mqcbs_per_second is low, it indicates that the number of calls or starts per second of the MQ API routine MQCB for this queue manager is low. This could be due to a normal state where the batch delete mechanism was not driven yet for messages that were put out-of-syncpoint. When an out-of-syncpoint MQGET is performed, the message is moved to an uncommitted list header on the structure, and the message is added to the batch delete list. When an in-syncpoint MQGET is performed, the message is moved to the uncommitted list header; then, when a commit is issued, the message is deleted. A message takes up one structure entry and however many 256-byte elements are needed for the message plus a x'30'-byte header. The batch delete mechanism does not take place for a particular queue manager until the number of entries to be deleted reaches a threshold of 341. This threshold is per queue manager, so you could have up to (341 * N) entries in the structure, where N=number_of_queue_managers_in_qsg, when all queues on the structure have no messages and no uncommitted activity. If the structure fills, the entries to be deleted are cleaned up. In this context, a low mqcbs_per_second might not necessarily indicate a problem, as it could be a normal state. However, if you suspect that the low value is causing issues, you might want to review your queue manager's configuration and activity to ensure that it is functioning as expected. If the low value is causing problems, you might consider increasing the number of messages being processed or optimizing the queue manager's performance to increase the mqcbs_per_second. Remember, the mqcbs_per_second value fluctuates and might not reach 0, even when the queues have no depth or low CURDEPTH. description: Anomaly detected: Metric mqcpl_max_ent_us is lower than usual on MQ Coupling Facility
actions: {"If the MQCPL_MAX_ENT_US KPI is low, it indicates that the number and sizes of messages on shared queues have changed. This could be due to a change in application workload patterns or failed applications resulting in messages accumulating on queues. To address this issue, consider changing the size of the coupling facility structure. This KPI comes directly from the QESTMNUS field in the Coupling Facility section of SMF 115 subtype 2. The number of entries in use is shown in ENTSUSED in the command CSQM201I +CSQ1 CSQMDMSG DISPLAY CFSTATUS DETAILS CFSTATUS(APPLICATION1) TYPE(SUMMARY) CFTYPE(APPL) STATUS(ACTIVE) SIZEMAX(20224) SIZEUSED(31) ENTSMAX(2227) ENTSUSED(691) FAILTIME( ). When an out-of-syncpoint MQGET is performed, the message is moved to an uncommitted list header on the structure, and the message is added to the batch delete list. When an in-syncpoint MQGET is performed, the message is moved to the uncommitted list header; then, when a commit is issued, the message is deleted. A message takes up one structure entry and however many 256-byte elements are needed for the message plus a x'30'-byte header. situation_name: Metric non_persistent_pages is lower than usual on MQ Page Set
description: Anomaly detected: Metric non_persistent_pages is lower than usual on MQ Page Set
actions: {"If the non_persistent_pages in z/OS is low, it may indicate a potential issue with buffer pool management. This could lead to a situation where applications hang during MQI calls due to BDSC latch contention, and internal MQ processing and queue manager shutdown also hangs. This issue is caused by the deferred write processor (CSQP4DWP) marking a buffer as clean after updating a pageset, making it eligible for page stealing, and then attempting to check if the buffer needs to be added back on to the LRU chain while holding a latch on the lru chain. However, between the page being marked clean and CSQP4DWP obtaining the LRU latch, the readahead task CSQP1RAH stole the buffer and obtained the buffer latch, resulting in a deadlock. To resolve this issue, the queue manager should be restarted. If necessary, it may be required to cancel it. The problem is addressed in APAR PI41605, where CSQP4DWP is updated to prevent the pages it is processing from being eligible for stealing until after they have been added back to the LRU chain, thus preventing the deadlock situation. In summary, low non_persistent_pages in z/OS could indicate a buffer pool management issue leading to application hangs and internal MQ processing hangs. Restarting the queue manager, or in severe cases, canceling it, can help resolve this issue. The problem is resolved in APAR PI41605 by updating CSQP4DWP to prevent the deadlock situation."}

The logger checks periodically and can convert the wait for write waits into check writes, causing the records that are being waited for to be written to the WADS (write-ahead data set). This process enables the wait for writes to be resolved so that the callers can continue. To address this issue, you should focus on managing the IMS region's workload. This might involve optimizing the IMS region's configuration, such as adjusting the size of the log buffers or the frequency of checkpoints, to reduce the number of internal check writes. The WADS (write-ahead data set) is a data set used in the IMS (Information Management System) environment. Its primary role is to ensure data integrity and availability. When the IMS logger issues internal check writes due to wait for write (ILOG FUNC=WTWT) issues, it writes the records to the WADS instead of the OLDS (online log data set). This process, known as write-ahead logging, guarantees that the records are safely stored before the logger attempts to write them to the OLDS. If the write to the OLDS fails, the records are still available in the WADS, preventing data loss. Once the OLDS is successfully written to, the records are copied from the WADS to the OLDS. situation_name: Metric rel_brw_lock_req is lower than usual on MQ Queue Manager
description: Anomaly detected: Metric rel_brw_lock_req is lower than usual on MQ Queue Manager
actions: {"If the z/OS REL_BRW_LOCK_REQ is low, it indicates a change in MQ API call patterns. This KPI is extracted from the QISTMBLR field in the Data Manager section of SMF 115 subtype 2. A low REL_BRW_LOCK_REQ could suggest that the number of requests to release a browse lock (Release_Browse_Lock requests) has decreased. This could be due to applications not locking messages using the MQGMO_LOCK option on the MQGET call or not releasing the lock through MQGET with the option MQGMO_BROWSE_MSG_UNDER_CURSOR without MQGMO_LOCK, or not using MQGET with the option MQGMO_UNLOCK, or not using MQCLOSE on the handle. If you encounter a situation where the queue manager becomes unresponsive and cannot be connected to via the panels or the Admin tool over a svrconn channel, it might be due to a deadlock involving a latch. In such cases, you may see several threads, including the command server thread RTSSRV01, waiting for a latch. The deadlock might involve a BDSC Dlatch for Psid 00000006 Page 00003BE2. In rare cases, EOM processing can require one of the held latches, leading to it hanging until the system abnormally terminates the hung EOM task with abend S30D, resulting in abnormal queue manager termination. To resolve this issue, you can restart the queue manager. In some cases, it may be necessary to cancel the queue manager. If the problem persists, you may need to apply a fix for the APAR mentioned in the context, which addresses the issue of applications hanging during MQI calls due to BDSC latch contention. The fix updates CSQP4DWP to prevent the pages it is processing from being eligible for stealing until after they have been added back to the LRU chain, preventing the deadlock situation from occurring."}

actions: {"If the SCH_SMB_INT_CONFL is high, it indicates that there are numerous SMBs (Scheduler Message Blocks) that are not scheduled due to intent conflict. This conflict can be caused by an application using a processing option against a database that was listed in the DBPCB statement of the PSB and requesting a level of access that does not comply with existing access levels. For instance, if an application that is using a PSB tries to set a processing option of exclusive access against a database that is being updated, an intent conflict occurs. To resolve this issue, you can refer to the book titled 'z/OS Resource Measurement Facility Performance Management Guide' for practical, task-oriented approaches to resolving performance issues using RMF. This book covers common performance concepts for all MVS systems and provides guidelines and suggestions for improving performance in the sysplex. actions: {"If the z/OS TIMEOUT is high, it indicates that a unit of work was suspended for a time that exceeded the timeout value. To fix this, you should apply the following 9 PTFS and any pre-reqs or co-reqs: FMID Maintenance level HKCF730 UA83334 HKMC730 UA83330 HKMQ730 UA83394, UA83707, UA91741, UA92394 HKQI730 UA83372, UA94112, UA95011. Additionally, high GVUPWAIT counts and times in CICS Transaction Server for z/OS (CICS TS) might be caused by tasks that are browsing resources, such as files, terminals, functions where CICS domains browse the CICS catalog, RDO checking, and many other internal areas within CICS where it is desirable to give up control to allow other tasks an opportunity to run. A CICS domain issues a DFHDSATM FUNCTION(CHANGE_PRIORITY) which results in the DFHTASK 184 GVUPWAIT monitor field count and time being incremented. To determine the source of the GVUPWAIT, you can analyze the performance reports and look for tasks that are frequently browsing resources or causing the CICS domain to change priority."}

description: Anomaly detected: Metric total_active_user_transactions is higher than usual on CICS Region
actions: {"If the z/OS total_active_user_transactions is high, it could be due to various reasons. One possible cause is that various CICS domains need to periodically give up control to allow other tasks to run. Content: Networking on z/OS Previous topic | Next topic | Contents | Glossary | Contact z/OS | PDF Low-entry networking (LEN) nodes Networking on z/OS Low-entry networking nodes, also referred to as T nodes, were introduced in the mid-1980s to address the requirement for peer networking. The low-entry networking node was the first stage of the APPN evolution. The T node allows peer-to-peer connection and provides the physical and session-level connectivity required to support logical unit type (LU ). T nodes use protocols with reduced system definition requirements. For example, link station roles are negotiated as primary or secondary during the connection phase, instead of, as in the case of subarea networking, being predefined. Low-entry networking nodes do not implement a control point. With low-entry networking, you must predefine every partner resource (if it does not reside on this same node) along with the first hop (link) toward that resource (this is because neither searching nor topology exchanges are supported by low-entry networking nodes). This predefinition requirement is the primary drawback of low-entry networking nodes. Figure 1 illustrates a T skeleton network. The lines connecting the three nodes represent networking infrastructure like LAN, serial lines, or frame relay ATM. The T nodes are low-entry networking nodes without any APPN functionality. Figure 1. T peer connectivity In the T connection illustrated in Figure 1 , LU-LU sessions can be established between nodes A and B and nodes B and C. Because node B does not include a control point or any APPN functions, it cannot route sessions, and therefore node A and node C cannot establish LU- LU sessions. Prior to APPN, when only T nodes were implemented in SNA, transferring data from node A to node C required either a direct physical link between node A and node C or an application program in node B that relays messages between nodes A and C. Content: Networking on z/OS Previous topic | Next topic | Contents | Glossary | Contact z/OS | PDF Low-entry networking (LEN) nodes Networking on z/OS Low-entry networking nodes, also referred to as T nodes, were introduced in the mid-1980s to address the requirement for peer networking. The low-entry networking node was the first stage of the APPN evolution. The T node allows peer-to-peer connection and provides the physical and session-level connectivity required to support logical unit type (LU ). T nodes use protocols with reduced system definition requirements. For example, link station roles are negotiated as primary or secondary during the connection phase, instead of, as in the case of subarea networking, being predefined. Low-entry networking nodes do not implement a control point. With low-entry networking, you must predefine every partner resource (if it does not reside on this same node) along with the first hop (link) toward that resource (this is because neither searching nor topology exchanges are supported by low-entry networking nodes). This predefinition requirement is the primary drawback of low-entry networking nodes. Figure 1 illustrates a T skeleton network. The lines connecting the three nodes represent networking infrastructure like LAN, serial lines, or frame relay ATM. The T nodes are low-entry networking nodes without any APPN functionality. Figure 1. T peer connectivity In the T connection illustrated in Figure 1 , LU-LU sessions can be established between nodes A and B and nodes B and C. Because node B does not include a control point or any APPN functions, it cannot route sessions, and therefore node A and node C cannot establish LU- LU sessions. Prior to APPN, when only T nodes were implemented in SNA, transferring data from node A to node C required either a direct physical link between node A and node C or an application program in node B that relays messages between nodes A and C. This may include new applications, changes in transaction processing, or updates to database workloads. 2. Check zIIP availability: Ensure that there are sufficient zIIPs available to handle the workload. If zIIPs are overcommitted, consider allocating additional zIIPs to the system. 3. Monitor system performance: Use tools like SMF records, JES2 traces, and the interactive problem control system (IPCS) to collect problem data and locate any potential issues. 4. Adjust system settings: If necessary, adjust the MAXPROCUSER and MAXPROCSYS settings to optimize system performance. Keep the MAXPROCUSER value low and adjust PROCUSERMAX and MAXPROCSYS as needed. 5. Implement monitoring: Utilize a combination of console display output, SMF records, and REXX execs to monitor the system's settings and ensure they are properly tuned. Additionally, consider writing a REXX exec to issue procinfo() at a specified interval to find patterns of high watermark usage sorted by user ID. By following these steps, you can help ensure that the system's zIIPs are effectively utilized and that workloads are properly distributed, ultimately improving overall system performance."}
