situation_name: N3T_Appl_Backlog_Conns_Rejected
description: Application backlog connections rejected
actions: {"Application backlog connections rejected is the sum of the connections that the TCP/IP stack is rejecting because the connection backlog limit for the application has been exceeded. Acceptable levels can be determined in relation to service level requirements. Backlog connections rejected can affect application availability and lead to violations of service level agreements. This could be due to too many connections arriving or because the application stops accepting connections. Increasing the backlog limit and load balancing are possible solutions."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_Byte_Rate
description: Application throughput/byte rate per minute.
actions: {"The sum of the throughput rate for all connections to the application over the last sample interval, given in bytes per minute. Determine a threshold value by observing history to obtain a working baseline. Throughput significantly in excess of the established baseline indicates an increase in application workload and can signify an impending performance problem. Load balancing and work rescheduling are possible solutions."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_Connections_in_Backlog
description: Application connections in backlog
actions: {"The sum of the connections that are waiting to be accepted by the application. Determine a threshold value by observing history to obtain a working baseline. A number of connections in backlog significantly in excess of the established baseline indicates an increase in application workload and can signify an impending performance problem. Load balancing and work rescheduling are possible solutions."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_Datagram_Rate
description: Application datagram rate per minute.
actions: {"The sum of the datagram rate for all connections to the application over the last sample interval given in datagrams per minute. Determine a threshold value by observing history to obtain a working baseline. A datagram rate significantly in excess of the established baseline indicates an increase in application workload and can signify an impending performance problem. Load balancing (giving a higher priority to this application), application tuning, and work rescheduling are possible solutions."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_FTPD1_Rate
description: Example of a situation created for a particular application.
actions: {"This example situation demonstrates how to create a byte rate situation for a particular application, in this case, FTPD1. Application throughput in bytes per minute is the sum of the throughputs for all connections over the sample interval. To obtain a threshold for a particular application, determine a value by observing history. Samples much higher than the established baseline indicate an increase in application workload and can signify an impending performance problem."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_Not_Accepting_Conn
description: Application not accepting connections
actions: {"The idle time since the application last accepted a connection is greater than the defined time threshold, and there are connections in the backlog queue. The probable cause of the z/OS application being unable to complete its workload is a server application problem or a server system resource constraint. Use the z/OS Resource Measurement Facility to evaluate workload delay metrics (such as CPU or I/O) for the server address space to determine if possible system resource constraints exist."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_Pct_Datagrams_Discd
description: Application percent datagrams discarded
actions: {"The percentage of inbound datagrams discarded for all connections to the application over the last sample interval. Determine a threshold value by observing history to obtain a working baseline. A percentage of datagrams discarded much higher than the established baseline indicates an increase in application workload and might signify an impending performance problem. Removing the UDP queue limit, load balancing, and work rescheduling are possible solutions."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_Pct_OO_Segments
description: Application percent out-of-order segments
actions: {"The percentage of the segments received out of order for all connections to the application over the last sample interval. Only TCP segments can be received out of order. Acceptable levels can be determined in relation to service level requirements. Out-of-order segments can affect user response times and lead to violations of service level agreements. Check for congestion in the network, locate the source IP address of the sending application, and perform network diagnostic tests to solve this situation."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_Pct_Segs_Rexmit
description: Application percent segments retransmitted
actions: {"The percentage of the segment retransmissions for all connections to the application over the last sample interval. Only TCP transmissions can result in retransmissions. Acceptable levels can only be determined in relation to service level requirements. Retransmissions can affect user response times and lead to violations of service level agreements. Check for congestion in the network, locate the source IP address of the sending application, and perform network diagnostic tests to solve this situation."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_Reject_Conn
description: Application rejecting connections
actions: {"Requests for new connections are not satisfied by this application because the connection backlog limit has been exceeded. A server application workload spike or a server system resource constraint likely caused the z/OS application to be unable to complete the workload. Either increase the server application backlog queue limit, create an additional instance of the application server, or use the z/OS Resource Measurement Facility to evaluate workload delay."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_Reject_Conn_Resource
description: Application rejecting connections, possibly resource contraints
actions: {"Requests for new connections are not satisfied by this application because the connection backlog limit has been exceeded. The number of currently active connections is not a high percentage of the high water mark, indicating no spike in application workload. Constrained application system resources are likely causing the z/OS application to be unable to complete the workload. Increase the application backlog queue limit, or use z/OS Resource Measurement Facility to evaluate workload."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_Reject_Conn_WorkSpike
description: Application rejecting connections, possibly workload spike
actions: {"Requests for new connections are not satisfied by this application because the connection backlog limit has been exceeded. Also, the number of currently active connections is a high percentage of the high water mark for the number of currently active connections, indicating a spike in application workload. An application workload spike likely prevented the z/OS application from completing the workload. Increase the application backlog queue limit or create an additional instance of the application."}

situation_name: N3T_Appl_Retransmission_Count
description: Application retransmission count.
actions: {"The sum of the retransmissions for all connections to the application over the last sample interval. Only TCP transmissions can result in retransmissions. Acceptable levels can be determined in relation to service level requirements. Retransmissions can effect user response times and lead to violations of service level agreements. Check for congestion in the network, locate the source IP address of the sending application, and perform network diagnostic tests to solve this situation."}

situation_name: N3T_CPU_Pct_Critical
description: CPU percentage in use for TCPIP address space
actions: {"The percentage of CPU being used by TCP. High CPU usage is frequently accompanied by a high throughput rate. Determine if the throughput rate is excessive. Isolate the source of the high throughput by examining application throughput rates. Look for a high byte rate on a connection to isolate the sorce to individual connections. Applications can be load balanced across multiple OS images, connections can be terminated, work can be scheduled for non-peak hours, and capacity can be added."}

situation_name: N3T_CPU_Pct_Warning
description: CPU percentage in use for TCPIP address space.
actions: {"The percentage of CPU being used by TCP. High CPU usage is frequently accompanied by a high throughput rate. Determine if the throughput rate is excessive. Isolate the source of the high throughput by examining application throughput rates. Look for a high byte rate on a connection to isolate the sorce to individual connections. Applications can be load balanced across multiple OS images, connections can be terminated, work can be scheduled for non-peak hours, and capacity can be added."}

situation_name: N3T_CSA_Pct_Below_16MB
description: Percent of CSA in use by the TCPIP address space below 16MB.
actions: {"The percentage of CSA usage below 16 megabytes. The TCP/IP address space uses a nominal amount of CSA below the 16MB line. Determine a threshold value by observing history to obtain a working baseline. A percentage of CSA much higher than the established baseline indicates an increase in workload and might signify an impending performance problem. Use the diagnostic procedures outlined in the IBM IP Diagnosis Guide to take corrective action."}

situation_name: N3T_Conn_Backlog_Conns_Rejected
description: Backlog connections rejected
actions: {"The number of requests for new connections that were not connected by this listener because the connection backlog limit has been exceeded during the last sample interval. Acceptable levels can be determined in relation to service level requirements. Backlog connections rejected can effect application availability and lead to violations of service level agreements. Increasing server application backlog queue limits, load balancing, and work rescheduling are possible solutions."}

situation_name: N3T_Conn_Byte_Rate
description: Connection throughput/byte rate per minute.
actions: {"The average number of bytes per minute transmitted over this connection during the last sampling interval. The connection throughput rate is given in bytes per minute. Dividing the total current byte count for this interval by the sample interval size derives the rate. Normal or excessive rates can only be determined in relation to established baselines and service level requirements."}

situation_name: N3T_Conn_Connections_in_Backlog
description: Connection in backlog
actions: {"The total number of connections that are waiting to be accepted by the application. What is judged normal or excessive can only be determined in relation to established baselines and service level requirements. Load balancing and work rescheduling are possible solutions."}

situation_name: N3T_Conn_Current_Retransmits
description: Connection retransmission count.
actions: {"The total number of retransmitted segments for the current interval. Retransmissions occur when a TCP segment is sent but is not acknowledged by the receiving host within a specified timeout period. Possible causes of timeouts are hardware errors and congested servers."}

situation_name: N3T_Conn_Datagram_Rate
description: Connection datagram rate per minute.
actions: {"The average number of datagrams, per minute, transmitted over this connection during the last sampling interval. This is given in datagrams per minute and is derived by dividing total datagrams for the sampling interval by the size of the interval derives the rate. A normal or excessive rate can only be determined in relation to established baselines and service level requirements."}

situation_name: N3T_Conn_Pct_Datagrams_Discd
description: Connection percent datagrams discarded
actions: {"The percentage of datagrams discarded compared to the number of datagrams received during the last sample interval. Inbound datagrams are discarded because queue limits were exceeded. Removing UDP queue limits, load balancing, and work rescheduling are possible solutions."}

situation_name: N3T_Conn_Pct_OO_Segments
description: Connection percent out-of-order segments
actions: {"The percentage of segments received out of order compared to the number of segments received during the last sample interval. Only TCP segments can be received out of order. Acceptable levels can be determined in relation to service level requirements. Out-of-order segments can affect user response times and lead to violations of service level agreements. Check for congestion in the network and perform network diagnostic tests to solve this situation."}

situation_name: N3T_Conn_Pct_Segs_Rexmit
description: Connection percent segments retransmitted
actions: {"The percentage of the segment retransmissions compared to the number of segments sent during the last sample interval. Retransmissions occur when a TCP segment is sent but is not acknowledged by the receiving host within a specified time out period. Possible causes of timeouts are hardware errors and congested servers."}

situation_name: N3T_Conn_Rnd_Trip_Time
description: Connection round trip time
actions: {"The response time for the last TCP segment transmitted on the connection. It is the elapsed time, in tenths of a second, starting when the segment was sent and ending when the acknowledgment was received. Round trip time is not end-to-end response time since it does not account for application time. However in conjunction with the round trip variance, it is a good indication of the general health of the route."}

situation_name: N3T_Conn_Rnd_Trip_Variance
description: Connection round trip time statistical variance
actions: {"The statistical variance of round trip times since the connection was established. Round trip variance helps to determine the accuracy of the reported round trip time value. A small variance suggests accuracy of the current round trip time as an average. A high variance suggests that the current round trip time might not represent the average. A normal variance can be determined by baselines and service level requirements. Check for congestion in the network and perform network diagnostic tests."}

situation_name: N3T_Connection_Count
description: TCPIP connection count
actions: {"The total number of TCP connections, TCP listeners, and UDP endpoints at the end of the last sampling interval. This includes connections that are in an established or a listening state. Determine a value for connection count by observing history to obtain a working baseline. A count significantly in excess of the established baseline indicates a change in network workload and can signify an impending performance problem. Load balancing is a possible solution."}

situation_name: N3T_IPSec_IKE_Act_Fail
description: Internet Key Exchange (IKE) tunnel activations have failed.
actions: {"Evaluate the IKE daemon logs to understand the nature of the failures.Failures couldbe due to either a configuration mismatch where one of the peers is rejectingthe other peer's proposals or a network problem such as retransmissions.","Refer to the z/OS CommunicationServer: IP Diagnosis manual foradditional information.","This warning situation uses the CHANGE function and the Total Failed IKETunnel Activations attribute to determine if any IKE tunnel activations havefailed since the situation was last evaluated. An attribute is not highlighted when the CHANGE function is used, and the Current Situation Value Table may not display data.","By default, this situation is evaluatedevery 15minutes and is not run at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_IPSec_Key_Msgs_Auth_Fail
description: Authentication failures have occurred during the negotiation of Internet Key Exchange (IKE) tunnels.
actions: {"This condition can occur when using shared keys if the shared keys on thepeers do not match.Otherwise, this problem is likely an indication of networkdata corruption.","This warning situation uses the CHANGE function and the IKE Total Key Message Authentication Failuresattribute to determine if the total number of IKE key message authentication failures has increased since the situation was last evaluated. An attribute is not highlighted when the CHANGE function is used, and the Current Situation Value Table may not display data.","Bydefault, this situation is evaluated every 15 minutes and is not run at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_IPSec_Key_Msgs_Invalid
description: Invalid key exchange messages have been received from the remote security endpoint.
actions: {"This condition can occur either because of an Internet Security Associationand Key Management Protocol (ISAKMP) error (check the service levels on bothpeers) or, when using shared keys, if the shared keys on the peers do not match.","This warning situation uses the CHANGE function and the IKE Total Invalid Key Messages attribute to determine if the total number of invalid key messages has increased since the situation was last evaluated. An attribute is not highlighted when the CHANGE function is used, and the Current Situation Value Table may not display data.","By default, this situation is evaluated every 15 minutes and is not run at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_IPSec_Key_Msgs_Replayed
description: Key exchange messages used to negotiate Internet Key Exchange (IKE) tunnels have been replayed by the remote security endpoint.
actions: {"This situation is an indication of a networking problem or a configuration mismatch problem. Evaluate the UNIX syslog and identify the reason for the IKE daemon dropping messages.","This warning situation uses the CHANGE function and the IKE Total ReplayedKey Messages attribute to determine if the total number of replayed key messageswas more than five for three consecutive evaluations for the situation. During IKE tunnel negotiation theIKE daemon replays 10 messages before declaring a failed activation attempt.Key messages will be replayed periodically for an activation attempt. Thefive replayed messages in a sample interval may or may not be for the same activationattempt. An attribute is not highlighted when the CHANGE function is used, and the Current Situation Value Table may not display data.","By default, this situation is evaluated every 15 minutes and is not run at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_IPSec_Key_Msgs_Rtrnsmttd
description: Key exchange messages used to negotiate Internet Key Exchange (IKE) tunnels have been retransmitted by the local security endpoint.
actions: {"This situation is an indication of a networking problem or a configurationmismatch problem. Evaluate the UNIX syslog and identify the reason for the IKE daemondropping messages.","This warning situation uses theCHANGE function and the IKE Total RetransmittedKey Messages attribute to determine if the total number of retransmitted keymessages was more than five for three consecutive evaluations for the situation. During IKE tunnelnegotiation the IKE daemon retransmits 10 messages before declaring a failedactivation attempt. Key messages will be retransmitted periodically for anactivation attempt. The five retransmitted messages mayor may not be for the same activation attempt. An attribute is not highlighted when the CHANGE function is used, and the Current Situation Value Table may not display data.","By default, this situation is evaluated every 15 minutes and is not run at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_IPSec_Pkts_Denied_DENY
description: The number of packets being denied by the DENY action associated with one or more filters may be high.
actions: {"This situation could indicate attempted suspicious activity.Enable loggingfor the filters with DENY actions and monitor the traffic using the UNIX syslog.","This warning situation is based on the Percent Packets Denied by DENY attribute. By default, this situation is evaluated every 15 minutes andis not run at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_IPSec_Pkts_Denied_Mismatch
description: The number of packets being denied due to a mismatch with the filter'saction may be high.
actions: {"First identify which filters are causing the mismatch alert. This problem could indicate a policy mismatch between the peer and this TCP/IP stack. Anotherpossibility is attempted suspicious activity.Enable logging for the associated filter rule and monitor the traffic using the UNIXsyslog.","This warning situation is based on the Packets Denied by Mismatch attribute.By default, this situation is evaluated every 15 minutes and is not run atstartup."}

situation_name: N3T_IPSec_QUICKMODE_Invalid
description: Invalid QUICKMODE messages have been received from the remote security endpoint.
actions: {"This situation indicates an Internet Security Association and Key ManagementProtocol ( ISAKMP)error.Check the service levels on both peers.","This warning situation uses the CHANGE function and the Total Invalid QUICKMODE Messages attribute to determine if the total number of invalid QUICKMODE messages received (from the remote security endpoint) has increased since the situation was last evaluated. An attribute is not highlighted when the CHANGE function is used, and the Current Situation Value Table may not display data.","By default, this situation is evaluated every 15 minutes and is not run at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_IPSec_QUICKMODE_Replayed
description: QUICKMODE messages used to negotiate dynamic IP tunnels have been replayedby the remote security endpoint.
actions: {"This situation indicates a networking problem or a configuration mismatch problem.Evaluate the UNIX syslog and identify the reason for the Internet Key Exchange (IKE) daemon dropping messages.","This warning situation uses theCHANGE function and the Total ReplayedQUICKMODE Messages attribute to determine if the total number of replayedQUICKMODE messages was more than five for three consecutive evaluations for the situation. Duringdynamic tunnel negotiation the IKE daemon replays 10 messages before declaringa failed activation attempt. QUICKMODE messages will be replayed periodicallyfor an activation attempt. The five replayed messages mayor may not be for the same activation attempt. An attribute is not highlighted when the CHANGE function is used, and the Current Situation Value Table may not display data.","By default, this situation is evaluated every 15 minutes and is not run at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_IPSec_QUICKMODE_Rtrnsmttd
description: QUICKMODE messages used to negotiate dynamic IP tunnels have been retransmitted by the local security endpoint.
actions: {"This situation indicates a networking problem or a configurationmismatch problem. Evaluate the UNIX syslog and identify the reason for the Internet Key Exchange (IKE) daemondropping messages.","This warning situation uses theCHANGE function and the Total RetransmittedQUICKMODE Messages attribute to determine if the total number of retransmittedQUICKMODE messages was more than five for three consecutive evaluations for the situation. Duringdynamic tunnel negotiation the IKE daemon retransmits 10 messages before declaringa failed activation attempt. QUICKMODE messages will be retransmitted periodicallyfor an activation attempt. The five retransmitted messages may or may not be for the same activation attempt. An attribute is not highlighted when the CHANGE function is used, and the Current Situation Value Table may not display data.","By default, this situation is evaluated every 15 minutes and is not run at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_IP_Input_Discard_Pct
description: NULL
actions: {"Input Discard Percentage is the percentage of IP segments that this TCP/IP address space received from the network that were undeliverable and discarded during the most recent sampling interval. Input discards are datagrams that were discarded, includingno route found errors, unknown or unsupported protocol errors,truncation errors, invalid address errors,and reassembly failures.","Excessive discards waste network resources. Analyze the errors reportedin the IP Statistics, Interfaces, and OSA workspaces to further isolate the source of the problem.","A trace might be needed to determine the source of the discards. Discard reason codes (found in IBM z/OS Communications Server: IP and SNA Codes) may be used to filter the trace data to show only the packets pertaining to issues discovered in the IP statistics and interface investigation.When the offending interface or application or both have been identified, see the IBM z/OS Communications Server: IP Diagnosis Guide to take corrective action."}

situation_name: N3T_IP_Out_Disc
description: IP output discarded.
actions: {"The total number of IP output datagrams that were discarded since the TCPIP stack was initialized. Output discards are datagrams that were discarded, though no problem was encountered to prevent them from being sent to their destination. Often this is an indication that more buffer space needs to be allocated for the interface."}

situation_name: N3T_IP_Output_Discard_Pct
description: NULL
actions: {"Output Discard Percentage is the percentage of IP segments that this TCP/IP address space sent to the network that were undeliverable and discarded during the most recent sampling interval. Output discards are datagrams that were discarded,including no route found errors and fragmentation failures.","Often this is an indication that more buffer space must be allocated for the interface. Excessive discards waste network resources. Analyze the errors reported in the IP Statistics, Interfaces, and OSA workspaces to further isolate the source of the problem.","A trace might be required to isolate the source of the discards. Discard reason codes (found in IBM z/OS Communications Server: IP and SNA Codes) may be usedto filter the trace data to only show packets pertaining to issues discovered in theIP statistics and interface investigation. When the offending interface or application or both has been identified, see the IBM z/OS Communications Server: IP Diagnosis Guide to take corrective action."}

situation_name: N3T_Input_Discard_Pct
description: TCPIP input discard percentage.
actions: {"This is based on the total number of IP input segments that were undeliverable and discarded, divided by the total IP segments received since the TCPIP stack was initialized. Segments can be discarded due to hardware errors, addressing errors, unknown protocols, and other errors. Excessive discards waste network resources. A trace might be needed to isolate the source of the discards. Refer to the IBM z/OS Communications Server: IP Diagnosis Guide."}

situation_name: N3T_Interface_Bandwidth_Util
description: NULL
actions: {"Bandwidth utilization is the total percentage of capacity beingused. This is the rate at which data is sent or received on this interfaceover the last collection interval, divided by the current bandwidthof the interface.","Determine a conditional value by observinghistory to obtain a working baseline. High utilization over an extendedperiod of time could indicate that the interface is operating overcapacity. To solve this problem, add an additional interface or upgradeto a higher speed interface.","This is a warning situation."}

situation_name: N3T_Interface_Xmit_Rcv_Bytes
description: NULL
actions: {"The total amount of traffic across an interface is representedby the number of input bytes plus the number of output bytes sincethe statistics were last reset.","Normal, excessive or insufficientrates can only be determined in relation to established baselinesand service level requirements. Throughput significantly in excessof the established baseline indicates a change in network workloadand can signify an impending performance problem. Load balancing isa possible solution. The probable cause of low or no throughput isnetwork congestion or configuration error.","This is a warning situation."}

situation_name: N3T_OSA2_Missed_Packets
description: The number of missed packets was greater than zero (0) for four consecutive 15-minute collection intervals.
actions: {"Missed packets over consecutive collection intervals is an indication that too little buffer space is available on the OSA card. Recommended remediation is to add an additional OSA-Express2 10 Gigabit port.","This warning situationis based on the Missed Packets attribute. By default, this situation is runevery 15 minutes and is not set to run automatically at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_OSA2_Not_Stored_Frames
description: The number of not stored frames has been greater than zero (0) for four consecutive 15-minute collection intervals.
actions: {"Failing to have descriptor buffers available to store frames over consecutive collection intervals is an indication that the LAN is running near or at 100% utilization. Recommended remediation is to add an additional OSA-Express2 10 Gigabit port.","This warning situation is based on the Not Stored Frames Receivedattribute. By default, this situation is run every 15 minutes and is not setto run automatically at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_OSA3_Missed_Packets
description: The number of missed packets was greater than zero (0) for four consecutive 15-minute collection intervals.
actions: {"Missed packets over consecutive collection intervals is an indication that too little buffer space is available on the OSA card. Recommended remediation is to add an additional OSA-Express3 port of the same subtype.If you are running an OSA-Express3 Gigabit adapter, consider upgrading to OSA-Express3 10 Gigabit.","This warning situationis based on the Missed Packets attribute. By default, this situation is runevery 15 minutes and is not set to run automatically at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_OSA3_Not_Stored_Frames
description: The number of not stored frames has been greater than zero (0) for four consecutive 15-minute collection intervals.
actions: {"Failing to have descriptor buffers available to store frames over consecutive collection intervals is an indication that the LAN is running near or at 100% utilization. Recommended remediation is to add an additional OSA-Express3 port of the same subtype.If you are running an OSA-Express3 Gigabit adapter, consider upgrading to OSA-Express3 10 Gigabit.","This warning situation is based on the Not Stored Frames Receivedattribute. By default, this situation is run every 15 minutes and is not setto run automatically at startup."}

situation_name: N3T_OSA_Chan_PCI_Busy_Pct_5Min
description: OSA channel PCI busy percent over a 5 minute interval.
actions: {"The OSA channel PCI bus utilization has exceeded the threshold for a 5 minute interval. If this condition persists and performance has been degraded it might be necessary to increase channel capacity."}

situation_name: N3T_OSA_Chan_Pro_Util_Pct_5Min
description: OSA channel processor utilization percent over 5 minutes
actions: {"The OSA channel processor utilization has exceeded the threshold for a 5 minute interval. If performance is degraded, it might be necessary to expand capacity."}

situation_name: N3T_OSA_Utilization
description: OSA Adapter with high utilization
actions: {"Both the PCI bus utilization (per minute) and processor utilization (per hour) for the OSA adapter indicate a high percentage of use. The probable cause of the OSA adapter under performing is high adapter utilization rates. Confirm that the PathMTUDiscovery option is enabled and that network devices along routing paths are capable of exploiting a larger MTU size. Then increase the MTU Size parameter in the TCP/IP Profile, and add an additional OSA adapter."}

situation_name: N3T_Output_Discard_Pct
description: TCPIP ouput discard percentage.
actions: {"This is the total number of IP output datagrams discarded, divided by the total number of IP output datagrams. Output discards are datagrams that were discarded, though no problem was encountered to prevent them from being sent to their destination. Often this is an indication that more buffer space needs to be allocated for the interface."}

situation_name: N3T_Paging_Rate
description: Paging rate
actions: {"Paging by the TCPIP address space is generally moderate. Determine a threshold value by observing history to obtain a working baseline. A paging rate much higher than the established baseline indicates an increase in workload and might signify an impending performance problem. Use the diagnostic procedures outlined in the IBM IP Diagnosis Guide and take corrective action."}

situation_name: N3T_Pct_Auth_Pvt_Allocated_Stg
description: Percent authorized private allocated storage.
actions: {"The percentage of authorized private storage that is currently allocated compared to the maximum authorized private storage that is allowed. Determine a threshold value by observing history to obtain a working baseline. A percentage significantly larger than the established baseline shows an increase in workload and possibly an impending performance problem. Increasing maximum authorized private subpool storage allowed, load balancing, and work rescheduling are possible solutions."}

situation_name: N3T_Pct_ECSA_Allocated_Stg
description: Percent ECSA allocated storage
actions: {"The percentage of ECSA storage that is currently allocated compared to the maximum ECSA storage that is allowed. Determine a threshold value by observing history to obtain a working baseline. A percentage of ECSA allocated storage significantly in excess of the established baseline indicates an increase in workload and possibly an impending performance problem. Increasing the maximum ECSA storage allowed, load balancing, and work rescheduling are possible solutions."}

situation_name: N3T_Pct_IF_Err
description: Interface percent packets in error.
actions: {"The total number of inbound and outbound packets that contained errors, divided by the total number of IP packets from the last sampling period. Interface errors often indicate problems with the hardware or the line itself."}

situation_name: N3T_Pct_IF_In_Err
description: Interface percent inbound packets in error.
actions: {"The total number of inbound packets that contained errors preventing them from being delivered to a higher layer protocol, divided by the total number of inbound IP packets. Interface errors often indicate problems with the hardware or the line itself."}

situation_name: N3T_Pct_IF_Out_Err
description: Interface percent outbound packets in error.
actions: {"The total number of outbound packets that contained errors preventing them from being sent to their destination, divided by the total number of outbound IP packets from the last sampling period. Interface errors often indicate problems with the hardware or the line itself."}

situation_name: N3T_Pct_IF_Pkt_Disc
description: Interface percent packets discarded.
actions: {"The number of inbound and outbound packets that were discarded (though no errors had been detected) to prevent them from continuing to be processed, divided by the total number of packets from the last sampling period.One possible reason for discarding a packet could be to free up buffer space."}

situation_name: N3T_Pct_IP_In_Disc
description: Percent IP input discarded
actions: {"The total number of IP input datagrams that were discarded since the TCPIP stack was initialized. This means that the TCP/IP stack is runing out of memory in internal buffers. Input discards are datagrams that were discarded, though no problem was encountered to prevent them from being processed. Often this is an indication that more buffer space needs to be allocated for the interface."}

situation_name: N3T_Pct_TCP_OO_Segs
description: TCP percent out-of-order segments
actions: {"The number of inbound TCP data segments that did not contain the next expected sequence number (for example, out-of-order), divided by the total number of inbound segments from the last sampling period. This is often due to network congestion or possibly multiple routes defined to a destination host."}

situation_name: N3T_Reassembly_Failure_Pct
description: Reassembly failure percentage.
actions: {"The total number of reassemblies that fail, divided by the total number of reassemblies attempted. Reassemblies fail because some of the fragments required for reassembly of a message were not received. Required segments are being lost in transit and not received by the host. Excessive reassembly failures indicate a problem somewhere in the network. See the IBM IP Diagnosis Guide for assistance in isolating the cause of the problem."}

situation_name: N3T_Reassembly_Pct
description: Reassembly percentage.
actions: {"The total number of IP segments received requiring reassembly, divided by the total number of IP segments received. Messages can become fragmented when transmitted across a network. Message fragments must be reassembled before delivery to an application. Excessive reassembly wastes network resources and degrades network performance. See the IBM IP Diagnosis Guide for help in isolating the cause of the reassemblies and take corrective action."}

situation_name: N3T_Retransmission_Pct
description: Retransmission percentage.
actions: {"The total number of TCP segments retransmitted, divided by the total number of TCP segments sent. TCP segments are retransmitted when their receipt is not acknowledged by the destination host. Excessive retransmissions waste network resources, degrade network performance, and effect user response times. See the IBM IP Diagnosis Guide for assistance in isolating the cause of the retransmissions and take corrective action."}

situation_name: N3T_SSH_Version_Critical
description: The protocol version being used for the specified SSH session is outdated.Information shared in the specified session may not be secure.
actions: {"Update the SSH protocol used for the specified session to version 2 or later."}

situation_name: N3T_Sample_NetViewAuto_Cmd
description: Example of how to run a Tivoli NetView for z/OS command.
actions: {"This is a sample situation and is not intended to be used as is.The formula will always evaluate to True if the situation is started.The System Command field under the Action tab in the Situation Editor specifies a MVS MODIFY command for the NetView for z/OS procedure.","The situation provides an example of how to run a NetView for z/OS command when the situation fires.You will need to replace NetViewProcName in the System Command field with the name of the started procedure for the NetView program in your environment.The exec invoked, KN3SITEX, is provided. It expects the situation name followed by attributeName attributeValue pairs as input.","Note that MVS console commands are limited to 126 characters.","Refer to the IBM Z OMEGAMON Network Monitor: User's Guide for more information on how to trigger NetView automation from situations."}

situation_name: N3T_Sample_NetViewAuto_Msg
description: Example of how to send a message for automation by Tivoli NetView for z/OS.
actions: {"This is a sample situation and is not intended to be used as is. The formula will always evaluate to True if the situation is started. The System Command field under the Action tab in the Situation Editor specifies a MVS SEND command.","The situation provides an example of how to generate a message that can be recognized by the Tivoli NetView for z/OS automation table in order to perform an action when the situation triggers. The message generated by this situation matches the input requirements for sample REXX exec, KN3SITEX, is provided.A sample NetView automation table entry (KN3AUMSG) is also provided.","Note that MVS console commands are limited to 126 characters.","Refer to the IBM Z OMEGAMON Network Monitor User's Guide for more informationon how to trigger NetView automation from situations."}

situation_name: N3T_TCP_App_Conn_Flood_Warning
description: A TCP/IP application encountered a potential connection flooding attack.
actions: {"Check the TCP Applications workspace to determine the jobname of the server for which the Connection Flood condition occurred.","Check the TCP Listener workspace to determine the port for the server that was involved in the Connection Flood condition."}

situation_name: N3T_TCP_Conn_Drop
description: TCP connections dropped
actions: {"A number of connections for a TCPIP stack were dropped due to one or more of the following errors: Retransmit_dropped, Probe_dropped, Alive_dropped, Tcp_wait_drops. This situation occurs when the number of connections dropped, due to error conditions, is greater than zero (0) for three consecutive intervals. The TCPIP dropped connections value is a stack aggregate metric collected for each TCP/IP stack instance. Connections likely dropped due to network congestion or lost connectivity to the endpoint node."}

situation_name: N3T_TCP_Flow_Controls
description: NULL
actions: {"Flow Control is the sum of input window probes, input window updates, output window probes, and output window updates since TCP/IPinitialization.","This situation occurs when the reading application is having trouble keeping up with the sending application.In most cases this is not a problem, but is instead normal behavior.TCP has built-in self-correcting logic to address this type of situation. When the receiving application cannot keep up, TCP on the receiving side alerts TCP on the sending side to slow down the amount of data being sent.","However, if a flow control issue is instead a side effect of anapplication problem such as the application being hung, look for additional alerts that might have been triggered, indicating an application issue.","This is an informational situation."}

situation_name: N3T_TCP_In_Errs
description: TCP received segment errors
actions: {"The total number of segments received in error (for example, bad TCP checksums)."}

situation_name: N3T_TCP_List_Conn_Flood_Warning
description: A TCP/IP application encountered a potential connection flooding attack.
actions: {"Check the TCP Applications workspace to determine the jobname of the server for which the Connection Flood condition occurred.","Check the TCP Listener workspace to determine the port for the server that was involved in the Connection Flood condition."}

situation_name: N3T_TCP_Probes
description: TCP window probes sent
actions: {"The number of outbound keepalive window probe requests sent during the last sampling period. A number greater than 0 (zero) could indicate that a number of TCP connections were dropped during the last sampling interval because no response was returned while sending window probe requests. This might indicate a problem with connectivity to the remote application."}

situation_name: N3T_TLS_Version_Critical
description: The protocol version being used for the specified TLS session is outdated.Information shared in the specified session may not be secure.
actions: {"If using TLS, update the TLS protocol used for the specified session to version 1.2 or later.","If using SSL, update the specified session to instead use TLS at version 1.2 or later."}

situation_name: N3T_TN3270_Avg_IP_Resp_Time
description: The average IP response time measured over the last response time collection interval
actions: {"Average IP response time measured over the last response time collection interval. Response time collection interval is specified on the AvgSampPeriod parameter of MONITORGROUP statement in the TCP/IP profile dataset. The probable cause of a high average IP response time is network congestion. Possible procedures to isolate and correct the problem include the following:","This situation is triggered when the average total response timeis greater than 1.0 seconds.","As provided, this situation is not started automatically.","Note: Applicable only when monitoring TN3270 servers running on z/OS v1.8 and higher."}

situation_name: N3T_TN3270_Avg_SNA_Resp_Time
description: The average SNA response time measured over the last response time collection interval
actions: {"Average SNA response time measured over the last response time collection interval. Response time collection interval is specified on the AvgSampPeriod parameter of MONITORGROUP statement in the TCP/IP profile dataset. The SNA response time is calculated by subtracting the Average IP Response Time from the Average Total Response time.","The most likely causes ofa high average SNA response time are an application workload spike or z/OSsystem resource constraints.","To further investigate system resource constraints, use the z/OSResource Measurement Facility to evaluate workload delay metrics such as CPUand I/O for both the application and z/OS Communications Server address spaceto determine if possible system resource constraints exist.","This situationis triggered when the average total response time is greater than .5 seconds.","As provided, this situation is not started automatically.","Note: Applicable only when monitoring TN3270 servers running on z/OS v1.8 and higher."}

situation_name: N3T_TN3270_Avg_Tot_Resp_Time
description: The average total response time measured over the last response time collection interval
actions: {"Average total response time measured over the last response time collection interval. Response time collection interval is specified on the AvgSampPeriod parameter of MONITORGROUP statement in the TCP/IP profile dataset. The average total response time is comprised of both the SNA portion and the IP portion of the TN3270 session. The value is a good indication of the general health of the end-to-end route. By examining the IP (average IP response Time) and SNA (average SNA response time) components of the connection, youcan determine which component is contributing to the largest percent of the end to end response time.","This situation is triggered when the average total response time is greater than 1.5 seconds.","As provided, this situation is not started automatically.","Note: Applicable only when monitoring TN3270 servers running on z/OS v1.8 and higher."}

situation_name: N3T_TN3270_Bckt5_Resp_Time_Pct
description: Percentage of response times counted in the highest bucket exceeds 10 percent
actions: {"The percentage of response times falling into the highest response time bucket exceeds 10 percent. A high number of response times falling into Bucket 5 provides a general indication of whether the health of the end-to-end route is being degraded. Evaluate the Average Total Response Time (and its IP and SNA response time components) to isolate the cause of the degradation in response time.","This situation is triggered when the Bucket 5 Response Time Percent is greater than or equal to 10 percent.","As provided, this situation is not started automatically.","Note: Applicable only when monitoring TN3270 servers running on z/OS v1.8 and higher."}

situation_name: N3T_Telnet_Pool_Usage_Critical
description: Percentage of TELNET pool in use.
actions: {"The TELNET pool usage that has met or exceeded a critical threshold. One entry from the TELNET pool is assigned for each TELNET session request. When the pool is exhausted, no more TELNET sessions can be established. SNA over TELNET can quickly exhaust an inadequately sized TELNET pool. Allocating a large TELNET pool has very little cost and is recommended. TELNET pool size is specified in the TCPIP profile."}

situation_name: N3T_Telnet_Pool_Usage_Warning
description: Percentage of TELNET pool in use.
actions: {"The TELNET pool usage has met or exceeded a warning threshold. One entry from the TELNET pool is assigned for each TELNET session request. When the pool is exhausted, no more TELNET sessions can be established. SNA over TELNET can quickly exhaust an inadequately sized pool. Allocating a large TELNET pool has very little cost and is recommended. TELNET pool size is specified in the TCPIP profile."}

situation_name: N3T_Throughput_Rate
description: Throughput/byte rate per minute.
actions: {"The sum of throughput rates for all connections to the TCP/IP stack over the last sample interval in bytes per minute. The throughput value for your network can be determined by observing history to obtain a working baseline. Throughput significantly in excess of the established baseline indicates a change in network workload and can signify an impending performance problem. Load balancing is a possible solution."}

situation_name: N3T_Total_CSA_Pct
description: Total CSA percentage in use by TCPIP address space.
actions: {"The CSA above and below the 16MB line. CSA usage is generally moderate and reasonable. If CSA usage becomes excessive, isolate the cause of the problem using diagnostic procedures outlined in the IBM IP Diagnosis Guide."}

situation_name: N3T_UDP_Discard_Pct
description: UDP discard percentage.
actions: {"The total number of UDP datagrams received that were undeliverable, divided by the total number of UPD datagrams received. Most datagrams are discarded because the port number specified in the datagram cannot be associated with an active application on the receiving host. Excessive UDP discards can degrade network performance or indicate that a necessary application is not available. See the IBM IP Diagnosis Guide for help in isolating the cause of the discards."}

situation_name: N3V_BuffPool_Buf_Avail
description: Total number of buffers available
actions: {"The buffers available in the VTAM buffer pool are allocated as required.VTAM determines the condition of the buffer pool based on the Expansion ThresholdFlag. This flag indicates whether the Buffers Available is less than or equalto the Expansion Threshold. If the Buffers Available is less than or equalto the Expansion Threshold, then this situation triggered.","Monitor the total number of buffers over time.If this number continues to increase over time, then allocate additional base buffers.","This is aninformational situation. By default, this situation does not start automaticallyand should be run as needed, not at startup."}

situation_name: N3V_BuffPool_Buf_Expan_Lim_Pct
description: Percentage of total number of I/O buffers compared to expansion limit (IO buffer pool only)
actions: {"The I/O buffer pool manages the storage of all network input/output messagessent from application programs and across channel connections. All networktraffic passes through this pool, regardless of its destination. This bufferpool also contains channel programs used to service locally attached devices.","The maximum number of I/O buffers allowed is calculated by VTAM fromthe Expansion Limit value specified in IOBUF statement in the VTAM start options(for example, SYS1.VTAMLST(ATCSTRxx)).","When calculating this limit, VTAMtakes into account how many buffers fit on a page. If XPANLIM is not specifiedin buffer definition or is coded 0, buffer expansion is not limited and avalue of 2,147,483,647 is displayed in the field.","This situation istriggered when Expansion Limit is greater than 90% of its capacity. To address this situation, increase the Expansion Limit value.","This is a critical situation. By default, this situation starts automatically. It should be runat startup.","Note: Applies to the I/O buffer pool only."}

situation_name: N3V_BuffPool_Queue_Req
description: Number of queued requests
actions: {"VTAM honors requests for storage dynamically, as permitted by buffer availability. If buffers are not available, VTAM queues the requests until enoughstorage can be obtained to honor the user request. This situation is triggeredwhen the number of queued requests becomes greater than zero.","If you see this situation occurring over time for a particular pool, then allocate additional base buffers or increase the Expansion Point value. If the situation occurs for an I/O buffer pool, then also consider increasing the Slowpoint value.","This isa warning situation. By default, this situation does not start automaticallyand should be run as needed, not at startup."}

situation_name: N3V_CPU_Pct_Critical
description: CPU percentage in use for VTAM address space.
actions: {"The percentage of CPU being used by VTAM. High CPU usage is frequently accompanied by a high throughput rate. If the throughput rate is excessive, isolate the source of the high throughput using diagnostic techniques outlined in the SNA Network Implementation Guide and take corrective action."}

situation_name: N3V_CPU_Pct_Warning
description: CPU percentage in use for VTAM address space.
actions: {"The percentage of CPU being used by VTAM. High CPU usage is frequently accompanied by a high throughput rate. If the throughput rate is excessive, isolate the source of the high throughput using diagnostic techniques outlined in the SNA Network Implementation Guide and take corrective action."}

situation_name: N3V_CSA_Pct_Below_16MB
description: Percent of CSA in use by the VTAM address space below 16MB
actions: {"The percentage of CSA usage below 16 megabytes. The VTAM address space uses a nominal amount of CSA below the 16MB line. Common storage areas are used by VTAM and other resources in your network to maintain buffers and control blocks in the CSA for MVS systems. For performance reasons, VTAM offers you some control over its use of common storage areas with the start options. Isolate the cause of the problem using diagnostic procedures outlined in the IBM z/OS Communications Server: SNA Network Implementation Guide."}

situation_name: N3V_EE_Pct_Packets_Rexmit
description: EE percent packets retransmitted.
actions: {"The percentage of the HPR network layer packets retransmitted compared to the number of packets sent over this EE connection during the last sample interval. Retransmissions occur when a HPR packet is sent but is not acknowledged by the receiving host within a specified timeout period. Some possible causes of timeouts are hardware errors and congested servers."}

situation_name: N3V_HPR_Conn_OOS_Buffers
description: HPR RTP Connection with high number of out-of-sequence buffers
actions: {"A high number of out-of-sequence buffers indicates high CPU utilization of the remote z/OS Communications Server address space. This is probably due to network congestion or constrained CPU in the remote z/OS Communications Server address space. To solve, validate the router configuration parameters, confirm that CPU utilization is high for the remote system z/OS Communications Server address space, and redistribute the z/OS Communications Server workload on the HPR RTP connected remote system."}

situation_name: N3V_HPR_Conn_Path_Switch
description: HPR RTP connection with path switch due to error
actions: {"A number of path switches have one or more of the following path switch triggers:","Note: By default, this situation only tests for No NCB.","This situation is probably triggered by losingconnectivity to the remote endpoint or constrained CPU in the remote z/OSCommunications server address space.","To determine this, the followingmetrics in the HPR connections table are used:","This situation occurs when the path switches value is greater thanzero for 3 consecutive intervals and the path switch trigger value is oneof the following in the third interval:","This is probably because of lost connectivity to the remote endpointor constrained CPU in remote VTAM(R) address space. To resolve this problem,use the following procedures:"}

situation_name: N3V_HPR_Throughput
description: HPR RTP Connection with Low Throughput
actions: {"The actual throughput rate of the HPR RTP connection is less than the initial throughput rate of the HPR RTP connection (initial throughput rate is calculated as 5 percent of the capacity of the HPR RTP pipe). In addition, there are HPR packets waiting to be sent. The probable cause of low throughput is network congestion."}

situation_name: N3V_Paging_Rate
description: Paging rate
actions: {"Paging by the VTAM address space is generally moderate. Determine a threshold value by observing history to obtain a working baseline. A paging rate much higher than the established baseline indicates an increase in workload and might signify an impending performance problem. Use the diagnostic procedures outlined in the IBM SNA Network Implementation Guide and take corrective action."}

situation_name: N3V_Pct_ECSA_Allocated_Stg
description: Percent ECSA allocated storage
actions: {"The percentage of ECSA storage that is currently allocated compared to the maximum ECSA storage that is allowed. Determine a threshold value by observing history to obtain a working baseline. A percentage of ECSA allocated storage significantly in excess of the established baseline indicates an increase in workload and possibly an impending performance problem. Increasing the maximum ECSA storage allowed, load balancing, and work rescheduling are possible solutions."}

situation_name: N3V_Total_CSA_Pct
description: Total CSA percentage in use by the VTAM address space.
actions: {"A percentage of the common storage areas above and below the 16MB line. Common storage areas are used by VTAM and other resources in your network to maintain buffers and control blocks in the CSA for MVS systems. For performance reasons, VTAM offers some control over its use of common storage areas with the start options. Isolate the cause of the problem using diagnostic procedures outlined in the IBM SNA Network Implementation Guide."}

situation_name: N3V_VTAM_App_Except_Warning
description: A VTAM Application encountered an exceptional condition.
actions: {"Check the VTAM Applications workspace to determine the application that took the exception by examining the Exceptions attribute.","The possible exceptions include one or more of the following conditions which will be indicated in the workspace for the application that took the exception:","Examine the joblog for the VTAM application that took the exceptional condition to determine the cause of the problem."}

situation_name: NT_AMS_Alert_Critical
description: Agent Management Services Alert.
actions: {"Agent Management Services has issued an alert for a managed agent it cannot restart.Check the alert message for details."}

situation_name: NT_Available_Bytes_Critical
description: Virtual memory on the Zeroed, Free and Standby lists is too high.
actions: {"The system is running out of virtual memory.Consider moving workload to other servers or look for the program that is causing a memory leak.To determine the amount of memory required for the workload, look at the process report.To determine whether any program is causing memory leakage, use the short term history to see if any process memory requirement grows without shrinking with time."}

situation_name: NT_Available_Bytes_Critical_2
description: Virtual memory on the Zeroed, Free and Standby lists is too high.
actions: {"The system is running out of virtual memory.Consider moving workload to other servers or look for the program that is causing a memory leak.To determine the amount of memory required for the workload, look at the process report.To determine whether any program is causing memory leakage, use the short term history to see if any process memory requirement grows without shrinking with time."}

situation_name: NT_Available_Bytes_Warning
description: Virtual memory on the Zeroed, Free and Standby lists is rising.
actions: {"The system is running out of virtual memory.Consider moving workload to other servers or look for the program that is causing a memory leak.To determine the amount of memory required for the workload, look at the process report.To determine whether any program is causing memory leak, use the short term history to see if any process memory requirement grows without shrinking with time."}

situation_name: NT_Available_Bytes_Warning_2
description: Virtual memory on the Zeroed, Free and Standby lists is rising.
actions: {"The system is running out of virtual memory.Consider moving workload to other servers or look for the program that is causing a memory leak.To determine the amount of memory required for the workload, look at the process report.To determine whether any program is causing memory leak, use the short term history to see if any process memory requirement grows without shrinking with time."}

situation_name: NT_Bottleneck_Disk
description: Potential system slowdown due to disk activity.
actions: {"A system slowdown exists due to excessive disk activity. If this condition is caused by excessive paging consider adding more physical memory to the system. Otherwise consider moving frequently accessed application files across multiple physical disks to relieve disk bottlenecks."}

situation_name: NT_Bottleneck_Memory
description: Potential system slowdown due to insufficent available memory.
actions: {"A potential system slowdown exists due to insufficent available memory. Consider adding more physical memory to the system."}

situation_name: NT_Bottleneck_Paging
description: Potential system slowdown due to paging activity.
actions: {"A potential system slowdown exists due to paging activity. Consider adding more physical memory to the system or moving some applications to a different server."}

situation_name: NT_Bottleneck_Processor
description: Potential system slowdown due to high processor utilization.
actions: {"A potential system slowdown exists due to high processor utilization. Consider moving some applications to a different system or replacing the system hardware with faster hardware."}

situation_name: NT_Context_Switches_Sec
description: An indication of multitasking level. Context switches are too high.
actions: {"The system switches from application to application through context switches.Poor performance could be caused by having too many applications running on the system.Context switches can degrade server performance by taking up time switching between applications.Consider reducing the number of applications on the server."}

situation_name: NT_Context_Switches_Sec_Low
description: Context switches per second set at low setting for bottleneck analysis.
actions: {"The system switches from application to application through context switches.Poor performance could be caused by having too many applications running on the system.Context switches can degrade server performance by spending time switching between applications.Consider reducing the number of applications on the server."}

situation_name: NT_Disk_Space_Low
description: Free space on a logical disk drive is too low.
actions: {"You are about to run out of space in your disk.Consider deleting files in the temp or internet history directories (usually these are located in WINNT/HISTORY).If more space is needed, consider moving, archiving, or compressing some of your large files."}

situation_name: NT_Invalid_Logon_Attempt
description: Logon attempt with an incorrect account or password.
actions: {"Users have attempted to logon to the server without the correct password.Look at the NT Monitored Security log to find out which ID is generating these messages."}

situation_name: NT_Log_Space_Low
description: One of the NT Logs is close to capacity.
actions: {"One of your event logs is close to full.If you have the event log write over the old entries then no action is needed.If this message appears too often, consider enlarging the maximum log size for the corresponding event log by opening the Event Viewer and selecting from the menu Action - Properties on Windows XP/2000 or Log - Log Settings on Windows NT.You may also want to investigate where the log messages come from."}

situation_name: NT_Logical_Disk_Space_Critical
description: Free space on a logical disk drive is too low.
actions: {"You are about to run out of space in your disk.Consider deleting files in the temp or internet history directories (usually they are located in WINNT/HISTORY).If more space is needed, consider moving, archiving, or compressing some of your large files."}

situation_name: NT_Logical_Disk_Space_Warning
description: Free space on a logical disk drive is shrinking.
actions: {"You are about to run out of space in your disk.Consider deleting files in the temp or internet history directories (usually they are located in WINNT/HISTORY).If more space is needed, consider moving, archiving, or compressing some of your large files."}

situation_name: NT_Memory_Pages_Sec
description: An indication of high memory demand.
actions: {"Memory demand is too high. Consider adding more physical memory to the system."}

situation_name: NT_Memory_Pages_Sec_2
description: An indication of high memory demand.
actions: {"Memory demand is too high. Consider adding more physical memory to the system."}

situation_name: NT_Memory_Pages_Sec_Low
description: Memory Pages per second at low setting for bottleneck analysis.
actions: {"This situation is used by bottleneck analysis situations to indicate low paging activity caused by low memory usage. Low paging activity alone does not indicate a problem. Consider using the bottleneck analysis situations for detailed analysis of memory related problems."}

situation_name: NT_Memory_Pages_Sec_Low_2
description: Memory Pages per second at low setting for bottleneck analysis.
actions: {"This situation is used by bottleneck analysis situations to indicate low paging activity caused by low memory usage. Low paging activity alone does not indicate a problem. Consider using the bottleneck analysis situations for detailed analysis of memory related problems."}

situation_name: NT_Missing_Msdtc_Warning
description: The Microsoft Distributed Coordinator is not running.
actions: {"Start the Microsoft Distributed Coordinator process. If the Microsoft Distributed Coordinator process fails, check the Windows Event log for more information."}

situation_name: NT_Missing_Msdtc_Warning_2
description: The Microsoft Distributed Coordinator is not running.
actions: {"Start the Microsoft Distributed Coordinator process. If the Microsoft Distributed Coordinator process fails, check the Windows Event log for more information."}

situation_name: NT_Missing_Process
description: Test if the NT Scheduler process is running before using it.
actions: {"Start the NT Scheduler process. If the NT Scheduler process fails, check the Windows Event log for more information."}

situation_name: NT_Missing_Process_2
description: Test if the NT Scheduler process is running before using it.
actions: {"Start the NT Scheduler process. If the NT Scheduler process fails, check the Windows Event log for more information."}

situation_name: NT_Number_Processes_Critical
description: Number of processes present in the system is too high.
actions: {"Close any applications that are not being used. Determine whether any application processes are hung (not responding) and stop them."}

situation_name: NT_Number_Processes_Warning
description: Number of processes present in the system is rising.
actions: {"Close any applications that are not being used. Determine whether any application processes are hung (not responding) and stop them."}

situation_name: NT_Paging_File_Critical
description: Percent of the Page File in use is too high.
actions: {"Your paging file is running low in space.Either move applications to other servers if response time becomes an issue or increase your paging file to accommodate for more applications.For better performance, allocate additional paging storage in a separate disk drive.To reduce fragmentation, keep both the maximum and the minimum to be the same value."}

situation_name: NT_Paging_File_Warning
description: Percent of the Page File in use is rising.
actions: {"Your paging file is running low in space.Either move applications to other servers if response time becomes an issue or increase your paging file to accommodate for more applications.For better performance, allocate additional paging storage in a separate disk drive.To reduce fragmentation, keep both the maximum and the minimum to be the same value."}

situation_name: NT_Percent_Disk_Time
description: An indication of high disk activity.
actions: {"This situation is used by bottleneck analysis situations to indicate high disk activity. High disk activity alone does not indicate a problem. Consider using the bottleneck analysis situations for detailed analysis of disk related problems. Consider moving frequently accessed application files to multiple physical disks to relieve disk bottlenecks."}

situation_name: NT_Percent_Disk_Time_Low
description: The percent Disk Time low setting for bottleneck analysis.
actions: {"This situation is used by bottleneck analysis situations to indicate low disk activity. Low disk activity alone does not indicate a problem. Consider using the bottleneck analysis situations for detailed analysis of disk related problems."}

situation_name: NT_Percent_Processor_Time
description: An indication of high processor activity.
actions: {"This situation is used by bottleneck analysis situations to indicate high processor utilization. High processor utilization alone does not indicate a problem. Consider using the bottleneck analysis situations for detailed analysis of processor related problems. Consider moving workload to other systems to relieve processor bottlenecks."}

situation_name: NT_Percent_Processor_Time_Low
description: The Percent Processor time low setting for bottleneck analysis.
actions: {"This situation is used by bottleneck analysis situations to indicate low processor utilization. Low processor utilization alone does not indicate a problem. Consider using the bottleneck analysis situations for detailed analysis of processor related problems."}

situation_name: NT_Percent_Total_Proc_Time
description: An indication of high activity on all processors.
actions: {"The total processor utilization for all processors is too high. Consider moving some applications to other systems to reduce processor load."}

situation_name: NT_Percent_Total_Proc_Time_Low
description: Percent Total processor time low setting for bottleneck analysis.
actions: {"This situation is used by bottleneck analysis situations to indicate low total processor utilization across all processors. Low total processor utilization alone does not indicate a problem. Consider using the bottleneck analysis situations for detailed analysis of processor related problems."}

situation_name: NT_Physical_Disk_Busy_Critical
description: Percent of the time the disk drive is busy is too high.
actions: {"Your physical disk is receiving too many I/O requests.Before taking any action, check the queue length of the disk first.If it is more than 2, move some of your files to another disk.Consider using a SCSI drive that can handle more I/Os than EIDE because it may be able to handle I/O asynchronously."}

situation_name: NT_Physical_Disk_Busy_Warning
description: Percent of the time the disk drive is busy is rising.
actions: {"Your physical disk is receiving too many I/O requests.Before taking any action, check the queue length of the disk first.If it is more than 2, move some of your files to another disk.Consider using a SCSI drive that can handle more I/Os than EIDE because it may be able to handle I/O asynchronously."}

situation_name: NT_Process_CPU_Critical
description: Percent of processor time used by this process.
actions: {"The percentage of processor time used by this process is too high.Check the operation of the process to see if it is responding.If the percentage of processor time continues to be high, consider recycling the process."}

situation_name: NT_Process_CPU_Critical_2
description: Percent of processor time used by this process.
actions: {"The percentage of processor time used by this process is too high.Check the operation of the process to see if it is responding.If the percentage of processor time continues to be high, consider recycling the process."}

situation_name: NT_Process_CPU_Warning
description: Percent of processor time used by this process.
actions: {"The percentage of processor time used by this process is high.Check the operation of the process to see if it is responding.If the percentage of processor time continues to be high, consider recycling the process."}

situation_name: NT_Process_CPU_Warning_2
description: Percent of processor time used by this process.
actions: {"The percentage of processor time used by this process is high.Check the operation of the process to see if it is responding.If the percentage of processor time continues to be high, consider recycling the process."}

situation_name: NT_Process_Memory_Critical
description: Working set size for a specific process is too high.
actions: {"The working set size for an NT process is high.Check the operation of the process to see if it is responding.If the size continues to increase, consider recycling the process."}

situation_name: NT_Process_Memory_Critical_2
description: Working set size for a specific process is too high.
actions: {"The working set size for an NT process is high.Check the operation of the process to see if it is responding.If the size continues to increase, consider recycling the process."}

situation_name: NT_Process_Memory_Warning
description: Working set size for a specific process is rising.
actions: {"The working set size for an NT process is high.Check the operation of the process to see if it is responding.If the size continues to increase, consider recycling the process."}

situation_name: NT_Process_Memory_Warning_2
description: Working set size for a specific process is rising.
actions: {"The working set size for an NT process is high.Check the operation of the process to see if it is responding.If the size continues to increase, consider recycling the process."}

situation_name: NT_Processor_Interrupt_Critical
description: Number of device interrupts per second is too high.
actions: {"There are too many hardware and software interrupts in your server.You should look for applications that utilize interrupts extensively such as RAS, Print Server, Fax Server and move them to a dedicated Windows server.Identify and replace any defective boards.Replace any beta device drivers."}

situation_name: NT_Processor_Interrupts_Warning
description: Number of device interrupts per second is rising.
actions: {"There are too many hardware and software interrupts in your server.You should look for applications that utilize interrupts extensively such as RAS, Print Server, Fax Server and move them to a dedicated Windows server.Identify and replace any defective boards.Replace any beta device drivers."}

situation_name: NT_Service_Error
description: A Service Error was reported.
actions: {"A Service Error was reported. Look in the Windows Event Log Viewer for information about the service failure. Correct the problem, and restart the service."}

situation_name: NT_Services_Automatic_Start
description: Start any non-running Automatic Start services.
actions: {"An Automatic Start service was not running, and an attempt was made to restart the service.If the service failed to start look in the Windows Event Log Viewer for information about the service failure. Correct the problem, and restart the service."}

situation_name: NT_System_CPU_Critical
description: Percent of time all processors are busy is too high.
actions: {"The CPU in your system is being utilized heavily.Look at the process report and consider moving some applications to other servers.Look at short term history on process to see if any particular process is using excessive amount of CPU when you have this problem."}

situation_name: NT_System_CPU_Warning
description: Percent of time all processors are busy is rising.
actions: {"The CPU in your system is being utilized heavily.Look at the process report and consider moving some applications to other servers.Look at short term history on process to see if any particular process is using excessive amount of CPU when you have this problem."}

situation_name: NT_System_File_Critical
description: Rate of operations to file system devices per second.
actions: {"The rate of operations to file system devices per second is too high. Consider moving some frequently accessed files to other physical disks to avoid disk bottlenecks."}

situation_name: NT_System_File_Warning
description: Rate of operations to file system devices per second.
actions: {"The rate of operations to file system devices per second is rising. Consider moving some frequently accessed files to other physical disks to avoid disk bottlenecks."}

situation_name: NT_System_Proc_Q_Length
description: An indication of processor congestion.
actions: {"The processor queue length is too high indicating processor congestion. Consider moving workload to other systems to relieve processor bottlenecks or replacing the system hardware with faster hardware."}

situation_name: NT_System_Proc_Q_Length_Low
description: System proc queue length low setting for bottleneck analysis.
actions: {"The processor queue length is too low indicating that the system may be under utilized. Consider moving application workload to this system to increase its workload."}

situation_name: NT_System_Total_Interrupts
description: An indication of I/O device activity.
actions: {"SystemI/O device activity is too high. This could be an indication that the processor is unable to service the workload caused by device I/O. This could also be an indication of an impending device failure. Consider moving highly active devices to another processor or replacing the system hardware with faster hardware. Investigate the Windows System Event log or device logs for indications of potential device failure."}

situation_name: NT_System_Total_Interrupts_Low
description: System total interrupts low setting for bottleneck analysis.
actions: {"System device I/O activity is too low. Low device I/O alone does not indicate a problem. Consider using the bottleneck analysis situations for detailed analysis of system related problems.This could also be an indication of a device failure. Investigate the Windows System Event log or device logs for indications of a device failure."}

situation_name: OS390_Allocated_CSA_Crit
description: Allocated CSA Critical Situation
actions: {"Allocated CSA (Common Storage Area) storage exceeds its Critical threshold.A system crash may occur due to exhausted CSA. Identify the address spaces using high amounts of CSA. Nonessential address spaces with high usage should be stopped or canceled to prevent a crash.Workspace \"Address Space Common Storage - Active Users\" can be used to locate CSA users."}

situation_name: OS390_Allocated_CSA_Warn
description: Allocated CSA Warning Situation
actions: {"Allocated CSA (Common Storage Area) storage exceeds its Warningthreshold.A system crash may occur due to exhausted CSA.Identify the address spaces using high amounts of CSA. Nonessential address spaces with high usage should be stopped or canceled to prevent a crash.Workspace \"Address Space Common Storage - Active Users\" can be used to locate CSA users."}

situation_name: OS390_Available_Frames_Crit
description: Central storage available frame count critical situation
actions: {"Set the critical threshold (in frames) for the available frame queue low alert.The available frame queue is a list of frames that are available to the system. If the number of frames is too low, SRM automatically replenishes the queue by stealing frames that have not been recently referenced.Controlling the available frame queue is the method SRM uses to manage storage use. A low available frame queue is a problem only if it causes contention for storage."}

situation_name: OS390_Available_Frames_Warn
description: Central storage available frame count warning situation
