situation_name: OS390_Local_PageDS_Errors_Crit
description: Local Page Dataset Errors Critical Situation
actions: {"There are more errors on local page data sets than the current Critical threshold. Identify the failing data set(s). Check for spare page data set slots. If there is no spare, the PAGETOT parameter in IEASYSxx should be increased to provide at least one spare slot per two page data sets. Remove the failing data set(s) from the PAGE parameter in IEASYSxx. If there are spare slots, PAGEADD a large data set and use PAGEDEL REPLACE to move the pages of the failing data sets to a good data set."}

situation_name: OS390_Local_PageDS_Errors_Warn
description: Local Page Dataset Errors Warning Situation
actions: {"There are more errors on local page data sets than the current Warning threshold. Identify the failing data set(s). Check for a spare page data set slot. If there is no spare, the PAGETOT parameter in IEASYSxx should be increased to provide at least one spare slot per two page data sets. Remove the failing data set from the PAGE parameter in IEASYSxx. If there is a spare slot, PAGEADD a data set and use PAGEDEL REPLACE to move the pages to a good data set."}

situation_name: OS390_Local_PageDS_PctFull_Crit
description: Local Page Dataset Percent Full Critical Situation
actions: {"The percentage of slots in use on a local page data set exceeds the current Critical threshold. When usage approaches 30%, paging efficiency begins to decline, and blocked paging disappears at about 35% occupancy. Once this situation occurs, PAGEADD another data set. If the current PAGTOTL setting in IEASYSxx does not allow another data set to be added, it should be increased before the next IPL."}

situation_name: OS390_Local_PageDS_PctFull_Warn
description: Local Page Dataset Percent Full Warning Situation
actions: {"The percentage of slots in use on a local page data set exceeds the current Warning threshold. When usage approaches 30%, paging efficiency begins to decline, and blocked paging disappears at about 35% occupancy. Once this situation occurs, prepare to PAGEADD another data set if the Critical threshold is passed. If the current PAGTOTL setting in IEASYSxx does not allow another data set to be added, it should be increased before the next IPL."}

situation_name: OS390_Max_ASIDs_in_Use_Crit
description: Percent Max ASID in use Critical Situation
actions: {"The number of possible address spaces has reached its Critical threshold. If the maximum is reached, an emergency IPL may become necessary. System programmer help is needed immediately. Things to check include the values of the MAXUSER, RSVNONR, and RSVSTRT parameters and any known problems leading to address space IDs becoming unusable."}

situation_name: OS390_Max_ASIDs_in_Use_Warn
description: Percent Max ASID in use Warning Situation
actions: {"The number of possible address spaces has reached its Warning threshold. If the maximum is reached, an emergency IPL may become necessary. System programmer help is needed immediately. Things to check include the values of the MAXUSER, RSVNONR, and RSVSTRT parameters and any known problems leading to address space IDs becoming unusable."}

situation_name: OS390_OLTEP_Active_Crit
description: OLTEP Active Critical Situation
actions: {"OLTEP is active. Determine who is using OLTEP and minimize its time of use. OLTEP (On-Line Test Executive Program) is a framework for IBM hardware diagnostic programs that dates back to OS/360. No current device requires OLTEP, but some systems may have older devices (such as 3420 tapes) in which OLTEP runs out of its own library. When OLTEP is running, system integrity may be at risk."}

situation_name: OS390_OLTEP_Active_Warn
description: OLTEP Active Warning Situation
actions: {"OLTEP is active. Determine who is using OLTEP and minimize its time of use. OLTEP (On-Line Test Executive Program) is a framework for IBM hardware diagnostic programs that dates back to OS/360. No current device requires OLTEP, but some systems may have older devices (such as 3420 tapes) in which OLTEP runs out of its own library. When OLTEP is running, system integrity may be at risk."}

situation_name: OS390_Outstanding_WTORs_Crit
description: Outstanding Operator Replies Critical Situation
actions: {"Outstanding operator replies exceeds the current Critical threshold.Check the operator console for outstanding replies and address them as required.If all the outstanding replies are correct and routine, the threshold should be adjusted."}

situation_name: OS390_Outstanding_WTORs_Warn
description: Outstanding Operator Replies Warning Situation
actions: {"Outstanding operator replies exceeds the current Warning threshold.Check the operator console for outstanding replies and address them as required.If all the outstanding replies are correct and routine, the threshold should be adjusted."}

situation_name: OS390_PLPA_PageDS_PctFull_Crit
description: PLPA Page Dataset Percent Full Critical
actions: {"PLPA Page Dataset Percent Full situation indicates that the Pageable Link Pack Area page dataset is full beyond the Critical threshold and may require further action. Because pages can spill to the common page dataset when the PLPA dataset fills up, the PLPA dataset may be deliberately made small (often defined as just a cylinder) and will always fill up. Since the full condition may be expected as normal, this situation is disabled by default."}

situation_name: OS390_PLPA_PageDS_PctFull_Warn
description: PLPA Page Dataset Percent Full Warning
actions: {"PLPA Page Dataset Percent Full situation indicates that the Pageable Link Pack Area page dataset is full beyond the Warning threshold and may require further action.Because pages can spill to the common page dataset when the PLPA dataset fills up, the PLPA dataset may be deliberately made small (often defined as just a cylinder) and will always fill up. Since the full condition may be expected as normal, this situation is disabled by default."}

situation_name: OS390_PageDSNotOperational_Crit
description: Page Dataset Not Operational Critical Situation
actions: {"The number of non-operational page data sets exceeds the Critical threshold. Verify paging devices are operational. If a device is not operational, attempt to VARY it online. If a page data set had been DRAINed by a prior PAGEDEL DRAIN command, it may now be removed by a PAGEDEL DELETE command. If this situation pops up without warning, an IPL is imminent. Prepare to shut down and immediately get help from a systems programmer."}

situation_name: OS390_PageDSNotOperational_Warn
description: Page Dataset Not Operational Warning Situation
actions: {"The number of non-operational page data sets exceeds the Warning threshold. Verify the paging devices are operational. If a device is not operational, attempt to VARY it online. If a page data set had been DRAINed by a prior PAGEDEL DRAIN command, it may now be removed by a PAGEDEL DELETE command. If this situation pops up without warning, an IPL is imminent. Prepare to shut down and immediately get help from a systems programmer."}

situation_name: OS390_Page_Rate_Crit
description: Page Rate Critical
actions: {"The current paging rate exceeds the Critical threshold. This situation is disabled by default and should be activated only when necessary to characterize a chronic excessive paging problem."}

situation_name: OS390_Page_Rate_Warn
description: Page Rate Warning
actions: {"The current paging rate exceeds the Warning threshold.This situation is disabled by default and should be activated only when necessary to characterize a chronic excessive paging problem."}

situation_name: OS390_Physical_CPUs_Online_Crit
description: System physical CPUs online count critical situation
actions: {"The number of online CPUs is less than the current Critical threshold. This situation is disabled by default (threshold of 0) and should be activated only to diagnose chronic configuration problems. The threshold should be carefully examined if the LPAR CPU Management Vary CPU function of Intelligent Resource Director is in use."}

situation_name: OS390_Physical_CPUs_Online_Warn
description: System physical CPUs online count warning situation
actions: {"The number of online CPUs is less than the current Warning threshold. This situation is disabled by default (threshold of 0) and should be activated only to diagnose chronic configuration problems. The threshold should be carefully examined if the LPAR CPU Management Vary CPU function of Intelligent Resource Director is in use."}

situation_name: OS390_RMF_Not_Active_Crit
description: RMF Not Active Critical Situation
actions: {"The RMF data collector is not active. RMF data is essential to performance management and problem analysis. Attempt to restart the RMF collector. If this is not possible, notify a system programmer."}

situation_name: OS390_RMF_Not_Active_Warn
description: RMF Not Active Warning Situation
actions: {"The RMF data collector is not active. RMF data is essential to performance management and problem analysis. Attempt to restart the RMF collector. If this is not possible, notify a system programmer."}

situation_name: OS390_SMF_Not_Recording_Crit
description: SMF Not Recording Critical Situation
actions: {"SMF data is not being recorded. SMF data has numerous uses including resource accounting and capacity management. Missing data can damage the data center management process. Immediately get help from a system programmer to check the SMF data sets and restart the collection process as quickly as possible."}

situation_name: OS390_SMF_Not_Recording_Warn
description: SMF Not Recording Warning Situation
actions: {"SMF data is not being recorded. SMF data has numerous uses including resource accounting and capacity management. Missing data can damage the data center management process. Immediately get help from a system programmer to check the SMF data sets and restart the collection process as quickly as possible."}

situation_name: OS390_Syslog_Not_Recording_Crit
description: Syslog Not Recording Critical Situation
actions: {"SYSLOG recording has stopped. A system programmer should be called to diagnose the reason. One possibility is that JES SPOOL space is exhausted. SYSLOG should be going to a printer or other device designated for backup."}

situation_name: OS390_Syslog_Not_Recording_Warn
description: Syslog Not Recording Warning Situation
actions: {"SYSLOG recording has stopped. A system programmer should be called to diagnose the reason. One possibility is that JES SPOOL space is exhausted. SYSLOG should be going to a printer or other device designated for backup."}

situation_name: OS390_System_PageFaultRate_Crit
description: System page fault rate critical situation
actions: {"The system page fault rate exceeds the current Critical threshold. This situation is disabled by default."}

situation_name: OS390_System_PageFaultRate_Warn
description: System page fault rate warning situation
actions: {"The system page fault rate exceeds the current Warning threshold. This situation is disabled by default."}

situation_name: OS390_System_Page_Rate_Crit
description: System Page Rate Critical
actions: {"The system page rate exceeds the Critical threshold. Excessive paging may increase application wait and response time. Because system page rate is dependent on processor type, real storage configuration, and workload you may need to adjust your paging system based on your installation defined service requirements. This situation is disabled by default and should be activated only to diagnose a chronic high paging rate."}

situation_name: OS390_System_Page_Rate_Warn
description: System Page Rate Warning
actions: {"The system page rate exceeds the Warning threshold.Excessive paging may increase application wait and response time. Because system page rate is dependent on processor type, real storage configuration, and workload you may need to adjust your paging system based on your installation defined service requirements. This situation is disabled by default and should be activated only to diagnose a chronic high paging rate."}

situation_name: OS390_Tape_Dropped_Ready_Crit
description: Tape Drive Dropped Ready Critical Situation
actions: {"The number of tape devices that have dropped ready exceeds the current Critical threshold. Check the devices and attempt to make the indicated devices ready. If this is not possible, report this condition as a hardware problem."}

situation_name: OS390_Tape_Dropped_Ready_Warn
description: Tape Drive Dropped Ready Warning Situation
actions: {"The number of tape devices that have dropped ready exceeds the current Warning threshold. Check the devices and attempt to make the indicated devices ready. If this is not possible, report this condition as a hardware problem."}

situation_name: OS390_Tape_Mount_Pend_Time_Crit
description: Tape Mount Pending Time Critical
actions: {"Tape Mount Pending Time exceeding thresholds may require contacting operations to ensure that the MOUNT request has been recognized by personnel responsible for mounting tapes on the requested tape unit(s)"}

situation_name: OS390_Tape_Mount_Pend_Time_Warn
description: Tape Mount Pending Time Warning
actions: {"Tape Mount Pending Time exceeding thresholds may require contacting operations to ensure that the MOUNT request has been recognized by personnel responsible for mounting tapes on the requested tape unit(s)"}

situation_name: OS390_Tape_Not_Responding_Crit
description: Tape Drive Not Responding Critical Situation
actions: {"The number of tape drives not responding exceeds the Critical threshold. If this condition is persistent and the device(s) cannot be activated by varying them online, open a hardware incident and have the tape subsystem checked for hardware errors."}

situation_name: OS390_Tape_Not_Responding_Warn
description: Tape Drive Not Responding Warning Situation
actions: {"The number of tape drives not responding exceeds the Warning threshold. If this condition is persistent and the device(s) cannot be activated by varying them online, open a hardware incident and have the tape subsystem checked for hardware errors."}

situation_name: OS390_Tape_Permanent_Error_Crit
description: Tape Permanent Errors Critical Situation
actions: {"The number of permanent errors on the current tape device exceeds the current Critical threshold. There should be a standard procedure to deal with this condition. If not, request help from a media specialist."}

situation_name: OS390_Tape_Permanent_Error_Warn
description: Tape Permanent Errors Warning Situation
actions: {"The number of permanent errors on the current tape device exceeds the current Warning threshold. There should be a standard procedure to deal with this condition. If not, notify a media specialist."}

situation_name: OS390_Tape_Temp_Errors_Crit
description: Tape Temporary Errors Critical Situation
actions: {"The number of recoverable (temporary) errors on a tape device exceeds the current Critical threshold. This could be either a media problem or a device problem. If no procedures are in place to deal with such a problem, report it to a media or storage management specialist."}

situation_name: OS390_Tape_Temp_Errors_Warn
description: Tape Temporary Errors Warning Situation
actions: {"The number of recoverable (temporary) errors on a tape device exceeds the current Warning threshold. This could be either a media problem or a device problem. Monitor the situation carefully to see if it degrades further. If it does worsen, follow any existing procedures to deal with such a problem, or report it to a media or storage management specialist."}

situation_name: OS390_Undispatched_Tasks_Crit
description: Undispatched Tasks Critical Situation
actions: {"The number of undispatched tasks exceeds the Critical threshold. This threshold should be at least equal to three times the number of [logical] processors in the configuration. No particular action is necessary, but if the condition persists for more than an hour a capacity upgrade may be necessary. Check also to see if any important service classes are missing their goals."}

situation_name: OS390_Undispatched_Tasks_Warn
description: Undispatched Tasks Warning Situation
actions: {"The number of undispatched tasks exceeds the Warning threshold. This threshold should be at least equal to the number of [logical] processors in the configuration. No particular action is necessary."}

situation_name: OS390_Unowned_Common_Stor_Crit
description: Amount of unowned common storage critical situation
actions: {"The amount of \"unowned\" storage in the Common Storage Area(CSA) exceeds the Critical threshold. Unowned CSA is caused when an address space terminates without freeing its CSA.Although it may be used by other address spaces, the unowned storage can cause CSA to become fragmented.Identifying and freeing unowned (and unused) CSA may help prevent system failure when CSA becomes overallocated. Contact the systems programmer to verify where storage is taken."}

situation_name: OS390_Unowned_Common_Stor_Warn
description: Amount of unowned common storage warning situation
actions: {"The amount of \"unowned\" storage in the Common Services Area (CSA) exceeds the Warning threshold. Unowned CSA is caused when an address space terminates without freeing its CSA.Although it may be used by other address spaces, the unowned storage can cause CSA to become fragmented.Identifying and freeing unowned (and unused) CSA may help prevent system failure when CSA becomes overallocated."}

situation_name: OS390_Unref_Interval_Cnt_Crit
description: Unreferenced Interval Count Critical Situation
actions: {"Set the critical threshold for the unreferenced interval count. The value can be 1 to 2540.Because lower values indicate resource contention, the unreferenced interval count (UIC) is an alert where the critical threshold must be less than the warning value."}

situation_name: OS390_Unref_Interval_Cnt_Warn
description: Unreferenced Interval Count Warning Situation
actions: {"Set the warning threshold for the unreferenced interval count. The value can be 1 to 2540.Because lower values indicate resource contention, the unreferenced interval count (UIC) is an alert where the warning threshold must be greater than the critical."}

situation_name: OS390_WTO_Buffers_Left_Crit
description: WTO Buffers Remaining Critical Situation
actions: {"Available write-to-operator message buffers are less than the Critical threshold. The default number of buffers is 1500, and the maximum is 9999. Check as soon as possible to see if a console device is down. If so, switch the message stream to another device. An IPL may be needed if prompt action is not taken."}

situation_name: OS390_WTO_Buffers_Left_Warn
description: WTO Buffers Remaining Warning Situation
actions: {"Available write-to-operator message buffers are less than the Warning threshold. The default number of buffers is 1500, and the maximum is 9999. Check as soon as possible to see if a console device is down. If so, switch the message stream to another device. An IPL may be needed if prompt action is not taken."}

situation_name: OS400_ASP_Nearing_Capacity
description: An Auxiliary Storage Pool's (ASP) storage capacity is filled beyond a comfortable threshold. The default threshold is 80% of capacity.
actions: {"You need to investigate why the ASP is nearing its capacity.Consider adding storage to the ASP, archiving and removing objects that are no longer needed,or look for objects that are suspiciously large and determineif an application is writing to them in error."}

situation_name: OS400_ASP_Overflow_Warning
description: An Auxiliary Storage Pool (ASP) was full and overflowed into the system ASP.Object allocations directed into the user ASP were instead directed into the system ASP.
actions: {"You need to investigate why the ASP overflowed its capacity. If the ASP is no longer full then probably a spike in usage caused the overflow.If the ASP is still full then you should be able to determine the largest objects.","Consider adding storage to the ASP, archiving or removing objects that are no longer needed,or looking for suspiciously large objects which might be growing in error.","You should also consider balancing the ASP after the situation is corrected."}

situation_name: OS400_Address_Critical
description: Permanent addresses, temporary addresses, or the system auxiliary storage pool (ASP) are nearing capacity.
actions: {"This situation goes true when the percentage of permanent address space use is high, the percentage of temporary address space use is high,or the system ASP's storage use is high.","If the system ASP use is high then you might need to add disk units to the system ASP, add new ASPs, balance storage use between ASPs, or investigate if unneeded objects can be archived and removed from the system ASP.","If the temporary address space percentage is high then you need to IPL the system to recover addresses."}

situation_name: OS400_Aux_Stor_Near_Guidelines
description: The usage of total auxiliary storage capacity is nearing its guideline value.By default the guideline for maximum storage usage is 90% andthis situation triggers at 80%.The auxiliary storage capacity is the total of all basic ASP and active independent ASP capacities.
actions: {"You need to investigate why usage of auxiliary storage is nearing its capacity. You can use the System or Disk and I/O workspaces to see which ASPs and disks are filling. If available, the BRMS command Display ASP Information (DSPASPBRM) can also be used.","Consider adding storage to one or more ASPs, archiving or removing objects that are no longer needed, or looking for suspiciously large objects which might be growing in error.","You should also consider balancing ASPs after the situation is corrected."}

situation_name: OS400_Aux_Stor_Over_Guidelines
description: The usage of total auxiliary storage capacity is over its guideline value.By default the guideline for maximum storage usage is 90%.The auxiliary storage capacity is the total of all basic ASP and active independent ASP capacities.
actions: {"You need to investigate why usage of auxiliary storage is over its capacity guideline. You can use the System or Disk and I/O workspaces to see which ASPs and disks are filling. If available, the BRMS command Display ASP Information (DSPASPBRM) can also be used.","Consider adding storage to one or more ASPs, archiving or removing objects that are no longer needed, or looking for suspiciously large objects which might be growing in error.","You should also consider balancing ASPs after the situation is corrected."}

situation_name: OS400_CPU_Guidelines_Warning
description: The overall CPU utilization is over default guidelines.The guideline thresholds are based on the processing capacity in useand the default values are:
actions: {"You should investigate whether the high level of CPU utilization is normalor just an occasional spike.You can do this by collecting historical data orusing i5/OS commands such as Work with System Activity (WRKSYSACT).","If the CPU usage is increasing because of normal increases in the number or usage of applications then you should consider adding processors and/or memory to the system or partition, or upgrading the system hardware.","If the CPU usage is because of applications in error then the WRKSYSACT command can help identify the jobs which have suspiciously large CPU utilization."}

situation_name: OS400_CPU_Util_Warning
description: Monitors for high CPU utilization.
actions: {"This warning indicates that the average CPU usage was equal to or greater than 95 percent over the amount of time specified by the SSTS_DELAY environment variable."}

situation_name: OS400_Comm_FunctnChk_Workaround
description: Situation to eliminate function check errors logged with APPN
actions: {"This situation is started at the agent startup to reduce the function check errors and eventual agent failures when running consecutive APPN reports or running a situation after running an APPN report results in a machine check.Before running an APPN report, start an APPN situation (any formula)and keep it running. Then the user can run as many report as (s)he wants.Environment variable KA4_COMM_SIT_INTERVAL=600 is available in KMSPARM(KBBENV) file to customize collection intervals for comm situations."}

situation_name: OS400_Comm_IOP_Util_Warning
description: Monitors for high communications IOP usage.
actions: {"This Warning indicates that the total IOP processor time used by communications tasks during the monitor interval is greater than or equal to 25 percent."}

situation_name: OS400_Communication_Line_Failed
description: Monitors the QSYSOPR message queue for message CPA58CC or message CPA58CD.
actions: {"This situation goes true when either message CPA58CC (Line failed. Probable local hardware problem.) or message CPA58CD (Controller failed. Probable local system problem.) are reported to QSYSOPR.","Use the i5/OS command Work with Messages (WRKMSG MSGQ(*SYSOPR)) todisplay and reply to the message.The message contains more detailed information on the error condition."}

situation_name: OS400_Disk_Capacity_Critical
description: Monitors for potential capacity problems on individual disk units.
actions: {"This situation checks the amount of storage used on each individualdisk unit.By default it turns true if disk usage is greater than or equal to 90 percent.","If most disk units assigned to one ASP are nearing capacity then you may need to add storage to the ASP.If only a few disk units are filling thenconsider balancing the utilization within the ASP using the i5/OScommands Start ASP Balance (STRASPBAL) and End ASP Balance (ENDASPBAL)."}

situation_name: OS400_Disk_IOP_Util_Warning
description: Monitors for high disk IOP usage.
actions: {"This warning indicates that the disk IOP processor time is equal to or greater than 25 percent."}

situation_name: OS400_Disk_Mirroring_Not_Active
description: Checks for disk units which are configured for mirroring but which are not actively being mirrored.
actions: {"You need to investigate why the disk unit is not actively being mirrored.You can use the Disk and I/O workspace to see disk status and mirroring status,or use i5/OS commands such as Work with Disk Status (WRKDSKSTS).","The problem might be hardware related."}

situation_name: OS400_Disk_Util_Critical
description: Checks for the disk actuator arm being abnormally busy.
actions: {"This Alert indicates that the percentage of time that the actuator for the disk was busy during the monitor interval was greater than or equal to 60 percent."}

situation_name: OS400_Disk_Util_Warning
description: Checks for the disk actuator arm being busy.
actions: {"This Warning indicates that the percentage of time that the actuator for the disk was busy during the monitor interval was greater than or equal to 40 percent."}

situation_name: OS400_Interactive_Feature_CPU
description: Checks the percent of the interactive feature that is being used.The defaultvalue compared is 90 percent.
actions: {"The amount of interactive CPU being used is approaching the limit ofthe interactive feature.This may be caused by normal application usage, a temporary spike in usage, or an application that is in error.","Investigate the jobs using interactive CPU by collecting historical data or by using i5/OS commands such as Work with System Activity (WRKSYSACT).You may need to increase the interactive feature limit, or modify applications to improve performance or correct errors."}

situation_name: OS400_Interactive_Jobs_CPU_High
description: Monitors for abusers of the system.
actions: {"This Alert indicates that an interactive job is using 20 percent or more of the system's CPU time."}

situation_name: OS400_Job_AvgResponse_Time_High
description: Monitors interactive jobs for periods of poor response time. The default average response time comparison value is 5 seconds.
actions: {"Use this situation to determine which interactive jobs are having poor average response times.Consider redirecting the jobs to different queues,submitting them for processing at different time intervals, adjusting memory and processor resources, and investigating performance problems inthe job's application."}

situation_name: OS400_Job_Queue_Not_Active
description: Checks for job queues that are not activebut have jobs queued and ready to run.
actions: {"You need to investigate why the job queue is not active, and ifthe queued jobs should be started.You can use the Jobs and Queuesworkspace to see which job queues are held.You can use the i5/OS command Work with All Job Queues (WRKJOBQ) to see the list of jobsqueued to each job queue.","If the job queue should be started to allow the held jobs to run, thenuse the i5/OS command Release Job Queue (RLSJOBQ) to release the job queue."}

situation_name: OS400_Job_Queue_Not_Assigned
description: Checks for job queues which are not assignedto any subsystem but which have jobs queued and ready to run.
actions: {"You need to investigate why the job queue has not beenassigned to a subsystem.You can use the Jobs and Queuesworkspace to see which job queues are not assigned (theSubsystem field is blank).You can use the i5/OS command Work with All Job Queues (WRKJOBQ) to see the list of jobsqueued to each job queue.","If the job queue should be assigned to a subsystem so that its jobs can run, thenuse the i5/OS command Add Queue Entry (ADDJOBQE) command to add the job queue's entry to the appropriate subsystem description."}

situation_name: OS400_Management_Central_Events
description: Checks for any events that have been created by Management Central monitors since the situation startedrunning.The Management Central monitors create events based on user defined thresholds and values for system statistics, files, jobs, message queues, and Business toBusiness activity.The monitors are created and managed usingthe i5/OS Navigator graphical user interface.
actions: {"The purpose of this situation is to allow Management Centralevents to be fed into the IBM Tivoli Monitoring (ITM) environment.You can investigate the cause of the event using the i5/OS Navigator graphical user interface.The event canbe handled as if it came from an ITM situation."}

situation_name: OS400_Network_Attribute_Changed
description: Monitors for a change to network attributes.
actions: {"This Alert indicates that a change to a network attribute has occurred and has been logged in the audit journal. Such changes may affect or compromise the security of your system and/or network.","Investigate if the change is appropriate and intended."}

situation_name: OS400_OMA_Message_Log
description: Monitors for messages arriving in the QAUTOMON/KMSOMLOG message queue.
actions: {"This Alerts you to messages arriving in the IBM Tivoli Monitoring:i5/OS Agent message log.The messages show status such as whensituations start and stop, and might indicate problems in the agent with situations or reports."}

situation_name: OS400_Output_Queue_No_Writer
description: Checks for output queues which have no writer assigned but which have files spooled to them ready for processing.The spooled files cannot be processed until the appropriate writeris assigned to the output queue.
actions: {"You need to investigate why the output queue does not have awriter assigned to it.You can use the Messages and Spool workspaceto display the output queues which do not have writers assigned (theWriters column will contain a zero and the Writer Name column willbe blank).You can use the i5/OS command Work with All Output Queues (WRKOUTQ) to work with the output queue's writers and assign themas appropriate."}

situation_name: OS400_Perm_Addresses_Warning
description: Monitors for permanent addresses being used up.
actions: {"This warning indicates that the percentage of maximum possible addresses for permanent objects that have been used is greater than or equal to 95 percent."}

situation_name: OS400_Pool_Faulting_Warning
description: Monitors for high storage pool faulting rates.
actions: {"This warning indicates that the storage pool faulting rate is equal to or greater than 30 percent.Jobs using the storage pool might have slower than desired performance.You should investigate if more storageshould be added to the pool."}

situation_name: OS400_Pool_Transitions_High
description: Monitors for any pool active-to-ineligible transistions.
actions: {"This alert indicates a pool active-to-ineligible transition.These transitions occur when a transaction does not complete during a single time slice."}

situation_name: OS400_Snads_Critical
description: Checks if either situation OS400_Snads_Ended or OS400_Snads_Router_Failed is true.
actions: {"This situations goes true if SNADS has ended or the SNADS router has failed.You should investigate why SNADS has ended, correct any problems, andrestart SNADS."}

situation_name: OS400_Snads_Ended
description: Checks for a message that QSNADS subsystem ended.
actions: {"This alert indicates that the QSNADS subsystem has ended. The QSNADS subsystem must be active for SNA distributions to work."}

situation_name: OS400_Snads_Job_Missing
description: Checks for the QROUTER job.
actions: {"This Situation will raise if an active QROUTER job is not found. This indicates a problem with SNADS."}

situation_name: OS400_Snads_Router_Failed
description: Checks for a message that SNADS router ended abnormally.
actions: {"This alert indicates that the Snads Router has ended abnormally."}

situation_name: OS400_System_ASP_Warning
description: Monitors for the system auxiliary storage pool (ASP) getting full.
actions: {"This warning indicates that the system ASP's usage is greater than or equal to 95 percent.","You need to investigate why the system ASP is nearing its capacity.Consider adding storage to the ASP, archiving and removing objects that are no longer needed,or look for objects that are suspiciously large and determineif an application is writing to them in error."}

situation_name: OS400_System_Value_Changed
description: Monitors for a change to system values.
actions: {"This Alert indicates that a change to a system value was logged in the audit journal. You should investigate if this change was appropriate and intended."}

situation_name: OS400_Temp_Addresses_Warning
description: Monitors for temporary addresses being used up.
actions: {"This warning indicates that 95 percent or more of the addresses usedfor temporary objects have been allocated. You need to IPL to recoverthe addresses."}

situation_name: OS_CMD_CF_Systems_Perform_Crit
description: Sysplex Automation for CF Systems Performance Critical
actions: {"The coupling facility is experiencing a very high activity rate or has failed.Use the details view to determine which problem is occurring.If the status is failed, switch to the secondary coupling facility and restart and rebuild the failed one.In the case of high request rate or CPU usage, bring the situation to the attention of a system programmer.Reconfiguration or load balancing may be necessary."}

situation_name: OS_CMD_DASD_Device_ContIdx_Warn
description: DASD contention on a device exceeds the threshold of 0.500
actions: {"Give this information to a system programmer or DASD specialist.","If the device is on a cached storage subsystem with RAID, this may not be much of a problem.","If that is the case, the threshold should be adjusted to an appropriate value for the subsystem."}

situation_name: QI_Automation_Start_Component
description: This situation is triggered when one or more IBM Integration Bus components have been stopped.
actions: {"The stopped components are started by the action associated with this situation. The situation event is reset when the components are started. If the components fail to be started, go to the Product Events workspace to check if there are agent issues that inhibit the action.Also, look in your system log for BIP messages that describe any problems with broker startup."}

situation_name: QI_Average_Flow_Time_High
description: The current average flow time value for a message flow has exceeded its threshold. The default \"Current Average Flow Time\" threshold value in the situation formula is a suggested value. The threshold value can be customized to suit your own environment.
actions: {"To determine flow areas with bottlenecks, deploy CandleMonitor nodes of types subFlowIn and subFlowOut around nodes in the flow and view data in the Sub-Flow Statistics workspace."}

situation_name: QI_Broker_Not_Started
description: A broker is not started.
actions: {"A broker is not started. Start the broker, and this situation event will be reset. You can use the Take Action command QI Start Broker to start the broker.If it fails, go to the Product Events workspace to check if there are agent issues that inhibit the action.Also, look in your system log for BIP messages that describe any problems with broker startup."}

situation_name: QI_Broker_QMgr_Not_Connected
description: The monitoring agent cannot connect to a queue manager associated with a monitored broker.
actions: {"View the Product Events workspace to determine the reason for the queue manager connection failure."}

situation_name: QI_Exception_Terminal_Invoked
description: Messages have gone down a failure path in a message flow.
actions: {"Go to the Archive Node Accounting workspace to identify the problematic message node."}

situation_name: QI_Message_Flow_Events
description: A message flow event has occurred in a monitored message flow.
actions: {"These events are configured by the user with the CandleMonitor node; determine from the attributes available what exact event caused this alert. The Message Flow Events workspace also contains the most recent of these events."}

situation_name: QI_MsgFlow_Elapsed_Time_High
description: The time that a message takes to go through the message flow in an archive statistics interval has exceeded the threshold(the default is 100 milliseconds), which indicates a problem in the message flow.
actions: {"Go to the Archive Node Accounting workspace to identify the performance bottlenecks."}

situation_name: QI_Product_Events
description: A product event has occurred in the monitoring agent to indicate a problem with collecting or reporting data.
actions: {"Go to the Product Events workspace that contains the most recent events to determine from the attributes what exact event caused this alert, then go to the relevant Node workspace to check the Node status, queue manager connection status, deployed Integration Servers, Applications, Message flows and so on."}

situation_name: QI_Publication_Expiry_Event
description: A broker event has been published by the broker to indicate that a retained publication has expired.
actions: {"Determine from the attributes the topic for which a publication expired. The Retained Publications workspace contains all active retained publications."}

situation_name: QI_Status_Stop_Event
description: A broker event has been published by the broker to indicate that one or more message flows (or the broker itself) have stopped.
actions: {"Determine the stopped entity from the attributes. The Message Flow Information workspace indicates which flows are active."}

situation_name: QI_Subscription_Expiry_Event
description: A broker event has been published by the broker to indicate that a subscription has expired.
actions: {"Determine from the attributes the topic for which the subscription expired. The Subscriptions workspace contains all active subscriptions."}

situation_name: Quiesced_UNIX_File_System
description: The indicated File System is in a Quiesced state
actions: {"This condition may or may not be a matter of immediate concern.","For example, this could be due to an HSM Backup Recovery in progress.","If this condition persists, a system programmer should be notified."}

situation_name: Shortage_of_UNIX_Processes_Crit
description: The number of possible Processes has reached its Critical threshold
actions: {"If the maximum is reached, no more Processes can be started.","If this condition is due to expected growth, increase the maximum value.","Otherwise a system programmer should be notified."}

situation_name: Shortage_of_UNIX_Processes_Warn
description: The number of possible Processes has reached its Warning threshold
actions: {"If the maximum is reached, no more Processes can be started.","If this condition is due to expected growth, increase the maximum value.","Otherwise a system programmer should be notified."}

situation_name: Sysplex_DASDSys_VaryStatus_Warn
description: A DASD volume is in a 'Boxed' or 'Not Ready' status and is not available
actions: {"If needed data sets are on the device and no backup devices are available, a system or subsystem failure may occur.","If you cannot use the VARY command to return the device to online status, there may be a hardware malfunction and a Severity 1 or 2 hardware incident should be opened with the hardware vendor."}

situation_name: Sysplex_DASD_Dev_ContIndx_Warn
description: DASD contention on a device exceeds the threshold of 0.500
actions: {"Give this information to a system programmer or DASD specialist.","If the device is on a cached storage subsystem with RAID, this may not be much of a problem.","If that is the case, the threshold should be adjusted to an appropriate value for the subsystem."}

situation_name: Sysplex_GlobalEnq_Wait_Crit
description: ENQueue delay is high and has remained so for over a minute
actions: {"Check the details to determine who is holding the ENQ.","If it is a batch job that can be cancelled and requeued, the deadlock can be broken by doing so.","If it is a started task or on-line user, a system programmer should be called."}

situation_name: Sysplex_GlobalEnq_Wait_Warn
description: ENQueue delay is high
actions: {"Check the details to determine who is holding the ENQ.","If it is a batch job that can be cancelled and requeued, the deadlock can be broken by doing so.","If it is a started task or on-line user, a system programmer should be called."}

situation_name: Sysplex_Workloads_PerfIdx_Crit
description: A service class is failing to meet its goal
actions: {"If this situation persists, the person responsible for the Workload Manager service definition should determine if the missed goal needs to be changed.","Bottleneck analysis of the service class should provide useful information."}

situation_name: Sysplex_Workloads_PerfIdx_Warn
description: A service class is failing to meet its goal
actions: {"If this situation persists, the person responsible for the Workload Manager service definition should determine if the missed goal needs to be changed.","Bottleneck analysis of the service class should provide useful information."}

situation_name: Sysplex_XCFGroups_Warn
description: There is a problem in XCF
actions: {"A system programmer should be contacted to research and correct the problem."}

situation_name: Sysplex_XCFSystems_Status_Crit
description: XCF is missing
actions: {"Cross-system communication within the sysplex is disabled.","A system programmer should be contacted to determine why XCF is down and to restore it as soon as possible."}

situation_name: Sysplex_XCFSystems_Status_Warn
description: The XCF system status indicates that XCF is being shut down
actions: {"A sysplex communication failure can be expected imminently.","System programmer help is required to determine why the shutdown is occurring and to restart the facility as soon as possible."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Avg_ReqInWaitQ_MS_Info
description: The time a disk transfer request is in the wait queue is high.
actions: {"If the average time a disk transfer request spends in the wait queue is higher than normal, disks might not be optimally configured. Run disk diagnostic tools to help tune for optimal disk performance."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Avg_Transfer_MS_Info
description: The average time it takes to complete a disk read or write is high.
actions: {"If the average service transfer time is higher than normal, try defragmenting the disks to reduce disk head access time."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Bad_Pkts_Recvd_Info
description: The rate that bad packets are received is higher than normal.
actions: {"The rate per second that bad packets were received by the communications device driver is higher than normal. Monitor the network for errors and try re-routing connections."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_CPU_CtxSwitch_Hi_Info
description: The number of Process Context Switches is higher than expected.
actions: {"If the process context switching is high, overall system performance degrades because there is CPU overhead associated with each Context Switch between processes. Increasing the process time slice might help this problem."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Device_Stopped_Warning
description: Triggers when the status of a device is not normal.
actions: {"Operator must check that the flagged device is operational.This might entail checking physical connections and running hardware diagnostics."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Dsk_AvgRTrnsMS_Info
description: The average time it takes to complete a disk read is high.
actions: {"If the average read transfer time is higher than normal, try defragmenting the disks to reduce disk head access time."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Dsk_AvgWTrnsMS_Info
description: The average time it takes to complete a disk write is high.
actions: {"If the average write transfer time is higher than normal, disks might not be optimally configured. Run disk diagnostic tools to help tune for optimal disk performance."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Dsk_FailReadSec_Info
description: The number of failed disk read requests per second is high.
actions: {"If the number of failed reads per second is higher than normal, run disk diagnostics."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Dsk_FailWSec_Info
description: The number of failed disk write requests per second is high.
actions: {"If the number of failed disk write requests per second is higher than normal, disks might not be optimally configured. Run disk diagnostic tools to help tune for optimal disk performance."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Dsk_RTimSec_Info
description: The number of disk read timeouts per second is high.
actions: {"If the number of read timeouts per second is higher than normal, try defragmenting the disks to reduce disk head access time. If the condition persists, run disk diagnostic tests."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Dsk_WTimSec_Info
description: The number of disk write timeouts per second is high.
actions: {"If disk write timeouts per second is higher than normal, disks might not be optimally configured. Run disk diagnostic tools to help tune for optimal disk performance."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Memory_RePg_Hi_Info
description: The Physical Memory Repaging rate is high.
actions: {"If the Physical Memory Repaging Rate is high, memory is being overcommitted. Try allocating more memory to the LPAR or adding more physical memory to the CEC."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_NetBandwidth_High_Info
description: Bandwidth utilization for the interface is higher than expected.
actions: {"The network interface is approaching its throughput maximum capacity.If this trend continues, replace the interface with a higher capacity interface, or distribute the network load to other devices."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Pkts_Recv_Err_Info
description: The packets received error rate is higher than normal.
actions: {"The rate per second that input errors were encountered on this communication device is higher than normal. Check the network adapter or the switching and routing devices."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Pkts_Sent_Err_Info
description: The packets sent error rate is higher than normal.
actions: {"If the rate of packets sent errors is higher than normal, check the tuning parameters of the network adapter."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Proc_TxtSz_Info
description: The process text size is larger than expected.
actions: {"If the text size for a process is a high percentage of the available memory and other processes are contending for memory, paging is likely to occur. Allocating more memory to the LPAR or adding more memory might help if excessive paging occurs."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Process_ResDat_Hi_Info
description: The process resident data size is larger than expected.
actions: {"If resident data size is very large for a process, and there is a high percentage of the available memory, more paging is likely to occur. Adding more memory might help if excessive paging occurs."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Process_ResTxt_Hi_Info
description: The process resident text size is larger than expected.
actions: {"If resident text size for a process is a high percentage of the available memory and other processes are contending for memory, paging is likely to occur. Allocating more memory to the LPAR or adding more memory might help if excessive paging occurs."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_Qoverflow_Info
description: The transmit queue overflow rate is higher than normal.
actions: {"The number of outgoing packets that have overflowed the communication software transmit queue is higher than normal. Try increasing the hardware or software queue limits for the communications device driver."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_ServQ_Full_PerSec_Info
description: The rate at which the disk service queue becomes full is high.
actions: {"If the number of times the disk service queue is full is higher than normal, disks might not be optimally configured. Run disk diagnostic tools to help tune for optimal disk performance."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_System_HypPct_Hi_Info
description: The percent of time spent in the hypervisor is high.
actions: {"The time spent in the CEC hypervisor is high and might negatively affect the overall performance of the CEC and all of the CEC LPARs. There might be a problem in the system software."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_System_NProcs_Hi_Info
description: The total number of processes is higher than expected.
actions: {"If the total number of processes is high, there is likely to be more context switching and contention for system resources. If performance is degraded, try rebalancing the processes over more computers."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_TCP_ConnEst_High_Info
description: The number of TCP connections established is high.
actions: {"If there are a large number of established connections, system performance might degrade because of the overhead of servicing those connections. Closing idle or infrequently used connections might help. Redistributing connections over more systems helps."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_User_Acct_Locked_Info
description: The user account is locked.
actions: {"If the user's account is Locked, it is likely to be because of too many failed login retries or administrator security action."}

situation_name: UNIX_AIX_User_Login_Retry_Info
description: The user login retries is high.
actions: {"If the number of user login retries is high, it might be an unauthorized user or a memory challenged user. The system administrator must check for security breeches."}

situation_name: UNIX_AMS_Alert_Critical
description: Agent Management Services Alert.
actions: {"Agent Management Services has issued an alert for a managed agent it cannot restart.Check the alert message for details."}

situation_name: UNIX_Active_Virtual_Memory
description: Checks if the Active Virtual Memory approaches a preset limit.
actions: {"You are running out of virtual memory. If your load average is less than 2 per processor, consider adding additional virtual memory."}

situation_name: UNIX_Agent_Processes_Failure
description: A subprocess of the ITM UNIX OS Agent is not running properly. Data collection may be affected.
actions: {"If a child process of the ITM OS Agent for UNIX is in the \"Failed\" status, the corresponding metrics are not being collected. It is recommended to check if any other failure indication is reported for the system. Then recycle the agent."}

situation_name: UNIX_CMD_Disk_Inodes_Critical
description: The number of free inodes in the /tmp and /var directories is low.
actions: {"Inodes in the /tmp or /var directories is low. Remove unwanted files and consider reorganising the filesystem."}

situation_name: UNIX_CMD_Disk_Space_Warning
description: Check if any filemount's percent space used is greater than 90%.
actions: {"A filesystem is getting full. Remove unwanted files and consider reorganising your filespace."}

situation_name: UNIX_CMD_Runaway_Process
description: Reports High CPU processes.
actions: {"A process might be looping. Determine its userid and contact the user. The process might need to be terminated."}

situation_name: UNIX_CPU_Busy_Critical
description: Monitors if the CPU workload is high (> 90%).
actions: {"CPU workload is high. Try reducing the workload."}

situation_name: UNIX_CPU_Busy_Warning
description: Monitors if the CPU workload is greater than 70% and less than 90%.
actions: {"CPU workload is high. Consider reducing the workload."}

situation_name: UNIX_CPU_Critical
description: The process CPU utilization is greater than or equal to 85%.
actions: {"A process is highly CPU bound. Monitor the process closely, it may be looping."}

situation_name: UNIX_CPU_Warning
description: The process CPU utilization is greather than or equal to 70% and less than 85%.
actions: {"A process is strongly CPU bound.Monitor it closely, it might be looping."}

situation_name: UNIX_Device_Stopped_Warning
description: Triggers when the status of a device is not normal.
actions: {"Operator must check that the flagged device is operational.This might entail checking physical connections and running hardware diagnostics."}

situation_name: UNIX_Disk_Availability
description: Determines under utilized disk space.
actions: {"The /usr filesystem is used less than 25%.Consider reallocating this space elsewhere."}

situation_name: UNIX_ENQ_Contention_Critical
description: ENQueue Contention time has reached its Critical threshold
actions: {"Check the details to determine who is holding the ENQueue.","If it is a batch job that can be cancelled and requeued, the deadlock can be broken by doing so.","If it is a started task, UNIX Process, or on-line user, a system programmer should be notified."}

situation_name: UNIX_ENQ_Contention_Warning
description: ENQueue Contention time has reached its Warning threshold
actions: {"Check the details to determine who is holding the ENQueue.","If it is a batch job that can be cancelled and requeued, the deadlock can be broken by doing so.","If it is a started task, UNIX Process, or on-line user, a system programmer should be notified."}

situation_name: UNIX_File_System_FreeSpace_Crit
description: Detect when any file system has less than 10% free space
actions: {"Free Space in the indicated File System has reached its Critical threshold.The File System space should be extended.This can be accomplished with UNIX System Services commands.If this condition becomes chronic, a system programmer should be notified."}

situation_name: UNIX_File_System_FreeSpace_Warn
description: Detect when any file system has less than 20% free space
actions: {"Free Space in the indicated File System has reached its Warning threshold.Consider extending the File System space.This can be accomplished with UNIX System Services commands.If this condition becomes chronic, a system programmer should be notified."}

situation_name: UNIX_HD_Config_Critical
description: Hard drive space OR Inodes free going critically low.
actions: {"This is an overused disk. Consider moving some files to another volume, or deleting them."}

situation_name: UNIX_HD_Excessive_IO_Wait
description: Notes typical I/O bound processor (NFS).
actions: {"This system is constrained by waiting on I/O. Remove some I/O bound tasks."}

situation_name: UNIX_LAA_Bad_su_to_root_Warning
description: An attempt to switch to the root user failed.
actions: {"Investigate the source of the su command to determine if an attack was attempted."}

situation_name: UNIX_LAA_Log_Size_Warning
description: A log file has grown larger than 10 MB.
actions: {"Reduce the size of the log file.Archive the old log entries, if desired."}

situation_name: UNIX_LAA_Log_Size_Warning_2
description: A log file has grown larger than 10 MB.
actions: {"Reduce the size of the log file.Archive the old log entries, if desired."}

situation_name: UNIX_LPARBusy_pct_Warning
description: The LPAR logical busy percentage is high.
actions: {"If the LPAR logical busy percentage is high, performance might be degraded. Run performance diagnostic tools to determine which applications are the primary cause. Offloading work to other LPARs can improve performance."}

situation_name: UNIX_LPARPhanIntrs_Info
description: The number of LPAR phantom interrupts is high.
actions: {"If there are a large number of phantom interrupts, other LPARS might have lost their interrupts. Report to the system administrator, who might try converting shared LPARs to dedicated LPARs that can reduce phantom interrupts."}

situation_name: UNIX_LPARPhyBusy_pct_Warning
description: The LPAR physical busy percentage is high.
actions: {"If the LPAR physical busy percentage is high, performance might be degraded. Try loading work to other CECs if available. If none are available, try adding more processing units."}

situation_name: UNIX_LPAR_MaxCPUCapUsed_Info
description: Triggers when Max_CPU_Cap_Used Pct GT 80%.
actions: {"When an LPAR is consistently using more than 80% of the LPAR maximum CPU capacity, the administrator must consider increasing the maximum capacity."}

situation_name: UNIX_LPAR_Moved_Info
description: Triggers when last and current LPAR Machine ID are not equal.
actions: {"This is an indicator that an LPAR has been migrated."}

situation_name: UNIX_LPAR_Phyp_Used_High_Info
description: The PHYP (hypervisor) is using more CPU than expected.
actions: {"If the time spent in the hypervisor is large, there are fewer CPU cycles available for LPARs. Run additional performance tools to identify the cause of this condition."}

situation_name: UNIX_LPARentused_Info
description: The LPAR CPU utilization is more than its entitlement.
actions: {"If an LPAR is using more than 100 percent of its entitlement, it is getting extra allocations from the CPU free pool. If this is a chronic condition, consider increasing the entitlement for the LPAR."}

situation_name: UNIX_LPARfreepool_Warning
description: The LPAR CPU free pool space is getting low.
actions: {"If there is little unallocated capacity in the CPU free pool, quality of service might decline under increasing CPU loads. Try adding more processor units or offload work onto other CECs."}

situation_name: UNIX_LPARvcs_Info
description: The LPAR virtual context switching rate is high.
actions: {"If the LPAR virtual context switching rate is high, performance might be degraded. Run performance diagnostic tools to determine which applications are the primary cause. Offloading applications to other LPARs might help."}

situation_name: UNIX_Logged_On_User_Idle
description: The indicated Logged-On user has been idle for a length of time that exceeds the current threshold
actions: {"This condition may or may not be a matter of immediate concern.","Consult installation procedures for appropriate action."}

situation_name: UNIX_Max_Sockets_Critical
description: UNIX Sockets in use Critical
actions: {"The number of UNIX Sockets in use has reached its Critical threshold. If the maximum is reached, UNIX System Services functionality will be impacted. System programmer help is needed immediately. Consider increasing the value of NETWORK DOMAINNAME(AF_UNIX)- MAXSOCKETS(). Use the SETOMVS RESET command to dynamically change the MAXSOCKETS value or to make a permanent change, edit the BPXPRMxx member in SYS1.PARMLIB."}

situation_name: UNIX_Max_Sockets_Warning
description: UNIX Sockets in use Warning
actions: {"The number of UNIX Sockets in use has reached its Warning threshold. If the maximum is reached, UNIX System Services functionality will be impacted. Consider increasing the value of NETWORK DOMAINNAME(AF_UNIX)- MAXSOCKETS(). Use the SETOMVS RESET command to dynamically change the MAXSOCKETS value or to make a permanent change, edit the BPXPRMxx member in SYS1.PARMLIB."}

situation_name: UNIX_Memory_PgFault_Hi_Info
description: The VMM page fault rate is higher than expected.
actions: {"If the Virtual Memory Manager Page fault rate is persistently high, the system memory might be constrained. Allocating more memory to the LPAR or adding more physical memory might improve performance."}

situation_name: UNIX_NFS_RPC_Rejects
description: Monitors rejected NFS/RPC calls.
actions: {"NFS calls are being rejected. Monitor occasions when this situation fires. If it is more likely at certain times of the day, your network or your NFS server might be overloaded then. If it occurs randomly, you might have noise on the network caused by a bad connection or failing hardware."}

situation_name: UNIX_Network_Collsns_Critical
description: Notes large number of packet collisions on a network interface.
actions: {"Network collisions have been detected at this interface. Monitor this closely, you might have too much traffic on this portion of the network at certain times of the day."}

situation_name: UNIX_Network_Collsns_Warning
description: Notes small number of network interface collisions.
actions: {"Network collisions have been detected at this interface. Monitor this closely, you might have too much traffic on this portion of the network at certain times of the day."}

situation_name: UNIX_Network_Errors
description: The number of received or transmitted errors has exceeded limit.
actions: {"Network errors detected. Check for noise on the network or overworked intermediate gateway machines dropping datagrams."}

situation_name: UNIX_Process_MISSING_inted
description: Tests if the Internet Services Daemon, inetd, is up running.
actions: {"The Internet Services Daemon is not running. Re-start the inetd daemon."}

situation_name: UNIX_System_Busy_Critical
description: Checks for the critical states of I/O Wait, Low Free Mem, and CPU Idle.
actions: {"This system is very busy. Reduce the workload."}

situation_name: UNIX_System_Busy_Warning
description: Checks the System CPU, Idle, I/O Wait, and Load Averages for the Busy state.
actions: {"This system is busy. If CPU usages and load averages continue to increase, reduce the workload."}

situation_name: UNIX_System_Capacity_Critical
description: Monitors system capacity withthe process number and the CPU Utilization.
actions: {"The CPU usage and the number of system processes are high. Consider restricting the number of allowed processes."}

situation_name: UNIX_System_RunqAvg_Hi_Info
description: The process run queue is higher than expected.
actions: {"If the process run queue average is high there are many process threads waiting to run. This usually indicates a performance bottleneck or an excessive load on the current CPU resources. Rebalancing the CPU load might help."}

situation_name: UNIX_Virtual_Memory_Warning
description: Monitors if the virtual memoryavailability is running low.
actions: {"The system is running out of virtual memory.Consider moving some workload to other servers or look for the program that is causing a memory leak.To determine the amount of memory required for the workload, look at the process report.To determine whether any program is causing the memory leak, use short term history to see if any process memory requirement grows and does not shrink as time goes on.If your load average is less than 2 per processor, consider adding additional virtual memory."}

situation_name: UNIX_WPAR_Admin_Op_Info
description: The WPAR is running a system administation task.
actions: {"The WPAR is undergoing an administrative operation. Check the detailed workspace views to learn more about the operation being performed."}

situation_name: UNIX_WPAR_Broken_Warning
description: A WPAR has entered broken state.
actions: {"A failure has occurred within the WPAR and it is now in a broken state. Check the logs or the processes inside the WPAR to identify the cause."}

situation_name: UNIX_WPAR_CPU_Usage_Warning
description: The WPAR CPU utilization is high.
actions: {"The CPU usage of the WPAR is close to the specified hard limit. The system administrator can tune the workloads and the CPU hard limit for a better balance."}

situation_name: UNIX_WPAR_Mem_Usage_Warning
description: The WPAR Memory utilization is high.
actions: {"The memory resources used by the WPAR is close to the specified hard limit. The system administrator might want to tune the memory hard limit or add additional memory for better overall performance."}

situation_name: UNIX_WPAR_Min_CPU_Limit_Info
description: The WPAR CPU minimum resource control is not set.
actions: {"A minimum CPU limit value must be specified. Setting a minimum value insures that the WPAR receives CPU resource when there is CPU resource contention."}

situation_name: UNIX_WPAR_Min_Mem_Limit_Info
description: The WPAR memory limit minimum resource control is set to zero.
actions: {"If the minimum memory for a WPAR is set to zero, more of its memory can get paged out during periods of memory resource contention. This can result in lower performance. A minimum memory limit based on the requirement of the WPAR must always be set."}

situation_name: UNIX_WPAR_RC_Inactive_Info
description: Resource controls are not active for this WPAR.
actions: {"Resource controls are not active for this WPAR. Activate the resource controls to allow WLM to effectively manage the available resources."}

situation_name: UNIX_WPAR_Unlim_CPU_Shares_Info
description: The WPAR CPU resource controls are set to unlimited.
actions: {"Setting unlimited CPU shares can result in excessive usage of CPU by a WPAR. Setting the desired CPU shares and limits for each WPAR might improve overall system performance."}

situation_name: UNIX_WPAR_Unlim_Mem_Shares_Info
description: The WPAR Memory Share Resource Controls are set to unlimited.
actions: {"Setting unlimited memory shares can result in excessive usage of memory by a WPAR. Setting the desired memory shares and limits for each WPAR might improve the overall system performance."}

situation_name: Unwanted_UNIX_inetd_Process
description: The inetd daemon is active
actions: {"The inetd daemon provides UNIX networking services.","Consult installation procedures for appropriate action.","If the inetd daemon should be active, then stop this situation."}

situation_name: WMB_App_Not_Started
description: An Application is not started.
actions: {"An Application has not been started. Start the Application, and this situation event will be reset. You can use the Take Action command WMB Start Message Flow(s) (setting only Execution Group and Application parameters) to start the Application.If it fails, go to the Product Events workspace to check if there are agent issues that inhibit the action.Also, look in your system log for BIP messages that describe any problems with Application startup."}

situation_name: WMB_Average_Flow_Time_High
description: The current average flow time value for a message flow has exceeded its threshold. The default \"Current Average Flow Time\" threshold value in the situation formula is a suggested value. The threshold value can be customized to suit your own environment.
actions: {"To determine flow areas with bottlenecks, deploy CandleMonitor nodes of the subFlowIn and subFlowOut types around nodes in the flow and view data in the Monitor Node Sub-Flow Statistics workspace."}

situation_name: WMB_Broker_Not_Started
description: A broker is not started.
actions: {"A broker is not started. Start the broker, and this situation event will be reset. You can use the Take Action command WMB Start Broker to start the broker.If it fails, go to the Product Events workspace to check if there are agent issues that inhibit the action.Also, look in your system log for BIP messages that describe any problems with broker startup."}

situation_name: WMB_Broker_QMgr_Not_Connected
description: The monitoring agent cannot connect to a queue manager associated with a monitored broker.
actions: {"View the Product Events workspace to determine the reason for the queue manager connection failure."}

situation_name: WMB_Exception_Terminal_Invoked
description: Messages have gone down a failure path in a message flow.
actions: {"Go to the Archive Accounting Node Statistics workspace to identify the problematic message node."}

situation_name: WMB_IntServer_Not_Started
description: An Integration Server is not started.
actions: {"An Integration Server has not been started. Start the Integration Server, and this situation event will be reset. For IBM Integration Bus you can use the Take Action command WMB Start Message Flow(s) (setting only Execution Group parameter) to start the Integration Server.If it fails, go to the Product Events workspace to check if there are agent issues that inhibit the action.Also, look in your system log for BIP messages that describe any problems with broker startup."}

situation_name: WMB_Monitor_Node_Events
description: A message flow event has occurred in a monitored message flow.
actions: {"These events are configured by the user with the CandleMonitor node. Determine from the attributes available what exact event has caused this alert. The Monitor Nodes Events workspace also contains the most recent ones of these events."}

situation_name: WMB_MsgFlow_Elapsed_Time_High
description: The time that a message takes to go through the message flow in an archive statistics interval has exceeded the threshold (the default is 100 microseconds), which indicates a problem in the message flow.
actions: {"Go to the Archive Accounting Node Statistics workspace to identify the performance bottlenecks."}

situation_name: WMB_MsgFlow_Not_Started
description: A Message Flow is not started.
actions: {"A Message Flow has not been started. Start the Message Flow, and this situation event will be reset. You can use the Take Action command WMB Start Message Flow(s) to start the Message Flow.If it fails, go to the Product Events workspace to check if there are agent issues that inhibit the action.Also, look in your system log for BIP messages that describe any problems with Message Flow startup."}

situation_name: WMB_Node_Not_Started
description: A Node is not started.
actions: {"A Node has not been started. Start the Node, and this situation event will be reset. For IBM Integration Bus you can use the Take Action command WMB Start Broker to start the Node.If it fails, go to the Product Events workspace to check if there are agent issues that inhibit the action.Also, look in your system log for BIP messages that describe any problems with broker startup."}

situation_name: WMB_Node_QMgr_Not_Connected
description: The monitoring agent cannot connect to a queue manager associated with a monitored Node.
actions: {"View the Product Events workspace to determine the reason for the queue manager connection failure."}
